> पद्याभिः । अशुं । वचसा । च । वाजिनं । त्वां । हिनोमि । पुरुहूत । विश्वहा ॥ ३ ॥

> *aheḷatā | manasā | śruṣṭiṃ | ā | vaha | duhānāṃ | dhenuṃ | pipyuṣīṃ | asaścataṃ ‖*
> *padyābhiḥ | aśuṃ | vacasā | ca | vājinaṃ | tvāṃ | hinomi | puruhūta | viśvahā ‖ 3 ‖*

### Printed p. 183

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 183.*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इंद्र त्वष्टर्वा अहेळता अक्रुध्यता मनसा श्रुष्टिं सुखकरीं दुहानां
> दोग्निं पिप्युषीं प्रवृद्धां पीनां ॥ प्याया वृद्धौ । लिटः क्वसुः । लिड्यजोश्चेति
> पीभावः । उगितश्चेति जीप् । संप्रसारणमिति संप्रसारणं । शासिवसिघसीनां चेति
> षत्वं ॥ असश्चतमसक्तावयनां एवंभूतां धेनुं गामावह। अभिमुख्येन प्रापय।
> अपि च हे पुरुहूत बहुभिराहूतेंद्र त्वष्टर्वा पद्याभिः पादगतिभिराशुं व्यापन-
> शीलं वचसा वाचा च वाजिनं वेगवंतं त्वां विश्वहा सर्वेष्वहःसु हिनोमि ।
> स्तुतिभिः प्रेरयामि ॥ हि गतौ वृद्धौ च ॥

*Gist:* O Indra (or Tvaṣṭṛ), bring us the well-nourished, milk-yielding cow; I urge you, swift in your steps and in your words, with praises on all days.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(O Indra) अहेळता (*aheḷatā*)—without anger. मनसा (*manasā*)—with the mind. श्रुष्टिं (*śruṣṭiṃ*)—that gives happiness. दुहानां (*duhānāṃ*)—that is to be milked. पिप्युषीं (*pipyuṣīṃ*)—well-fed. असश्चतं (*asaścataṃ*)—having limbs well fitted together. धेनुं (*dhenuṃ*)—the milch cow. आ वह (*ā vaha*)—bring and join to us, towards us. पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—O Indra, who are called by many. पद्याभिः (*padyābhiḥ*)—by the movements of the feet. आशुं (*āśuṃ*)—who pervade everything. वचसा (*vacasā*)—by speech. वाजिनं च (*vājinaṃ ca*)—and swift. त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you. विश्वहा (*viśvahā*)—on all days. हिनोमि (*hinomi*)—I urge with praises.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, with a mind free from anger, bring and join to us, towards us, the cow that gives happiness, that is to be milked, that is well-fed and has limbs well fitted together. O Indra, who are called by many, you who pervade everything by the movements of your feet and are swift by speech, I urge on all days with praises.

**Printed English translation**

Bring to us, with benignant mind, the well-nourished and compactly-limbed milch cow, yielding milk, and conferring happiness : daily I glorify, you, who are adored by many, quick (your) steps, and rapid in (your) words.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Let Indra, or the god Tvaṣṭṛ, with a mind free from anger, that is अहेळता मनसा (*aheḷatā manasā*)—अक्रुध्यता मनसा (*akrudhyatā manasā*), that is, a mind filled with joy, towards us the sacrificers, grant us for our good a cow (milch cow) that gives happiness, that yields milk

### Printed p. 184

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 32, p. 184.*

abundantly, whose body is well grown, and that is free from bad marks; thus the wish is expressed.
Indra and the god Tvaṣṭṛ are addressed as पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—बहुभिराहूत (*bahubhirāhūta*), called in many sacrifices, with recitation of praises, by many priests and sacrificers. Then, पद्याभिः आशुं वचसा च वाजिनं त्वा विश्वहा हिनोमि (*padyābhiḥ āśuṃ vacasā ca vājinaṃ tvā viśvahā hinomi*)—the greatness of this god is described: he pervades everything by the movements of his own feet and is swift by his words; and it is said that, addressing this god who is endowed with such greatness, the sacrificer recites praises on all days.
श्रुष्टिं (*śruṣṭiṃ*)—सुखकरीं (*sukhakarīṃ*). The word श्रुष्टी (*śruṣṭī*) is explained by Yāska as श्रुष्टीति क्षिप्रनाम (*śruṣṭīti kṣipranāma*) (Ni. 6-13). Durgācārya, giving the meaning श्रुष्टीवरीः सुखवतीः (*śruṣṭīvarīḥ sukhavatīḥ*), explains that the word is used in several senses.
अहेळता (*aheḷatā*)—अक्रुध्यता (*akrudhyatā*). Yāska (Ni. 3-9) has read हेळतेः (*heḷateḥ*) among the words for the action of being angry. On this basis Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning here as "free from anger".

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> रा॒काम॒हं सु॒हवां॑ सुष्टु॒ती हु॑वे शृ॒णोतु॑ नः सु॒भगा॒ बोध॑तु॒॑
> त्मना॑ ।
> सीव्य॒त्वपः॑ सू॒च्याच्छि॑द्यमानया॒ ददा॑तु वी॒रं श॒तदा॑यमु॒क्त्यं॑ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> राकां अहं । सुहवां । सुस्तुती । हुवे । शृणोतु । नः । सुभगा । बोधतु ।
> त्मना ।
> सीव्यतु । अपः । सूच्या । अच्छैद्यमानया । ददातु । वीरं । शतदायं । उक्तं ॥

> *rākāṃ ahaṃ | suhavāṃ | sustutī | huve | śṛṇotu | naḥ | subhagā | bodhatu |*
> *tmanā |*
> *sīvyatu | apaḥ | sūcyā | acchaidyamānayā | dadātu | vīraṃ | śatadāyaṃ | uktaṃ ‖*

### Printed p. 185

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 185.*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> पत्नीसंयाजेषु गृहपतेः प्राक् राकासिनीवाल्यौ यष्टव्ये । तत्र राकाया-
> गस्य राकामहमित्यादिके याज्यानुवाक्ये । सूत्रितं च । राकामहं सिनीवालि कुहू-
> महमिति द्वे द्वे याज्यानुवाक्ये । आ. १-१० । इति ॥ तथाग्निमारुतेष्टेते धाय्कॆ ।
> सूत्रितं च । राकामहमिति द्वे । आ. ५-२० । इति ॥
> संपूर्णचंद्रा पौर्णमासी राका । तां देवीं सुहवां स्वाह्वानामाह्वान-
> प्रयोजनकारिणीं सुष्टती शोभनया स्तुत्याहं हुवे । आह्वयामि ॥ सुष्टुति-
> शब्दात्तृतीयैकवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगिति पूर्वसवर्ण ईकारः॥ सा च सुभगा शोभन-
> धना नोऽस्माकमाह्वानं शृणोतु । श्रुत्वा च त्मना आत्मना स्वयमेव बोधतु ।
> अस्मदभिप्रायं बुध्यतां । बुद्ध्वा चापः कर्म पुत्रोत्पादनलक्षणं सूच्या सूची-
> स्थानीययाच्छिद्यमानयाविच्छन्नयानुग्रहबुद्ध्या सीव्यतु । संतनोतु । यथा
> वस्त्रादिकं सूच्या सूतं चिरं तिष्ठति एवमिदं करोतु । कृत्वा च वीरं विक्रांतं
> शतदायं बहुधनं बहुप्रदं वोक्ष्यं प्रशस्यं पुत्रं ददातु ॥

*Gist:* Rākā, the full-moon deity, is invoked with praise at the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings; may she hear, understand, and bestow a valiant, wealthy, praiseworthy son.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सुहवां (*suhavāṃ*)—worthy of an excellent invocation. राकां (*rākāṃ*)—the deity called Rākā. सुष्टुती (*suṣṭutī*)—with excellent praise. अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I. हुवे (*huve*)—call. सुभगा (*subhagā*)—that goddess who has excellent wealth. नः (*naḥ*)—our invocation. शृणोतु (*śṛṇotu*)—may she hear! त्मना (*tmanā*)—of her own accord. बोधतु (*bodhatu*)—may she understand our desire. अपः (*apaḥ*)—the work in the form of begetting a son. सूच्या (*sūcyā*)—like a needle. अच्छिद्यमानया (*acchidyamānayā*)—unbroken. With a mind of favour सीव्यतु (*sīvyatu*)—may she weave. वीरं (*vīraṃ*)—a valiant. शतदायं (*śatadāyaṃ*)—wealthy. उक्ष्यं (*ukṣyaṃ*) (as supplied; the Saṃhitā has उक्त्यं (*uktyaṃ*))—praiseworthy son. ददातु (*dadātu*)—may she give.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

I call the deity called "Rākā", who is worthy of an excellent invocation, with excellent praise. May that goddess, who has excellent wealth, hear our invocation. May she understand our desire of her own accord. May she weave the work in the form of begetting a son with a mind of favour that is like a needle and unbroken. May she give a son who is valiant, wealthy and praiseworthy.

**Printed English translation**

I invoke, with suitable praise, Raka, who is worthily invoked : may she, who is auspicious of good fortune, hear us, and spontaneously

### Printed p. 186

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 32, p. 186.*

understand (our purpose): may she sew her work with an infallible needle : may she grant us excellent and opulent descendants.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In the sacrifice called Patnīsaṃyāja, before the offering to the Gṛhapati, offerings are to be made to the deities Rākā and Sinīvālī. Then, in the Rākā sacrifice, the first Ṛk of this sūkta, राकामहं (*rākāmahaṃ*), and the second Ṛk, यास्ते राके (*yāste rāke*), are used as the Yājyā and Puronuvākyā mantras, as expounded by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra राकामहं सिनीवालि कुहू-महमिति द्वे द्वे याज्यानुवाक्ये (*rākāmahaṃ sinīvāli kuhū-mahamiti dve dve yājyānuvākye*) (Ā. 1-10); and in the mantras having the Maruts as deity these Ṛks are to be used as Dhāyyā mantras, as expounded by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra राकामहमिति द्वे (*rākāmahamiti dve*) (Ā. 5-20).
By this Ṛk and the next one the goddess Rākā is praised.
Rākā: the full-moon night. The night that has the full moon is commonly called Pūrṇimā; this is what is called Rākā. सुहवां सुष्टुती अहं हुवे (*suhavāṃ suṣṭutī ahaṃ huve*): it is said that I call her who is well-called, i.e. who brings about the fulfilment of invocations, with excellent praise; as this goddess fulfils the wishes of those who call her, the sacrificer invokes her with excellent praise.
The word सुभगा (*subhagā*) is taken to mean one who has excellent wealth: may this goddess who has excellent wealth hear the sacrificer's invocation, and having heard it, त्मना बोधतु (*tmanā bodhatu*), may she of herself understand the purpose for which the sacrificer has invoked her; and अपः सूच्या अच्छिद्यमानया सीव्यतु (*apaḥ sūcyā acchidyamānayā sīvyatu*), may she so favour us that the sacrificer's line is not broken. वीरं शतदायं उक्थं पुत्रं ददातु (*vīraṃ śatadāyaṃ ukthaṃ putraṃ dadātu*): the wish is expressed that she grant a son who is valiant, possessed of abundant wealth or giving abundantly, and praiseworthy.
अपः सूच्या अच्छिद्यमानया सीव्यतु (*apaḥ sūcyā acchidyamānayā sīvyatu*)—the bhāṣya says: पुत्रोत्पादनलक्षणं कर्म सूचीस्थानीयया अविच्छन्नया अनुग्रहबुद्धा संतनोतु । यथावस्त्रादिकं सूच्यास्यतं चिरं तिष्ठति एवमिदं करोतु (*putrotpādanalakṣaṇaṃ karma sūcīsthānīyayā avicchannayā anugrahabuddhā saṃtanotu | yathāvastrādikaṃ sūcyāsyataṃ ciraṃ tiṣṭhati evamidaṃ karotu*). The word अपः (*apaḥ*) has been read by Yāska among the names of action (Ni. 3-2). Here its meaning is explained as the action consisting of the begetting of sons. The meaning is explained thus: through the favour of the goddess Rākā, as a garment stitched with a needle remains firm for a long time, so may our line, by the birth of sons, remain firm for a long time.

### Printed p. 187

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 187.*

The author of the Nirukta, in explaining the word राका (*rākā*), cites this very Ṛk (Ni. 11-32); gives the derivation राका—रातेर्दान कर्मणः (*rākā—rāterdāna karmaṇaḥ*), and then explains the Ṛk राकामहं सुह्वानां सुष्टुत्या-ह्वये शृणोतुनस्सुभगा बोधत्वात्मना सीव्यत्वपः प्रजननकर्म सूच्याच्छिद्यमानया। सूची सीव्यतेः ददातु वीरं शतप्रदमुक्थं व्यक्तव्यप्रशंसं (*rākāmahaṃ suhvānāṃ suṣṭutyā-hvaye śṛṇotunassubhagā bodhatvātmanā sīvyatvapaḥ prajananakarma sūcyācchidyamānayā| sūcī sīvyateḥ dadātu vīraṃ śatapradamukthaṃ vyaktavyapraśaṃsaṃ*) in the same way as the bhāṣyakāra has explained it.

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यास्ते॑ राके सुम॒तयः॑ सु॒पेश॑सो॒ याभि॒र्ददा॑सि दा॒शुषे॒ वसू॑नि ।
> ताभि॑र्नो अ॒द्य सु॒मना॑ उ॒पाग॑हि सहस्रपो॒षं सु॑भगे॒ ररा॑णा॥ ५ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> याः । ते । राके । सुमतयः । सुपेशसः । याभिः । ददासि । दाशुषे । वसूनि ।
> ताभिः । नः । अद्य । सुमनाः । उपआगहि । सहस्रपोषं । सुभगे । रराणा ॥ ५ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे राके देवि सुपेशसः शोभनरूपास्ते तव याः सुमतयः शोभनबु-
> द्धयः याभिर्मतिभिर्दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय वसूनि धनानि ददासि ।
> प्रयच्छसि । अद्येदानीं ताभिर्मतिभिः सहिता त्वं सुमनाः शोभनमना भूत्वापा-
> गहि । उपागच्छ ॥ गमेश्चांदसः शपो लुक् । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिक-
> लोपः । असिद्धवदत्राभादित्यस्यासिद्धत्वाद्देर्लुगभावः ॥ किं कुर्वती । हे सुभगे
> शोभनधने सहस्रपोषं सहस्रसंख्याकस्य धनस्य पुष्टिं रराणा ददती ॥ रा दाने ।
> व्यत्ययेन शानच् । छांदसः शपः श्लुः । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

*Gist:* O goddess Rākā, with the good intentions with which you give wealth to the offerer, come to us today with good mind, bestowing a thousand-fold increase of wealth. The tail explains the verb forms *upāgahi* and *rarāṇā*.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सुभगे (*subhage*)—one with excellent wealth. राके (*rāke*)—O goddess Rākā. सुपेशसः (*supeśasaḥ*)—of excellent form. ते (*te*)—your. याः सुमतयः (*yāḥ sumatayaḥ*)—which auspicious intentions there are. याभिः (*yābhiḥ*)—by which very benevolent intentions. दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers oblation.

### Printed p. 188

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 32, p. 188.*

वसूनि (*vasūni*)—wealth. ददासि (*dadāsi*)—you give. अद्य (*adya*)—now. नः (*naḥ*)—in our regard. ताभि (*tābhi*)—with those very intentions. सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)—having an auspicious mind. सहस्रपोषं (*sahasrapoṣaṃ*)—increase of wealth numbering a thousand. रराणा (*rarāṇā*)—giving. उपागहि (*upāgahi*)—be gracious (come).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O goddess Rākā, who have excellent wealth, with those auspicious intentions of yours, of excellent form, and with those very kindly intentions by which you give wealth to the sacrificer who offers oblation, now in our regard, with the same intentions, being of auspicious mind and giving an increase of wealth numbering a thousand, be gracious.

**Printed English translation**

Raka, with those your kind and gracious intentions, wherewith you grant riches to the donor (of oblations), approach us to-day; you who are auspicious of good fortune, favourably inclined, and bestowing a thousand blessings.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Addressing this goddess by the words हे राके (*he rāke*), in याभिः दाशुषे यजमानाय वसूनि ददासि, अद्य ताभिः सुमनाः उपागहि—याभिः मतिभिः हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय धनानि प्रयच्छसि ताभिः मतिभिः सहिता त्वं शोभनमना भूत्वा उपागच्छ (*yābhiḥ dāśuṣe yajamānāya vasūni dadāsi, adya tābhiḥ sumanāḥ upāgahi—yābhiḥ matibhiḥ havirdattavate yajamānāya dhanāni prayacchasi tābhiḥ matibhiḥ sahitā tvaṃ śobhanamanā bhūtvā upāgaccha*) the prayer is made that, since this goddess is of a benevolent mind towards those who perform sacrifice addressed to her, she come to our sacrificial hall, accompanied by the kind intention that brings welfare to the sacrificers who offer oblations to her, in order to bestow wealth. And of सुभगे सहस्रपोषं रराणा—शोभनधने सहस्रसंखातस्य धनस्य पुष्टिं ददती (*subhage sahasrapoṣaṃ rarāṇā—śobhanadhane sahasrasaṃkhātasya dhanasya puṣṭiṃ dadatī*): since this goddess has abundant wealth she is addressed by the word सुभगे (*subhage*), and she will bestow on those who serve her the increase (abundance), the prosperity, of wealth numbering thousands; thus the generosity of this goddess is also described.

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> सिनी॑वालि॒ पृथु॑ष्टुके॒ या दे॒वाना॒मसि॒ स्वसा॑ ।
> जु॒षस्व॑ ह॒व्यमाहु॑तं प्र॒जां दे॑वि दिदिड्डि नः ॥ ६ ॥

> *sinīvāli pṛthuṣṭuke yā devānāmasi svasā |*
> *juṣasva havyamāhutaṃ prajāṃ devi didiḍḍi naḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

### Printed p. 189

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, p. 189.*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सिनीवालि । पृथुस्तुके । या । देवानां । असि । स्वसा ।
> जुषस्व । हव्यं । आहुतं । प्रजां । देवि । दिदिड्डि । नः ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> सिनिवाल्या यागे सिनीवालीत्यादिके द्वे याज्यानुवाक्ये । सूत्रं पूर्व-
> मुदाहृतं ॥
> दृष्टचंद्रामावास्या सिनीवाली । हे सिनीवालि पृथुष्टुके पृथुजघने पृथु-
> संहते वा या त्वं देवानां स्वसासि स्वयंसंचारिणी भगिनी वा भवसि सा त्वमाहु-
> तमाभिमुख्येनाग्नौ प्रक्षिप्तं हव्यमस्मदीयं हविर्जुषस्व । सेवस्व । किंच हे देवि
> सिनीवालि नोऽस्माकं प्रजां पुत्रादिकां दिदिड्डि । उपचिनु अतिसर्जय वा । देही-
> त्यर्थः ॥ दिह उपचये । लोट छांदसः शपः श्लुः । दिश अतिसर्जन इत्यस्माद्वा ॥

> *sinivālyā yāge sinīvālītyādike dve yājyānuvākye | sūtraṃ pūrva-*
> *mudāhṛtaṃ ‖*
> *dṛṣṭacaṃdrāmāvāsyā sinīvālī | he sinīvāli pṛthuṣṭuke pṛthujaghane pṛthu-*
> *saṃhate vā yā tvaṃ devānāṃ svasāsi svayaṃsaṃcāriṇī bhaginī vā bhavasi sā tvamāhu-*
> *tamābhimukhyenāgnau prakṣiptaṃ havyamasmadīyaṃ havirjuṣasva | sevasva | kiṃca he devi*
> *sinīvāli no 'smākaṃ prajāṃ putrādikāṃ didiḍḍi | upacinu atisarjaya vā | dehī-*
> *tyarthaḥ ‖ diha upacaye | loṭa chāṃdasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ | diśa atisarjana ityasmādvā ‖*

*Gist:* The Sinīvālī sacrifice uses this and the next Ṛk as yājyā and anuvākyā (the sūtra was cited earlier). Sinīvālī is the new-moon day on which the moon is seen as a thin sliver; O broad-hipped one, sister of the gods, enjoy our oblation and give us offspring. The tail explains *didiḍḍi* (from दिह (*diha*) or दिश (*diśa*)).

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

पृथुष्टुके (*pṛthuṣṭuke*)—having broad hips. सिनीवालि (*sinīvāli*)—O goddess Sinīvālī. या (*yā*)—you who. देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of the gods. स्वसा असि (*svasā asi*)—are the sister; such a you. आहुतं (*āhutaṃ*)—offered (into the fire). हव्यं (*havyaṃ*)—the oblation. जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—partake of. देवि (*devi*)—O goddess. नः (*naḥ*)—to us. प्रजां (*prajāṃ*)—sons and the like. दिदिड्डि (*didiḍḍi*)—give. (The printed text has "ಎಲೆಲ ದೇವಿಯೇ" for "O goddess"; read as an evident slip for "ಎಲೈ", as printed.)

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O goddess Sinīvālī, of broad hips, you who are the sister of the gods, such a you, partake of the oblation we have offered in the fire. O goddess, give us sons and the like.

**Printed English translation**

Wide-hipped Sinivali, who are the sister of the gods, accept the offered oblation, and grant us, goddess, progeny.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

It has been said earlier (Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, as printed "ಆ. ೫-೨೦") that in the Sinīvālī sacrifice this Ṛk beginning सिनीवालि (*sinīvāli*) and the next Ṛk beginning या सुबाहुः (*yā subāhuḥ*) are to be used as the yājyā and the purorucā/anuvākyā mantras.


### Printed p. 190

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 32, p. 190.*

The new-moon day (amāvāsyā) is of two kinds. Of these, the new-moon day on which the moon is seen as a mere sliver is known as Sinīvālī. This very sense is explained by the words "dṛṣṭacandrā amāvāsyā sinīvālī". The deity presiding over this new-moon day is addressed by the word हे सिनीवालि (*he sinīvāli*). She is described as पृथुष्टके (*pṛthuṣṭake*) [sic, as printed]—"pṛthujaghane pṛthusaṃhate vā", having a stout lower belly, or a strong bodily frame; and as देवानां स्वसा आसि (*devānāṃ svasā āsi*)—"svayaṃsaṃcāriṇī bhaginī vā bhavasi", one who moves about at her own will, or the sister of the gods. The Ṛk further wishes that she partake of the oblation offered into the fire ("āhutaṃ haviḥ juṣasva") by the sacrificers in her name; and it prays नः प्रजां दिदिड्डि (*naḥ prajāṃ didiḍḍi*) that this goddess increase or bestow sons and the like upon us sacrificers who offer shares of oblation in the sacrifices.

If on the day of new moon the moon is seen by itself as a mere sliver, that new-moon day is called by the name Sinīvālī; hence the explanation "dṛṣṭacandrā amāvāsyā sīnivālī" is given here. Yāska says: सिनीवाली कुहूरिति देव पत्न्याविति नैरुक्ताः । अमावास्या इति याज्ञिकाः । या पूर्वा अमावास्या सा सीनीवाली, या उत्तरा सा कुहूरिति विज्ञायते (*sinīvālī kuhūriti deva patnyāviti nairuktāḥ | amāvāsyā iti yājñikāḥ | yā pūrvā amāvāsyā sā sīnīvālī, yā uttarā sā kuhūriti vijñāyate*) (words as printed). That is: the Nairuktas hold that the two goddesses named Sīnīvālī and Kuhū are wives of gods; the ritualists hold that the time called amāvāsyā is of two kinds, Sīnīvālī and Kuhū (the earlier new-moon day is Sīnīvālī, the later is known as Kuhū). Having set out the two views, the commentator cites the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa passage that teaches this.

Further: सिनीवाली सिनमन्नं भवति सिनाति भूतानि वालं पर्व वृणोतेः तस्मिन्नन्नवती वालिनी वा, वालेनेवास्यामणुत्वाच्चंद्रमाः सेवितव्यो भवति इति वा (*sinīvālī sinamannaṃ bhavati sināti bhūtāni vālaṃ parva vṛṇoteḥ tasminnannavatī vālinī vā, vālenevāsyāmaṇutvāccaṃdramāḥ sevitavyo bhavati iti vā*) (Nirukta 11-32, as printed). *Sina* means food, which binds (nourishes) living beings and makes them possessed of food; since the gods desire oblations at the parva (junction) time, Sinīvālī is she who is filled with food—one kind of meaning. Secondly, the word *vāla* is used in the sense of *bāla* (a young boy): she is filled with oblations dear to the gods, or is served by the moon, which is minute in form, like a *vāla* (hair). 

Also, citing this very mantra, he explains: सिनीवाली पृथुजघने, स्तुकः स्त्यायतेः संघातः । पृथुकेशस्तुते पृथुष्टुते वा । या त्वं देवानामसि स्वसा । स्वसा सु असा । स्नेषु सीदतीति वा । जुषस्व हव्यमदनं प्रजां च देवि दितुनः (*sinīvālī pṛthujaghane, stukaḥ styāyateḥ saṃghātaḥ | pṛthukeśastute pṛthuṣṭute vā | yā tvaṃ devānāmasi svasā | svasā su asā | sneṣu sīdatīti vā | juṣasva havyamadanaṃ prajāṃ ca devi ditunaḥ*) (Nirukta 11-34, as printed), and gives the meaning thus.


### Printed p. 191

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, p. 191.*

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> या सु॑बा॒हुः स्वं॑गु॒रिः सु॒षूमा॑ बहु॒सूव॑री ।
> तस्यै॑ वि॒श्वत्नै॑ ह॒विः सि॑नीवा॒लै जु॑होतन ॥ ७ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> या । सुबाहुः । सुअंगुरिः । सुसूमा । बहुसूवरी ।
> तस्यै । विश्वत्स्थलि । हविः । सिनीवालैलि । जुहोतन ॥ ७ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> या सिनीवाली सुबाहुः शोभनबाहुः स्वंगुरिः शोभनांगुलिः सुषूमा
> सुष्टु प्रसवित्री ॥ षूज् प्राणिप्रसवे । अन्येभोऽपि दृश्यंत इति मनिन् । कृदुत्तर
> पदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ बहुसूवरी बह्नीनां प्रजानां सवित्री ॥ तेनैव सूत्रेण क्वनिप्स्
> वनो र चेति जीब्रेफौ । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ तस्यॆ सीनीवालै विश्वत्न्यै ।
> विशां पालयित्र्यै ॥ विभाषा सपूर्वस्येति पत्युर्नकारांतादेशः । आयस्मयादित्वेन
> भत्वाद्विसो जश्वाभावः । परादिश्चंदसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ हे
> ऋत्विग्यजमाना हविर्जुहोतन । जुहुत ॥ तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति तनबादेशः ॥

*Gist:* Sinīvālī has beautiful arms and fingers, bears children well and is mother of many, and protects the people; priests and sacrificers, offer the oblation to her. The tail explains *suṣūmā*, *bahusūvarī*, *viśvatnyai* and *juhotana*.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

या (*yā*)—she who. सुबाहुः (*subāhuḥ*)—having excellent arms. स्वंगुरिः (*svaṃguriḥ*)—having excellent fingers. सुषूमा (*suṣūmā*)—having borne excellent sons. बहुसूवरी (*bahusūvarī*)—having many sons. तस्यै (*tasyai*)—to such a one. विश्वत्नै (*viśvatnai*)—the protectress of the people. सिनीवाल्यै (*sinīvālyai*)—to the goddess Sinīvālī. हविः (*haviḥ*)—oblation. जुहोतन (*juhotana*)—offer.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O sacrificers, to that goddess Sinīvālī who has excellent arms, excellent fingers, excellent sons and many sons, offer the oblation.

**Printed English translation**

Offer the oblation to that Sinivali, the protectress of mankind, who has beautiful fingers, who is the parent of many children, and who had numerous childrn [sic].

### Printed p. 192

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 32, p. 192.*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

या सुबाहुः स्वंगुरिः सुषूमा बहुसूवरी (*yā subāhuḥ svaṃguriḥ suṣūmā bahusūvarī*)—सिनीवाली शोभनबाहुः शोभनांगुलिः सुष्टु प्रसवित्रि, बह्नीनां प्रजानां सवित्रि (*sinīvālī śobhanabāhuḥ śobhanāṃguliḥ suṣṭu prasavitri, bahnīnāṃ prajānāṃ savitri*). This goddess called Sinīvālī has beautiful, excellent arms and fingers; she bears good sons and bears many children. Having thus described this goddess and her power, the commentator says तस्यॆ सिनीवाल्कॆ विश्वत्कृ हवि: जुहोतन (*tasyè sinīvālkè viśvatkṛ havi: juhotana*) (words as printed)—विशां पालयित्र्यै हवि: जुहुत (*viśāṃ pālayitryai havi: juhuta*): "Offer oblations to this Sinīvālī goddess, of such power, who protects the people" — the seer of the mantra's exhortation is thus described: priests and sacrificers are to offer oblations to her.

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> या गुं॒गूर्या सि॑नीवा॒ली या रा॒का या सर॑स्वती ।
> इं॒द्रा॒णीम॑ह्व ऊ॒तये॑ वरुणा॒नीं स्व॒स्तये॑ ॥ ९ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> या । गुंगूः । या । सिनीवाली । या । ताका [?] । या । सरस्वती .
> इंद्राणीं । अह्वे ऊतये । वरुणानीं । स्वस्तये ॥ ८ ॥

> *yā | guṃgūḥ | yā | sinīvālī | yā | tākā [?] | yā | sarasvatī .*
> *iṃdrāṇīṃ | ahve ūtaye | varuṇānīṃ | svastaye ‖ 8 ‖*

(In the supplied text the Saṃhitā ends with the Ṛk number "९" and the Pada with "८"; the Pada's third word reads ताका (*tākā*) where the Saṃhitā has राका (*rākā*) [?]; both as supplied.)

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अत्र गुंगूशब्देन राकासिनीवाल्ल्योः साहचर्यात्कुहूरुच्यते । > या
> गुंगूः कुहूस्तामह्वे । आह्वयामि । एवमुत्तरत्रापि योज्यं । इंद्राणीमिंद्रस्य
> पत्निमूतये रक्षणार्थमह्वे : आह्वयामि । तथा वरुणानीं वरुणस्य पत्निं
> स्वस्तयेऽविनाशायाह्वयामि ॥ इंद्रवरुणेत्यादिना जीष् आनुगागमश्च ॥

*Gist:* here the word *guṅgū*, because of its association with Rākā and Sinīvālī, means Kuhū; the Ṛk invokes each of these goddesses, Indrāṇī for protection and Varuṇānī for welfare. The tail notes the feminine suffix *īṣ* and the *ānuk* augment in *indrāṇī*, *varuṇānī*.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

या (*yā*) (*yā*)—who; गुंगूः (*guṃgūḥ*)—the goddess Kuhū; या (*yā*)—who; सिनीवाली (*sinīvālī*)—Sinīvālī; या (*yā*)—who; राका (*rākā*)—Rākā; या (*yā*)—who; सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—Sarasvatī: she who is famed under these names. अह्वे (*ahve*)—I call. इंद्राणीं (*iṃdrāṇīṃ*)—Indra's wife; ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—I call her for protection. वरुणानीं (*varuṇānīṃ*)—Varuṇa's wife; स्वत्तये (*svattaye*) [sic, as printed]—I call her so that welfare may come about.

### Printed p. 193

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, p. 193.*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

I call that goddess who is famed as Kuhū, as Sinīvālī, as Rākā and as Sarasvatī. I call Indrāṇī for protection and Varuṇānī for welfare.

**Printed English translation**

I invoke her who is Gangu, who is Sinivali, who is Raka, who is Saraswati : (I invoke) Indrani for protection, Varunani for welfare.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Here the goddess Kuhū is meant by the word गुंगूः (*guṃgūḥ*). Since Rākā and Sinīvālī were described in the preceding Ṛks, the commentator explains the word *guṅgū* here as Kuhū (that is, the new-moon day on which the moon is not seen). The Nirukta-writer says कूहूर्गूहतेः क्वा भूदिति वा क्व सती हूयत इति वा, क्वाहुतं जुहोतीति वा (*kūhūrgūhateḥ kvā bhūditi vā kva satī hūyata iti vā, kvāhutaṃ juhotīti vā*) (Nir. 11-34), and does not explain the word (*guṅgū*) formed from the root गुहू (*guhū*) (*guhū*), "to cover, to veil". The word *kuhū* itself is derived from the root *gūh*; and in three ways the form of the word *kuhū* is explained: "Where was she? Where is she invoked? Where does one offer the oblation?"—that is, "Where is this goddess? Where is she called? Where is the offering made?" The passage describes that the sacrificers invoke the goddess Kuhū, the goddess Sinīvālī, and the goddesses Rākā, Sarasvatī, Indrāṇī and Varuṇānī, for the sake of स्वस्तये अविनाशाय (*svastaye avināśāya*) (*svastaye avināśāya*), that welfare may come to themselves.

इंद्राणीं (*iṃdrāṇīṃ*)—इंद्रस्य पत्निं (*iṃdrasya patniṃ*). The Nirukta-writer has commented इंद्राणी इंद्रस्य पत्नि (*iṃdrāṇī iṃdrasya patni*) (Nir. 10-39). वरुणानीं (*varuṇānīṃ*)—वरुणस्य पत्निं (*varuṇasya patniṃ*). Yāska, in explaining the Ṛk उत ग्ना व्यंतु देवपत्नीरिंद्राण्य १ ग्नाय्यश्विनी राट् । आ रोदसी वरुणानी शृणोतु व्यंतु देवीर्य ऋतुर्जनीनां (*uta gnā vyaṃtu devapatnīriṃdrāṇya 1 gnāyyaśvinī rāṭ | ā rodasī varuṇānī śṛṇotu vyaṃtu devīrya ṛturjanīnāṃ*) (Ma. Saṃ. 5-46-8, words as printed), says: इंद्राणींद्रस्य पत्नि, अग्नाया अग्नेःपत्नि, अश्विनी अश्वनोः पत्नि, रोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नि, वरुणानी वरुणस्य पत्नि (*iṃdrāṇīṃdrasya patni, agnāyā agneḥpatni, aśvinī aśvanoḥ patni, rodasī rudrasya patni, varuṇānī varuṇasya patni*) (Nir. 12-46): Indrāṇī is Indra's wife, Agnāyī Agni's wife, Aśvinī the Aśvins' wife, Rodasī Rudra's wife, Varuṇānī Varuṇa's wife.

### Printed p. 194

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 4, Sūkta 33, p. 194.*

## Sūkta 33 (Maṇḍala 2)

*The thirty-third sūkta.*

**Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta** (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

> चतुर्थेऽनुवाक एकादश सूक्तानि । तत्र ते पितरिति पंचदशर्चं प्रथमं

*Gist:* the first of the eleven sūktas of Anuvāka 4, of fifteen ṛks, of the Gṛtsamada seer, for Rudra, in *triṣṭubh*; the Anukramaṇī, the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra (4-8-23), the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (3-8) and Śaunaka are quoted for the application.

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** There are eleven sūktas in the fourth anuvāka of the second maṇḍala. Of them this sūkta beginning आ ते पितर्मरुतां (*ā te pitarmarutāṃ*) is the first. It has fifteen ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Gṛtsamada; Rudra is the deity; the metre is *triṣṭubh*. What is said in the Anukramaṇikā—आ ते पंचोना रौद्रमिति (*ā te paṃconā raudramiti*)—is explained: in the Rudra sacrifices beginning with the one named Śūlagava the western-quarter deity is to be worshipped with this sūkta, as set out by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra sūtra कद्रुद्रायेमा रुद्राया ते पितरिमा रुद्राय स्थिरधन्वन इति सर्वरुद्रयज्ञेषु दिशामुपस्थानं (*kadrudrāyemā rudrāyā te pitarimā rudrāya sthiradhanvana iti sarvarudrayajñeṣu diśāmupasthānaṃ*) (Gṛ. Sū. 4-8-23). In the animal sacrifice to Rudra, when the oblation is offered, the Ṛk आ ते पितः (*ā te pitaḥ*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra, as set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra sūtra आ ते पितर्मरुतां सुम्मनेतु प्रबभ्रवे वृषभाय .श्वितीच इति तिस्रः (*ā te pitarmarutāṃ summanetu prababhrave vṛṣabhāya .śvitīca iti tisraḥ*) (Ā. 3-8). And on the application of this sūkta the sage Śaunaka says in the book Ṛgvidhāna: चतुर्दशीमुपोष्यकां कृष्णस्य जुहुयाच्चरुं । आतेसूक्तेन रौद्रेण प्रत्यृचं वाग्यतः शुचिः ॥ पूर्वमाज्याहुतीर्हुत्वाथोपस्थाय च शंकरं । हविःशेषेण वर्तेतैकांतरमतंद्रितः ॥ पूर्णमासे जयेन्मृत्युं रोगैश्च परिमुच्यते ॥ (*caturdaśīmupoṣyakāṃ kṛṣṇasya juhuyāccaruṃ | ātesūktena raudreṇa pratyṛcaṃ vāgyataḥ śuciḥ ‖ pūrvamājyāhutīrhutvāthopasthāya ca śaṃkaraṃ | haviḥśeṣeṇa vartetaikāṃtaramataṃdritaḥ ‖ pūrṇamāse jayenmṛtyuṃ rogaiśca parimucyate ‖*) (Ṛgvidhāna 1-30). That is: on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, fasting, self-controlled and pure, one is to recite each Ṛk of this Rudra sūkta, and having cooked the caru ... [the sentence continues on the next page].

### Printed p. 195

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 16, p. 195.*

[Continuing the Anuvāda from p. 194:] ... and having cooked the caru, one is to offer the oblation with ghee. After the oblation, the deity Rudra is to be approached (*upasthāna*). Then on that day only the remnant of the oblation is to be eaten, in solitude, without harbouring any anxiety; no other food is to be taken. If one observes this from the fourteenth day onwards for a month, one is said to be freed from untimely death and disease and to live happily.

**Sūkta 33** — Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 33; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Vargas 16, 17, 18. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 15. Seer: Gṛtsamada. Deity: Rudra. Metre: *triṣṭubh*.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आ ते॑ पितर्मरुतां सु॒म्ममे॑तु॒ मा नः॒ सूर्य॑स्य सं॒दृशो॑-
> युयोथाः ।
> अ॒भि नो॑ वी॒रो अर्व॑ति क्षमेत॒ प जा॑येमहि रुद्र प्र॒जाभिः॑ ॥ १ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । ते । पितः । मरुतां । सुम्मं । एतु । मानः । नः । सूर्यस्य । संदृशः ।
> युयोथाः ।
> अभि । नः । वीरः । अर्वति । क्षमेत । प्र । जायेमहि । रुद्र । प्रजाभिः ॥ १ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतां पितः मरुत्संज्ञानां देवानामुत्पादक रुद्र ॥ परमपि छंदसीति
> षष्ठ्यंतस्य पूर्वामंत्रितांगवद्भावात्सर्वानुदात्तत्वं ॥ ते त्वदीयमस्मभ्यं दातव्यं
> सुम्मं सुखमैतु । आगच्छतु । रुद्रस्य च मरुतां पितृत्वमिदं पित्रे मरुतामाख्या-
> यिकामुखेनावादिष्ट । ऋग्वे. १-११४-६. । तथा त्वं नोऽस्मान् सूर्यस्य संदृशः
> संदर्शनान्मा युयोथाः । मा पृथक्कार्षिः ॥ यु मिश्रणामिश्रणयोः । लङ्ग
> छांदसः शपः श्लुः । छंदस्युभयथेत्यार्थधातुकत्वेन जित्वाभावाद्गुणः ॥ अर्वति

> *he marutāṃ pitaḥ marutsaṃjñānāṃ devānāmutpādaka rudra ‖ paramapi chaṃdasīti*
> *ṣaṣṭhyaṃtasya pūrvāmaṃtritāṃgavadbhāvātsarvānudāttatvaṃ ‖ te tvadīyamasmabhyaṃ dātavyaṃ*
> *summaṃ sukhamaitu | āgacchatu | rudrasya ca marutāṃ pitṛtvamidaṃ pitre marutāmākhyā-*
> *yikāmukhenāvādiṣṭa | ṛgve. 1-114-6. | tathā tvaṃ no 'smān sūryasya saṃdṛśaḥ*
> *saṃdarśanānmā yuyothāḥ | mā pṛthakkārṣiḥ ‖ yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ | laṅga*
> *chāṃdasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ | chaṃdasyubhayathetyārthadhātukatvena jitvābhāvādguṇaḥ ‖ arvati*

### Printed p. 196

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 3 [sic, as printed; Anuvāka 4], Sūkta 33, p. 196.*

> शत्रु । भ्रातृव्यो वा अर्वेति श्रुतेः । नोऽस्माकं वीरो वीर्यवान् पुत्रादिरभिक्ष-
> मेत । अभिभवतु । यद्वा वीरस्यं नोऽस्मानभिक्षमेथाः । अस्मान् कृतापराधानभि-
> क्षमस्व । हे रुद्र प्रजाभिः पुत्रपौत्रादिभिः प्रजायेमहि । प्रभूताः स्याम ॥

*Gist:* O Rudra, father of the Maruts, may your happiness come to us; do not separate us from the sight of the sun; may our brave son overcome the enemy (or: do you forgive our offences); may we increase with progeny. The tail treats *yuyothāḥ*, *arvati* and *abhikṣameta*.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

मारुतां पितः (*mārutāṃ pitaḥ*)—O Rudra, the father of the Maruts. ते (*te*)—from you to be obtained. सुम्मं (*summaṃ*)—happiness. आ एतु (*ā etu*)—may it come and reach us. नः (*naḥ*)—us. सूरस्य (*sūrasya*) [sic, as supplied]—of the sun. संदृशः (*saṃdṛśaḥ*)—from the sight. मा युयोथाः (*mā yuyothāḥ*)—do not separate (do not take his light away from us). अर्वति (*arvati*)—with the enemy (while fighting). नः (*naḥ*)—our. वीरः (*vīraḥ*)—brave son. अभिक्षमेत (*abhikṣameta*)—may he obtain the power to defeat him. रुद्र (*rudra*)—O Rudra. प्रजाभिः (*prajābhiḥ*)—with sons, grandsons and so on. प्र जायेमहि (*pra jāyemahi*)—cause us to increase.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Rudra, father of the Maruts, may the happiness that is to be had from you come and reach us. Do not separate us from the sight of the sun and keep us in darkness. May our brave son, fighting the enemy, obtain the power to defeat him. O Rudra, cause our line to prosper through sons, grandsons and the rest.

**Printed English translation**

Father of the Maruts, may your felicity extend to us : exclude us not from the sight of the sun : (grant that) our valiant (descendants) may overcome (these) foes, and that we may be multiplied, Rudra, by (our) progeny.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

रुद्र (*rudra*)—Sāyaṇa has explained the word *rudra* in six ways. The word *rudra* is formed from the root रुद् (*rud*) with the causative suffix. Yāska: रुद्रो रौतीति सतः रोरूयमाणो द्रवतीति वा रोदयतेर्वा (*rudro rautīti sataḥ rorūyamāṇo dravatīti vā rodayatervā*). *Rudra* means रौति (*rauti*)—he who makes a sound, like the thunder of a cloud; रोरूयमाणो द्रवति (*rorūyamāṇo dravati*)—he who runs in the midst of the cloud making a noise; रोदयतेर्वा (*rodayatervā*)—he who defeats enemies and makes them weep: thus the meaning is explained. Further, following the history well known in the Kaṭha Upaniṣad [as printed], or following the Maitrāyaṇīya and third-śākhā text, यदरुदत् तद्रुद्रत्वं (*yadarudat tadrudratvaṃ*) ("because he wept, that is Rudra-hood": when his father Prajāpati was struck by arrows, he saw him, was distressed and wept) and यदरोदीत् तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वम् (*yadarodīt tadrudrasya rudratvam*)—because he wept, he is named Rudra (Ni. 10-7): thus the derivation of the word *rudra* is given.

### Printed p. 197

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 16, p. 197.*

Sāyaṇa's explanation of the word *rudra* is different from this. He is *rudra* either because at the time of dissolution he makes all weep; or because he destroys the sorrow called *saṃsāra*; or because he is taught by the Upaniṣads, which are of the nature of sound; or because he teaches self-knowledge to the worshippers of self-knowledge; or because he destroys ignorance, which covers knowledge as thick darkness covers light. Thus, by showing the differences of meaning arising from the sense of the root रुत् (*rut*), the meaning of the word *rudra* is explained. And in accordance with the history set out in the Aitihāsika view, the meaning of the word *rudra*, formed from the root रुदिल् अश्रुविमोचने (*rudil aśruvimocane*) ("to shed tears"), is explained by citing the Vedic text सोऽरोदिद्यदरोदीत्तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं (*so 'rodidyadarodīttadrudrasya rudratvaṃ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-1-1). From this the greatness of Rudra and his compassion towards living beings become evident.

मरुतां पितः रुद्र ते सुम्नं आ एतु (*marutāṃ pitaḥ rudra te sumnaṃ ā etu*)—मरुत्संज्ञानां देवानामुत्पादक रुद्र त्वदीयमस्मभ्यं दातव्यं सुखं आगच्छतु (*marutsaṃjñānāṃ devānāmutpādaka rudra tvadīyamasmabhyaṃ dātavyaṃ sukhaṃ āgacchatu*) (Sāyaṇa's gloss: "O Rudra, begetter of the gods called Maruts, may your happiness, to be given to us, come"). Yāska has explained the word *marutaḥ* as मितराविणो वा, मितरोचिनो वा, महत् द्रवंतीति वा (*mitarāviṇo vā, mitarocino vā, mahat dravaṃtīti vā*) (Ni. 11-14) [as printed]; and having read the word *rudra* among the names of praisers (Ni. 3-19) [as printed] and commented रुद्रो रौतीति सतः, रोरूयमाणो द्रवतीति वा. रोदयतीर्वा (*rudro rautīti sataḥ, rorūyamāṇo dravatīti vā. rodayatīrvā*), he has cited the Kāṭhaka text यदरुदत् तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं (*yadarudat tadrudrasya rudratvaṃ*) and the Maitrāyaṇīya-śākhā text यदरोदीत् तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं (*yadarodīt tadrudrasya rudratvaṃ*) (Ni. 10-7). Sāyaṇa, explaining that the Marut deities are Rudra's sons, says रुद्रस्य च मरुतां पितृत्वं “ इदं पित्रॆ मरुतां ” (ऋ. सं. १-११४-६) इत्यत्र आख्यायिकामुखीनावादिष्म (*rudrasya ca marutāṃ pitṛtvaṃ “ idaṃ pitrè marutāṃ ” (ṛ. saṃ. 1-114-6) ityatra ākhyāyikāmukhīnāvādiṣma*) [as supplied; the bhāṣya above reads *-mukhenāvādiṣṭa*]: in explaining the sūkta इदं पित्रॆ मरुतां (*idaṃ pitrè marutāṃ*) he has described, by way of a narrative, Rudra as the begetter of the Maruts. The wish is that the happiness granted by Rudra, begetter of the Marut deities, may come to us, the sacrificers.

नः सूर्यस्य संदृशः मा युयोथाः (*naḥ sūryasya saṃdṛśaḥ mā yuyothāḥ*)—अस्मान् सूर्यस्य संदर्शनात् मा पृथक्कार्षिः (*asmān sūryasya saṃdarśanāt mā pṛthakkārṣiḥ*). The wish is that the god Rudra may protect us, the sacrificers, so that the light of the sun is not lost to us; and, in नः वीरः अर्वति अभिक्षमेत (*naḥ vīraḥ arvati abhikṣameta*), that Rudra may grant our sons and others the strength to overcome the enemy; or, यद्वा वीरस्त्वं नो अस्मानभिक्षमेथाः अस्मान् कृतापराधानभि क्षमस्व (*yadvā vīrastvaṃ no asmānabhikṣamethāḥ asmān kṛtāparādhānabhi kṣamasva*), that the heroic Rudra may forgive us our offences; and, प्रजाभिः प्रजायेमहि (*prajābhiḥ prajāyemahi*), that we sacrificers may prosper through sons, grandsons and the rest.

### Printed p. 198

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 33, p. 198.*

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वाद॑त्तेभी रुद्र॒ शंत॑मेभिः श॒तं हिमा॑ अतीय भेष॒जेभिः॑ ।
> व्य१॒॑गस्मद्वेषो॑ वित॒रं व्यंहो॒ व्यमी॑वाश्चातयस्वा॒ विषू॑चीः ॥ २ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वादत्तेभिः । रुद्र । शंतमेभिः । शतं । हिमाः । अशीय । भेषजेभिः ।
> वि । अस्मत् । द्वेषः । वितरं । वि । अंहः । वि । अमीवाः । चातयस्व । विषूचीः ॥ २॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे रुद्र त्वादत्तेभिस्त्वया दत्तैः शंतमेभिरतिशयेन सुखकरैर्भेषजेभिर्भे
> षजैरौषधैः शतं हिमाः शतं हेमंतान् शतं संवत्सरानशीय । व्याप्नुयां ॥
> अश्नोतेर्लिजि छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् ॥ अपि च अस्मदस्मत्तो द्वेषो द्वेष्टन्
> विचातयस्व । विनाशय । तथांहः पापं वितरमत्यंतं विचातयस्व । अमीना रोगा-
> न्विषूचीर्विषु नानांचंतीः कृत्स्नशरीरव्यापकान् रोगान्विचातयस्व । अस्मत्तः
> पृथक्कृत्य विनाशय ॥

*Gist:* O Rudra, may I live a hundred years through the soothing medicines given by you; drive away our haters, sin, and the diseases that spread through the whole body. The tail treats *aśīya* (loss of the vikaraṇa) and *vi-cātayasva*.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

रुद्र (*rudra*)—O Rudra. त्वादत्तेभिः (*tvādattebhiḥ*)—by those given by you, शंतमेभिः (*śaṃtamebhiḥ*)—and conducive to happiness, भेषजेभिः (*bheṣajebhiḥ*)—from the herbs. शतं हिमाः (*śataṃ himāḥ*)—a hundred years अशीय (*aśīya*)—may I attain in full. अस्मत् (*asmat*)—from us, द्वेषः (*dveṣaḥ*)—our enemies, वि चातयस्व (*vi cātayasva*)—destroy completely. अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)—sin, वितरं वि (*vitaraṃ vi*)—(destroy) utterly. विषूचीः (*viṣūcīḥ*)—spreading through the body in many ways, अमीवाः वि (*amīvāḥ vi*)—the diseases (destroy).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Rudra, nourished by the use of the herbs given by you and conducive to happiness, may I live fully a hundred years. Destroy completely our enemies, sin, and the diseases that spread in many ways through the body.

### Printed p. 199

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā [as printed मग्वेदसंहिता (*magvedasaṃhitā*)], Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 16, p. 199.*

**Printed English translation**

Nourished by the sanatory vegetables which are bestowed by you, may I live a hundred winters: extirpate my enemies, my exceeding sin, and my manifold infirmities.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Addressing Rudra, the sacrificer expresses the wish that, by the medicines given by Rudra, शंतमेभिः भेषजेभिः (*śaṃtamebhiḥ bheṣajebhiḥ*), that is, abundantly happiness-giving, he may live शतं हिर्मा अशीय (*śataṃ hirmā aśīya*) [as supplied; *hima*], many years, happily; and, in अस्मत् द्वेषः विचातयस्व (*asmat dveṣaḥ vicātayasva*), that Rudra may destroy those who hate us, the sacrificers. And in अंहः वितर (*aṃhaḥ vitara*)—पापं अत्यंतं वि चातयस्व (*pāpaṃ atyaṃtaṃ vi cātayasva*)—he prays that Rudra may destroy our sins. विषूचीः (*viṣūcīḥ*)—विषु नाना अंचतीः कृत्स्नशरीरव्यापर्का (*viṣu nānā aṃcatīḥ kṛtsnaśarīravyāparkā*) [as supplied; *-vyāpakān*]: explaining the word विसूची (*visūcī*) [as supplied] as diseases that pervade the whole body in many ways, the sacrificers pray to the god Rudra that such diseases may be destroyed so that they do not befall the sacrificers.

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> श्रेष्ठो॑ जा॒तस्य॑ रुद्र श्रि॒यासि॑ त॒वस्त॑मस्त॒वसां॑ वज्रबाहो ।
> षर्षि॑ णः पा॒रमंह॑सः स्व॒स्ति विश्वा॑ अ॒भी॑ती॒ रप॑सो युयोधि ॥ ३ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> श्रेष्ठः । जातस्य । रुद्र । श्रिया । असि । तवःतमः । तवसां । वज्रबाहो इति
> वज्रबाहो ।
> पर्षि । नः । पारं । अ०हसः । स्वस्ति । विश्वाः । अभिइतीः । रपसः । युयोधि ॥ ३ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे रुद्र जातस्योत्पन्नस्य सर्वस्य जगतो मध्ये श्रियैश्वर्येण श्रेष्ठः
> प्रशस्यतमोऽसि । भवसि । तथा हे वज्रबाहो आयुधहस्त रुद्र तवसां प्रवृद्धानां

> *he rudra jātasyotpannasya sarvasya jagato madhye śriyaiśvaryeṇa śreṣṭhaḥ*
> *praśasyatamo 'si | bhavasi | tathā he vajrabāho āyudhahasta rudra tavasāṃ pravṛddhānāṃ*

### Printed p. 200

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 33, p. 200.*

> मध्ये तवस्तमोऽतिशयेन प्रवृद्दोऽसि । स त्वं नोऽस्मानंहसः पापस्य पारं तीरं
> स्वस्ति क्षेमेण पर्षि । पारय । तथा रपसः पापस्य विश्वाः सर्वा अभीतीरभिगमनानि
> युयोधि । पृथक्कुरु ॥ यौतेश्छांदसः शपः श्लुः । वा छंदसीत्यपित्त्वस्य विकल्पनात्
> जित्वाभावेऽजितश्चेति हेर्धिः ॥

*Gist:* O Rudra, you are the best of all born beings in glory and the mightiest of the mighty; carry us across the far shore of sin safely and keep off all approaches of sin. The tail treats *yuyodhi*.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

रुद्र (*rudra*)—O Rudra. जातस्य (*jātasya*)—of the whole created world, श्रिया (*śriyā*)—in splendour, श्रेष्ठः (*śreṣṭhaḥ*)—you are supreme. वज्रबाहो (*vajrabāho*)—O Rudra, holding the thunderbolt. तवसा (*tavasā*) [as supplied; Saṃhitā *tavasām*]—among the mighty तवस्तमः (*tavastamaḥ*)—you are the most powerful. नः (*naḥ*)—us, अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—of sin पारं (*pāraṃ*)—to the end (bring), स्वस्ति (*svasti*)—safely पर्षि (*parṣi*)—carry (us) across it. रपसः (*rapasaḥ*)—of sin, विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all अभीतीः (*abhītīḥ*)—blows, युयोधि (*yuyodhi*)—ward off.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Rudra, among all created beings you are supreme by your glory. O Rudra, holding the thunderbolt as weapon, among the mighty you are the mightiest. Bring us to the end of sin and carry us safely across it. Ward off the blows of every kind of sin.

**Printed English translation**

You, Rudra, are the chiefest of beings in glory : you, wielder of the thunderbolt, are the mightiest of the mighty : do you waft us in the safety over (the ocean) of sin : repel all the assaults of iniquity.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Addressing Rudra, the commentary describes him, in जातस्य श्रिया श्रेष्ठः (*jātasya śriyā śreṣṭhaḥ*)—उत्पन्नस्य सर्वस्य जगतः मध्ये ऐश्वर्येण प्रशस्यतमः (*utpannasya sarvasya jagataḥ madhye aiśvaryeṇa praśasyatamaḥ*)—as the most praiseworthy of all, in the created world, by his power in the form of lordship over it.

वज्रबाहो तवसां तवस्तमः (*vajrabāho tavasāṃ tavastamaḥ*)—आयुधहस्त रुद्र प्रवृद्धानां मध्यॆ अतिशयेन प्रवृद्योसि (*āyudhahasta rudra pravṛddhānāṃ madhyè atiśayena pravṛdyosi*) [as supplied; *-vṛddho 'si*]. Explaining the word वज्र (*vajra*) as "weapon", it describes Rudra as bearing the weapon in his hand and as endowed with greatness exceeding that of all the great. The prayer is that this god may release the sacrificers from the sins each has committed and grant welfare; by the sentence अंधसः पारं स्वस्ति पर्षि (*aṃdhasaḥ pāraṃ svasti parṣi*) [as supplied; the ṛk has *aṃhasaḥ*] that he may remove sins committed earlier and bring about welfare; and, in रपसः विश्वाः अभीतीः युयोधि (*rapasaḥ viśvāḥ abhītīḥ yuyodhi*)—पापस्य (*pāpasya*) (continued on the next page)

### Printed p. 201

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 16, p. 201.*

(Continued:) सर्वाः अभिगमनानि पृथक्कुरु (*sarvāḥ abhigamanāni pṛthakkuru*)—that Rudra may keep us separate from contact with all the kinds of sin that may befall the sacrificers in future, that is, may destroy sins; thus the sacrificers' prayer is described.

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> मा त्वा॑ रुद्र चुक्रुधामा॒ नमो॑भि॒र्मा दुष्टु॑ती वृषभ॒ मा॑
> सहू॑ती ।
> उन्नो॑ वी॒रा अ॑र्पय भेष॒जेभि॑र्भि॒षक्त॑मं त्वा भि॒षजां॑ शृणोमि ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> मा । त्वा । रुद्र । चुक्रुधाम । नमभिः । मा । दुःस्तुती । वृषभ । मा । सहूती ।
> उत् । नः । वीरान् । अर्पय । भेषजेभिः । भिषक्तमं । त्वा । भिषजां ।
> शृणोमि ॥ ४ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे रुद्र त्वा त्वां नमोभिरयथाक्रियमाणैर्नमस्कारैर्हविर्भिर्वा मा
> चुक्रुधाम । मा क्रोधयाम । क्रुद्धं मा कार्ष्म ॥ क्रुद्ध कोपे । अस्माण्ण्यंता-
> ल्लुजि चजि रूपं ॥ हे वृषभ कामानां वर्षितर्दुष्टुती दुःस्तुत्याशोभनया
> स्तुत्या मा चुक्रुधामेत्येव । तथा सहूती सहूत्या विसदृशैरन्यर्दॆवैः सहाह्वानेन
> मा क्रोधयाम । श्रेष्ठो हि स्वस्मान्न्यूनेन सहाह्वाने क्रुद्धो भवति । स त्वं
> नोऽस्माकं वीरान् पुत्रान्वेषजेभिस्त्वदीयैर्भेषजैरौषधैरुदर्पय । उत्कृष्टं
> संयोजय । हे रुद्र त्वा त्वां भिषजां चिकित्साभिज्ञानां मध्यॆ भिषक्तममतिशयेन
> भैषज्यस्य कर्तारं शृणोमि । प्रथमो दैव्यो भिषक् । वा. सं. १६-५. । इति च
> मंत्रांतरेpप्युक्तं ॥

*Gist:* O Rudra, may we not anger you by faulty homage, bad praise, or by invoking other gods along with you; make our sons thrive with your medicines; I hear you are the best of physicians.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

रुद्र (*rudra*)—O Rudra. त्वा (*tvā*)—you, नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—with (defective) acts of worship, मा चुक्रुधाम (*mā cukrudhāma*)—we shall not make angry. वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—O Rudra, who showers desired objects. दुष्टुती (*duṣṭutī*)—with inauspicious praises, मा (*mā*)—we shall not make (you) angry.

### Printed p. 202

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 33, p. 202.*

(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 4 continued:) सहूती (*sahūtī*)—by invoking, along with you, other deities unlike you, and worshipping them. मा (*mā*)—(we shall) not (cause) you anger. नः (*naḥ*)—our. वीरान् (*vīrān*)—heroic sons. भेषजेभिः (*bheṣajebhiḥ*)—with your medicines. उत् अर्पय (*ut arpaya*)—cause (them) to be united (with them). त्वा (*tvā*)—you. भिषजां (*bhiṣajāṃ*)—among physicians [as supplied: "ವೈದ್ಯರಲ್ಲಿಲ್ಲಾ"; the Bhāvārtha has "ವೈದ್ಯರೆಲ್ಲೆಲ್ಲಾ", among all physicians]. भिषक्तमं (*bhiṣaktamaṃ*)—as the most excellent physician. शृणोमि (*śṛṇomi*)—I have heard and know.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Rudra, giver of what is desired, may we not provoke you to anger by worship that is deficient, by inauspicious praises, or by calling and worshipping other, unlike deities together with you. We could not do so. Make our heroic sons united with your medicines. I have heard and know you to be the most excellent physician among all physicians.

**Printed English translation**

Let us not provoke you, Rudra, to wrath by our (imperfect)
adorations; nor, showerer (of benifits) [sic], by our unworthy praise, nor by
our invocation (of other deities); invigorate our sons by your medicinal
plants, for I hear that you are a chief physician amongst physicians.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this Ṛk the verb चुक्रुदाम (*cukrudāma*) is repeated three times and added as the verb to each of the three sentences, and the sense is explained accordingly.

In the first sentence: नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*) — आयथाक्रियमाणैः नमस्कारैः हविर्भिर्वा (*āyathākriyamāṇaiḥ namaskāraiḥ havirbhirvā*): it is said that the sacrificers do not make this god Rudra angry by acts of homage performed without following the order laid down in the śāstra, or by offerings of oblation.

दुष्टतौ—दुःस्तुत्या अशोभनया स्तुत्या (*duṣṭatau—duḥstutyā aśobhanayā stutyā*) [as supplied; the Ṛk has दुष्टुती (*duṣṭutī*)]—"not proper", that is: by reciting praises whose sense makes one understand either the might or the qualities of this god otherwise than they are, and thereby preventing this god from giving the sacrificer his wishes as desired, the sacrificers do not act so as to make this god angry; so the sense is described.

सुहूती--सुहूत्या विसदृशैः अन्यैः देवैः सह आह्वानेन मा क्रोधयाम । श्रेष्ठो हि स्वस्मत् न्यूनेन सहाह्वाने न क्रुद्धो भवति । (*suhūtī--suhūtyā visadṛśaiḥ anyaiḥ devaiḥ saha āhvānena mā krodhayāma | śreṣṭho hi svasmat nyūnena sahāhvāne na kruddho bhavati |*) [as supplied; the Ṛk has सहूती (*sahūtī*)]. When this god is invoked at the sacrifices, he is not made angry with the sacrificers by being invoked together with other minor deities. If one who is superior in might and qualities is joined with one lower than himself, the impression arises that he has been slighted. Since that would amount to an offence, the sacrificers, knowing the might of this god, act accordingly; so it is described.

### Printed p. 203

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 16; Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, p. 203.*

(Continued:) Since in other mantras this god is declared "प्रथमो दैव्यो भिषक् (*prathamo daivyo bhiṣak*)" (Tai. Saṃ. 4-1-5-2), "the first divine physician", the sacrificers know him as त्वा भिषजां-चिकित्साभिज्ञानां मध्यॆ अतिशयेन भैषज्यस्य कर्तारं शृणोमि (*tvā bhiṣajāṃ-cikitsābhijñānāṃ madhyè atiśayena bhaiṣajyasya kartāraṃ śṛṇomi*)—the foremost among the physicians who treat and destroy diseases, whether of the mind or of the body. And for this reason also: नः वीर्रान् भेषजेभिः उत् अर्पय—अस्माकं पुत्रान् त्वदीयैः औषध्यैः उत्कृष्टं संयोजय (*naḥ vīrrān bheṣajebhiḥ ut arpaya—asmākaṃ putrān tvadīyaiḥ auṣadhyaiḥ utkṛṣṭaṃ saṃyojaya*) [as supplied: वीर्रान् (*vīrrān*)]. The wish is expressed that this god give proper medicines to the children of us sacrificers and make them excel all others.

Since the performers of sacrifice first invoke all the gods, satisfy them with oblations and the like, and only afterwards invoke this Rudra separately, it is described in this way here that they should not incur this god's wrath.

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> हवी॑मभि॒र्हव॑ते॒ यो ह॒विर्भि॒रव॒ स्तोमे॑भी रु॒द्रं दि॑षीय ।
> ऋ॒दू॒दरः॑ सु॒हवो॒ मा नो॑ अ॒स्यै ब॒भ्रुः सु॒शिप्रो॑ रीरधन्म॒नाय्कॆ ॥॑

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> हवीमभिः । हवते । यः । हविभिः । अव । स्तोमेभिः । रुद्रं । दिषीय ।
> यदूवरः । सुहवः । मा । नः । अस्यै । बभ्रुः । सुशिप्रः । रीरधत् । मनाय्कॆ ॥ ५ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> यो रुद्रो हविर्भिश्चरुपुरोडाशादिभिः सहितैर्हवीमभिराह्वानैः स्तुतिलक्ष-
> णैर्हवते । आह्वयते स्तूयते ॥ व्यत्ययेन कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः । बहुलं
> छंदसीति ह्वयतेः संप्रसारणं ॥ तं रुद्रं स्तोमेभिः स्तोत्रैरवदिषीय ।

> *yo rudro havirbhiścarupuroḍāśādibhiḥ sahitairhavīmabhirāhvānaiḥ stutilakṣa-*
> *ṇairhavate | āhvayate stūyate ‖ vyatyayena karmaṇi kartṛpratyayaḥ | bahulaṃ*
> *chaṃdasīti hvayateḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ‖ taṃ rudraṃ stomebhiḥ stotrairavadiṣīya |*

### Printed p. 204

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 33, p. 204.*

> अवखंडयामि । पृथक्करोमि । अपगतक्रोधं करोमीति यावत् ॥ दो अवखं-
> दने । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । बहुलं छंदसीतीत्वं ॥ युदूदरः । युदूदरो
> मृदूदर इति यास्कः । नि. ६ ४. । सुहवः शोभनाह्वानो बभ्रुर्भर्ता सर्वस्य
> बभ्रुवर्णो वा । सुशिप्रः । शिप्रे हनू नासिके वा । शोभनशिप्रः । एवंगुणविशिष्टः
> स रुद्रोस्यॆ मनाय्कॆ । हन्मीति मन्यमानाबुद्धिर्मना । तस्यै नोऽस्मान्मा रीरधत् ।
> मा वशं नैषीत् ॥ रथ हिंसासंराद्योः । अस्माण्ण्यंताल्लुज चजु रूपं । रध्यति-
> र्वशगमन इति यास्कः ॥

*Gist:* The Rudra who is invoked with oblations and praises I will appease with hymns; may he, soft-bellied, bountiful, tawny and fair-jawed, not give us over to this hostile intent.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

यः (*yaḥ*)—the Rudra who. हविर्भिः (*havirbhiḥ*)—accompanied by cooked offerings, cakes and the like. हवीमभिः (*havīmabhiḥ*)—with invocations that are in the form of praise. हवते (*havate*)—is praised. रुद्रं (*rudraṃ*)—such a Rudra. स्तोमेभिः (*stomebhiḥ*)—with hymns. अव दिषीय (*ava diṣīya*)—I make (him) free from anger and calm of mind. ऋतूदरः (*ṛtūdaraḥ*) [as supplied; Saṃhitā ऋदूदरः (*ṛdūdaraḥ*), bhāṣya युदूदरः (*yudūdaraḥ*)]—one with a soft belly. सुहवः (*suhavaḥ*)—one with an excellent invocation. बभ्रुः (*babhruḥ*)—one of tawny colour. सुशिप्रः (*suśipraḥ*)—one with fine cheeks or nose, that Rudra. अस्यॆ मनाय्कॆ (*asyè manāykè*)—to this evil mind that wishes us harm. नः (*naḥ*)—us. मा रीरधत् (*mā rīradhat*)—may he not bring (us) under its sway.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The Rudra who is praised with invocations that are in the form of praise and accompanied by cooked offerings, cakes and the like, such a Rudra I make free from anger and calm of mind by praising him with hymns. May Rudra, who has a soft belly, an excellent invocation, a form of tawny colour and a fine nose, not bring us under the sway of this evil mind that wishes us harm.

**Printed English translation**

May I pacify by my praises that Rudra, who is worshipped with
invocations and oblations; and never may he who is soft-bellied. of a
tawny hue, and handsome chin ; who is reverently invoked ; subject us not
to that malevolent disposition (that purposes our destruction).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

This Rudra is ऋदूदरः सुहवः बभ्रुः सुशिप्रः (*ṛdūdaraḥ suhavaḥ babhruḥ suśipraḥ*) — शोभनाह्वानः भर्ता सर्वस्य बभ्रुवर्णो वा शिप्रे हनूनासिके वा सुशिप्रः (*śobhanāhvānaḥ bhartā sarvasya babhruvarṇo vā śipre hanūnāsike vā suśipraḥ*) — "soft-bellied", that is, of fierce [text breaks off here] (continued on the next page)

### Printed p. 205

dress, ornaments and the like, yet he has an intention that produces welfare. Because the invocation of this god is beneficial, he is one of good invocation, the lord of all; or one whose body has a golden-brown lustre; one who has handsome cheeks or a nose; or, describing this god, the sacrificers (say): हविर्भिः हवीमभिः हवते स्तोमेभिः अवदिषीय (*havirbhiḥ havīmabhiḥ havate stomebhiḥ avadiṣīya*), चरुपुरोडाशादिभिः सहितैः आह्वानैः स्तुतिलक्षणै, स्त्युयते स्तोत्रैः अवखंडयामि—पृथक्करोमि (*carupuroḍāśādibhiḥ sahitaiḥ āhvānaiḥ stutilakṣaṇai, styuyate stotraiḥ avakhaṃḍayāmi—pṛthakkaromi*) (as supplied): by the offerings of oblations such as cooked offerings and cakes, and by invocations in the form of praise, having praised and gratified (him), we so act that no anger arises in this god; and अस्यॆ मनाय्कॆ नः मा रीरधत् (*asyè manāykè naḥ mā rīradhat*), हन्मीति मन्यमाना बुद्धिमना तस्यॆ अस्मान् मा वशं नैषीत् (*hanmīti manyamānā buddhimanā tasyè asmān mā vaśaṃ naiṣīt*)—it is prayed that the intention of destroying others, which exists (in him), may not arise towards the sacrificers.

ऋदूदरः (*ṛdūdaraḥ*): Yāska explains ऋदूदरः सोमो मृदूदरो मृदुरुदरेष्टिति वा (*ṛdūdaraḥ somo mṛdūdaro mṛdurudareṣṭiti vā*) (Si. 6-4 [as supplied]) as "one with a soft middle part", or "soft in the middle (inside)", and as the Soma (creeper); and he has explained the word शिप्र (*śipra*) as the cheeks or the nose.

सुशिप्रः (*suśipraḥ*): Yāska: सुशिप्रमेतेन व्याख्यातं । हनू नासिके वा, हनुः हंतेः । नासिका नसतेः (*suśiprametena vyākhyātaṃ | hanū nāsike vā, hanuḥ haṃteḥ | nāsikā nasateḥ*) (Ni. 6-17); he has explained the meaning of the word शिप्र as the cheeks or the nose.

बभ्रुः (*babhruḥ*): In explaining the meaning of the word बभ्रु (*babhru*), Yāska cites the Ṛk या ओषधीः पूर्वा जाता देवेभ्यस्त्रियुगं पुरा । मन्यॆ नु बभ्रूणामहं शतं धामानि सप्त च ॥ (*yā oṣadhīḥ pūrvā jātā devebhyastriyugaṃ purā | manyè nu babhrūṇāmahaṃ śataṃ dhāmāni sapta ca ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-97-1) and explains बभ्रूणां बभ्रुवर्णानां (*babhrūṇāṃ babhruvarṇānāṃ*) (Ni. 9-29). Durgācārya gives the meaning: ओषधयः स्वभावतः पच्यमानाः सर्वा एव बभ्रुवर्णाः कपिलाः संपद्यंते (*oṣadhayaḥ svabhāvataḥ pacyamānāḥ sarvā eva babhruvarṇāḥ kapilāḥ saṃpadyaṃte*); that is, the herbs take on a golden-brown colour at the time they generally ripen.

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उन्मा॑ ममंद वृष॒भो म॒रुत्वा॒न्त्वक्षी॑यसा॒ वय॑सा॒ नाध॑मानं ।
> घृणी॑व च्छा॒याम॑र॒पा अ॑ती॒या वि॑वासेयं रु॒द्रस्य॑ सु॒म्मं ॥ ६ ॥

> *unmā mamaṃda vṛṣabho marutvāntvakṣīyasā vayasā nādhamānaṃ |*
> *ghṛṇīva cchāyāmarapā atīyā vivāseyaṃ rudrasya summaṃ ‖ 6 ‖*

### Printed p. 206

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उत् । मा । ममंद । वृषभः । मरुत्वान् । त्वक्षीयसा । वयसा । नाधमानं ।
> घृणि इव । छायां। अरपाः । अतीय । आ । विवासेयं । रुद्रस्य । सुम्नं ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> वृषभः कामानां वर्षिता मरुत्वान् मरुद्भिः पुत्रैर्युक्तो रुद्रो नाध
> मानं याचमानं मामां त्वक्षीयसा दीप्तेन वयसान्नेनोन मंद । उत्कर्षेण
> तर्पयतु । अपि जाहं फृणीव छायां यथा सूर्यकिरणसंतप्तश्चायां प्रविशति
> एवं रुद्रस्य सुम्मं सुखमरपा आपापः सन् अशीय । व्याप्प्नुयां । तदर्थं तं
> रुद्रमाविवासेयं । परिचरेयं ॥ विवासतिः परिचरणकर्मा ॥

*Gist:* May Rudra, showerer of desires and accompanied by the Maruts, gratify me, a suppliant, with bright food; free from sin I would attain his happiness as one scorched by the sun's rays enters shade. The tail explains *vivāsati* as a verb of serving.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the one who showers the desired object; मरुत्वान् (*marutvān*)—accompanied by the Marut deities; that Rudra; नाधमानं (*nādhamānaṃ*)—who begs in humility; मा (*mā*)—me; त्वक्षीयसा (*tvakṣīyasā*)—with bright; वयसा (*vayasā*)—with food; उत् ममन्द (*ut mamanda*)—may he gratify exceedingly; (and may I also) घृणीव (*ghṛṇīva*)—like one scorched by the heat of the sun; छायां (*chāyāṃ*)—takes refuge in the shade; रुद्रस्य (*rudrasya*)—obtainable from Rudra; सुम्मं (*summaṃ*)—happiness; अरपाः (*arapāḥ*)—being free from sin; अशीय (*aśīya*)—may I obtain fully.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

May Rudra, who showers the desired object and is accompanied by the Marut deities, gratify me, who beg in humility, exceedingly with bright food. May I also, being free from sin, fully obtain the happiness obtainable from Rudra, as one scorched by the heat of the sun takes refuge in the shade.

**Printed English translation**

May the showerer of benifits [sic], the lord of Maruts, gratify me his
suppliant with invigorating food : may I, free from sin, so propitiate
Rudra, that I may attain to his felicity, as a man, distressed by heat,
(finds relief) in the shade.

### Printed p. 207

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—कामानां वर्षिता (*kāmānāṃ varṣitā*): the quality of the god Rudra is described thus, that he gives desired things to those who take refuge in him. May this Rudra, मरुत्वान् (*marutvān*), accompanied by his sons the Marut deities, fulfil the prayer of the sacrificers by granting bright food and so produce satisfaction; and फृणीव छायां रुद्रस्य सुम्नं अरसा आशीय—यथा सूर्यकिरणसंतप्तः छायां प्रविशति एवं रुद्रस्य सुखं अपापः व्यापु यां (*phṛṇīva chāyāṃ rudrasya sumnaṃ arasā āśīya—yathā sūryakiraṇasaṃtaptaḥ chāyāṃ praviśati evaṃ rudrasya sukhaṃ apāpaḥ vyāpu yāṃ*) (as supplied): as one scorched by the sharp heat of the sun takes refuge in the shade, so the sacrificer, free from sins, will obtain the happiness granted by Rudra—thus the sacrificer's blessing is described.

अरपाः (*arapāḥ*)—अपापः (*apāpaḥ*): रपोरिप्रमिति पापनामनी भवतः (*raporipramiti pāpanāmanī bhavataḥ*) (Ni. 4-21): Yāska explains that the two words रपः and रिप्र (*rapaḥ*, *ripra*) both denote sin. Here the word अरपाः is explained as one without sin.

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> क्व१॒ं॑ स्य ते॑ रुद्र मृळ॒याकु॒र्हस्तो॒ यो अस्ति॑ भेष॒जो जला॑षः ।
> अ॒प॒भ॒र्तान् रप॑सो॒ दैव्य॑सा॒भी नु मा॑ वृषभ चक्षमीथाः ॥ ७ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> क्व । स्यः । ते । रुद्र । मृळयाकुः । हस्तः । यः । अस्ति । भेषजः । जलाषः ।
> अपभर्ता । रहसः । दैव्यस्य । अभि । नु । मा । वृषभ । चक्षमीथाः ॥ ७ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे रुद्र ते तव मृळयाकुः सुखयिता स्यः स हस्तः क्व कुत्र वर्तते । यो
> हस्तो भेषजो भैषज्यकृत् जलाषः सर्वेषां सुखकरोऽस्ति । भवति । स हस्तो
> विद्यत एव । तेन हस्तेन मां रक्षेति भावः । अपि च हे वृषभ कामानां वर्षितः
> दैव्यस्य देवकृतस्य रपसः पापस्यापभर्तापहर्ता विनाशयिता भूत्वा कृतापराधं
> मां नु क्षिप्रमभिचक्षमीथाः । अभिक्षमस्व । क्षमूष् सहने । लजि छांदसः शपः श्लुः ।
> बहुलं छंदसीतीडागमः ॥

*Gist:* Where is that gracious, healing hand of yours, Rudra? With it protect me; showerer of desires, remove the sin caused by the gods and forgive me quickly. The tail explains *abhicakṣamīthāḥ*.

### Printed p. 208

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

रुद्र (*rudra*)—O Rudra. यः (*yaḥ*)—which hand. भेषजः (*bheṣajaḥ*)—that destroys disease. जलाषः (*jalāṣaḥ*)—that gives joy. अस्ति (*asti*)—is. ते (*te*)—your. मृळयाकुः (*mṛḷayākuḥ*)—the comforting. स्यः (*syaḥ*)—the well-known. हस्तः (*hastaḥ*)—hand. क्व (*kva*)—where? वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—O Rudra, showerer of desires. दैव्यस्य (*daivyasya*)—caused by the gods. रपसः (*rapasaḥ*)—also the sin. अपभर्ता (*apabhartā*)—you who have the power to destroy it. मा (*mā*)—me, the offender. नु (*nu*)—quickly. अभि चक्षमीथाः (*abhi cakṣamīthāḥ*)—forgive completely.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Rudra, where is that hand of yours, comforting and well known, which destroys disease and gives joy? O Rudra, showerer of desires, you who have the power to destroy even the sin done by the gods and to forgive: forgive me, the offender, quickly and completely.

**Printed English translation**

Where, Rudra, is your joy-dispensing hand, which is the healer and
delighter (of all) : showerer (of benifits) [sic], you are the dispeller of the sins
of the gods, quickly have compassion upon me.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

रुद्र ते मृळयाकुः हस्तः क्व (*rudra te mṛḷayākuḥ hastaḥ kva*)—Asking where the comforting hand is, the text states the extraordinary quality of the hand: that this hand destroys the disease of all and is comforting to all; and it expresses the wish that Rudra protect the sacrificers with that hand (भेषजः जलाषः भैषज्यकृत् सर्वेषां सुखकरः (*bheṣajaḥ jalāṣaḥ bhaiṣajyakṛt sarveṣāṃ sukhakaraḥ*); तेन हस्तेन मां रक्ष (*tena hastena māṃ rakṣa*)).

दैव्यस्य रपसः अपभर्ता मा अभिचक्षमीथाः (*daivyasya rapasaḥ apabhartā mā abhicakṣamīthāḥ*)—देवकृतस्य पापस्य विनाशयिता भूत्वा कृतापराधं मां अभिक्षमस्व (*devakṛtasya pāpasya vināśayitā bhūtvā kṛtāparādhaṃ māṃ abhikṣamasva*). It is explained thus: may Rudra destroy the sins that have come upon the sacrificer through contrary conduct towards the gods, and pardon me, the sacrificer who has committed the offence.

जलाषः—सर्वेषां सुखकरः (*jalāṣaḥ—sarveṣāṃ sukhakaraḥ*). The word जलाष (*jalāṣa*) is stated by Yāska (Ni. 2-24) among the names of water; here the meaning "comforting" is given.

### Printed p. 209

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्र ब॒भ्रवे॑ वृष॒भाय॑ श्वि ती॒चे म॒हो म॒हीं सु॑ष्टु॒तिमा॑रयामि ।
> न॒म॒स्या क॑ल्मली॒किनं॒ नमो॑भिर्गृणी॒मसि॑ त्वे॒षं रु॒द्रस्य॒ नाम॑ ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्र । बभ्रवे । वृषभाय । श्वितीचे । महः । महीं । सुस्तुतिं । ईरयामि ।
> नमस्य । कल्मलीकिनं । नमःभिः । गृणीमसि । त्वेषं । रुद्रस्य । नाम ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> रुद्रदेवत्ये पशौ वपापुरोडाशहविषां क्रमेण प्र बभ्रव इत्याद्यास्ति स्रो
> याज्याः । प्र बभ्रवे वृषभाय श्वितीच इति तिस्र आ पश्चातान्नासत्या पुरस्तात् ।
> आ. ३-८. । इति ॥
> बभ्रवे विश्वस्य भर्त्रॆ बभ्रुवर्णाय वा वृषभाय कामानां वर्षित्रे तद्वत्
> प्रसह्यकारिणे वा श्चितीचे श्वैत्यमंचते ॥ श्चिता वर्णॆ । औणादिक इन्मत्तयः । श्ति-
> मंचतीत्यंचतेर्यत्विगित्यादिना क्विन् । चतुर्थैकवचनेच इत्यकारलोपे चाविति
> दीर्घत्वं । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥ एवंगुणविशिष्टाय रुद्राय
> महो महीं महतोऽपि महतीं सुष्टुतिं शोभनस्तुतिं प्रेरयामि । प्रकर्षे-
> णोच्चारयामि । हे स्तोतः कल्मलीकिनं । ज्वलतो नामधेयमेतत्। नैघं. १-१७।
> ज्वलंतं । कलयत्यपगमयति मलमिति कल्मलीकं तेजः । तद्वंतं रुद्रं नमोभि-
> र्नमस्कारैर्हविर्भिर्वा नमस्य । पूजय । वयं च रुद्रस्य महादेवस्य त्वेषं
> दीप्तं नाम गृणीमसि ! गृणीमः संकीर्तयामः ॥ गृ शब्दे । क्रैयादिकः ।
> इदंतो मसिः । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः ॥

*Gist:* In the animal sacrifice to Rudra, this Ṛk and the next two are the yājyā verses for the vapā, puroḍāśa and oblations in order (Āśv. 3-8). Rudra is called *babhru*, *vṛṣabha*, *śvitīca*; the poet offers him a great praise and bids the worshipper adore the blazing Rudra. The tail treats *śvitīca*, *gṛṇīmasi*.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

बभ्रवे (*babhrave*)—to the one of brown colour; वृषभाय (*vṛṣabhāya*)—the showerer of desires; श्वितीचे (*śvitīce*)—the one of white form, to Rudra. महो महीं (*maho mahīṃ*)—greater than the excellent. सुष्टुतिं (*suṣṭutiṃ*)—excellent praise. प्र ईरयामि (*pra īrayāmi*)—I offer with devotion. कल्मलीकिनं (*kalmalīkinaṃ*)—Rudra, who has the radiance that destroys impurity. नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—with salutations or with oblations. नमस्य (*namasya*)—worship! (we also) रुद्रस्य (*rudrasya*)—of Rudra. त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*)—the radiant power. गृणीमसि नाम (*gṛṇīmasi nāma*)—we surely praise.

### Printed p. 210

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

To Rudra, who is of brown colour, the showerer of desires, and of white form, I offer praise greater than the excellent. Worship with oblations Rudra, who has the radiance that destroys impurity. We also praise the radiant power of Rudra.

**Printed English translation**

I address infinite and earnest praise to the showerer (of benifits) [sic], the
cherisher (of all), the white-complexioned : adore the consumer (of sin),
with prostrations: we gloriaify [sic] the illustrious name of Rudra.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In the animal sacrifice related to Rudra, when the vapā, puroḍāśa and oblations are offered, the Ṛk प्र बभ्रवे (*pra babhrave*) of this sūkta and the two following Ṛks are to be used in order as yājyā mantras; this is stated by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, प्र बभ्रवे वृषभाय श्वितीच इति तिस्र आ पश्चातान्नासत्या पुरस्तात् (*pra babhrave vṛṣabhāya śvitīca iti tisra ā paścātānnāsatyā purastāt*) (Āś. 3-8).

बभ्रवे-विश्वस्य भर्त्रे बभ्रुवर्णाय वा (*babhrave-viśvasya bhartre babhruvarṇāya vā*): Rudra is the lord of the whole world, or he is of brown colour. वृषभाय कामानां वर्षित्रॆ तद्वत्पसह्यकारिणे वा (*vṛṣabhāya kāmānāṃ varṣitrè tadvatpasahyakāriṇe vā*): he fulfils the wishes of those who serve him, or, like a bull, does his work by force. श्वितीचे—शैत्यमंचते (*śvitīce—śaityamaṃcate*): he has a pure radiance. Having so described Rudra, the Ṛṣi, seer of the mantra, says that for Rudra possessed of these qualities, महो महीं सुष्टुतिं ईरयामि (*maho mahīṃ suṣṭutiṃ īrayāmi*), "I shall utter abundantly praise full of greatness."

कल्मलीकिनं रुद्रं नमोभिः नमस्य—ज्वलंतं रुद्रं नमस्कारैः हविर्भिर्वा पूजय (*kalmalīkinaṃ rudraṃ namobhiḥ namasya—jvalaṃtaṃ rudraṃ namaskāraiḥ havirbhirvā pūjaya*): addressing the sacrificer and the priest who are the praisers, it is said: worship Rudra, who shines with radiance, with oblations and with salutations.

रुद्रस्य तेषं नाम गृणीमसि—महादेवस्य दीप्तं नाम संकीर्तयामः (*rudrasya teṣaṃ nāma gṛṇīmasi—mahādevasya dīptaṃ nāma saṃkīrtayāmaḥ*): it is explained that we, the seers of the mantra, recite the name, shining with brilliance, of this Mahādeva who is full of greatness beyond all the gods.

कल्मलीकिनं—कलयति अपगमयति मलमिति कल्मलीकं तेजः तद्वंतं (*kalmalīkinaṃ—kalayati apagamayati malamiti kalmalīkaṃ tejaḥ tadvaṃtaṃ*). Yāska, कल्मलीकिनं (*kalmalīkinaṃ*) the word, ज्वलतो नामधेयानि (*jvalato nāmadheyāni*) among the names of ज्वलतः (*jvalataḥ*) (blazing)

### Printed p. 211

*Running head: [A. 2 A. 7 V. 17.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 211 (as supplied). The window begins inside the Special Topics of Ṛk 8.*

(Ni. 2-28) he has read. Sāyaṇa explains मलं (*malaṃ*) as "that which destroys sin", explains the word कल्मलीक (*kalmalīka*) as radiance, and describes कल्मलीकुं (*kalmalīkuṃ*) as one possessed of radiance.

#### Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स्थि॒रेभि॒रंगैः॑ पुरु॒रूप॑ उ॒ग्रो ब॒भ्रुः शु॒क्रेभिः॑ पिपिशे॒ हिर॑ण्यैः ।
> ईशा॑नाद॒स्य भुव॑नस्य॒ भूरे॒न्वा उ॑ योषद्रु॒दाद॑सु॒र्यं॑ ॥ ९ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> स्थिरेभिः । अंगैः । पुरुरूपः । उग्रः । बभ्रुः । शुक्रेभिः । पिपिशे । हिरण्यैः ।
> ईशानात् । अस्य । भुवनस्य । भूरेः । न । वै । ऊं इति । योषत् । रुद्रात् ।
> असुर्यं ॥ ९ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> स्थिरेभिः स्थिरैर्दृढैरंगैरवयवय्यर्युक्तः पुरुरूपोऽष्टमूर्त्यात्मकैर्ब-
> हुभी रूपैरुपेत उग्र उद्धूर्णस्तेजस्वी बभ्रुर्भर्ता बभ्रुवर्णो वा रुद्रः
> शुक्रेभिर्दिप्तैर्हिरण्यैहिरण्मय्कॆर्हितरमणीय्कॆर्वालंकारैः पिपिशे ! दीप्यते ॥ पित
> अवयवे । कर्मणि लिट् ॥ ईशानादीश्वरादस्य भुवनस्य भूतजातस्य भूरेर्भर्तू
> रुद्रादसुर्यं ॥ असु क्षेपणे । असेरुरन् । आसरः क्षेप्ता । तत्र साधुः ॥ असुर्यं
> बलं न वा उ योषत् । नैव पृथग्भवति ॥ यौतेर्लॆट्व्यडागमः । सिब्बहुलं
> लेटीति सिप् ॥

*Gist:* Rudra, with firm limbs and many (eightfold) forms, fierce and brown, shines with bright golden ornaments; from the lord and sustainer of this world strength is never separate. The tail treats *piśe* and *asuryam*.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

स्थिरेभिः (*sthirebhiḥ*)—firm; अंगैः (*aṃgaiḥ*)—endowed with limbs; पुरुरूपः (*pururūpaḥ*)—endowed with many forms; उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—possessed of manifest brilliance; बभ्रुः (*babhruḥ*)—of brown colour: Rudra; शुक्रेभिः (*śukrebhiḥ*)—resplendent; हिरण्यैः (*hiraṇyaiḥ*)—golden; with such ornaments; पिपिशे (*pipiśe*)—he shines; ईशानात् (*īśānāt*)—from the lord; अस्य भुवनस्य (*asya bhuvanasya*)—for this whole world; भूरेः (*bhūreḥ*)—the sustainer; रुद्रात् (*rudrāt*)—from Rudra; असुरं (*asuraṃ*) [sic: the Saṃhitā has असुर्यं (*asuryaṃ*)]—universal power; न वा उ योषत् (*na vā u yoṣat*)—is not separated at all.

### Printed p. 212

*Running head: [212 Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2 A. 4 Sū. 33] (as supplied).*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Rudra, who has firm limbs, is endowed with many forms, has manifest brilliance and is of brown colour, shines with resplendent golden ornaments. From Rudra, the lord, who sustains this whole world, universal power is never separated.

**Printed English translation**

(Firm) with strong limbs, assuming many forms, fierce, and tawny-coloured, he shines with brilliant golden ornaments : vigour is inseparable from Rudra, the supreme ruler and lord of this world.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Rudra is स्थिरेभिरंगैः (*sthirebhiraṃgaiḥ*) (दृढैरवयवैर्युक्तः (*dṛḍhairavayavairyuktaḥ*)): endowed with limbs that are joined with strength and brilliance and are powerful. पुरुरूपः (*pururūpaḥ*) (अष्टमूर्त्यात्मकैः बहुभिः रूपैः उपेतः (*aṣṭamūrtyātmakaiḥ bahubhiḥ rūpaiḥ upetaḥ*)): he shines with the eight forms, namely earth, water, sun, moon, fire, wind, space and the yajamāna who performs the sacrifice; and उग्रः (*ugraḥ*) (उद्गूर्णः तेजस्वी (*udgūrṇaḥ tejasvī*)): he is filled with strength and brilliance; and बभ्रुः (*babhruḥ*) (भर्ता बभ्रुवर्णो वा (*bhartā babhruvarṇo vā*)): he is the overlord of the world, or he is of golden-brown colour. Having so described him, (Sāyaṇa) explains that Rudra शुक्रेभिः हिरण्यैः पिपिशे (*śukrebhiḥ hiraṇyaiḥ pipiśe*) (दीपैः हितरमणीयैः हिरण्मय्यरलंकारैर्वा दीप्यते (*dīpaiḥ hitaramaṇīyaiḥ hiraṇmayyaralaṃkārairvā dīpyate*)): adorns himself with golden ornaments that are very bright, beneficial and charming.

ईश्वरात् रुद्रात् असुर्यं न वा उ योषत् (*īśvarāt rudrāt asuryaṃ na vā u yoṣat*)—अस्य भूतजातस्य भर्तुः (*asya bhūtajātasya bhartuḥ*) ईश्वरात् असुर्यं बलं नैव पृथक् भवति (*īśvarāt asuryaṃ balaṃ naiva pṛthak bhavati*): it is said that no other thing is mightier than this Rudra, the lord of all beings and master of everything.

असुर्यं (*asuryaṃ*)—the suffix उरन् (*uran*) is added to the root असु क्षेपणे (*asu kṣepaṇe*) and the word असुर (*asura*) results; by असुरः क्षेप्ता (*asuraḥ kṣeptā*) the word असुर (*asura*) means "one who throws". By the sūtra तत्र साधुः (*tatra sādhuḥ*) the suffix य (*ya*) is added, giving असुर्य (*asurya*). Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as "strength".

### Printed p. 213

*Running head: [A. 2 A. 7 V. 17.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 213 (as supplied).*

#### Ṛk 10

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अर्ह॑न्बिभर्षि॒ साय॑कानि॒ धन्वाह॑न्नि॒ष्कं य॑ज॒तं वि॒श्वरू॑पं ।
> अर्प॑न्नि॒दं द॑यसे॒ विश्व॒मभ्वं॒ न वा ओजी॑यो रुद्र॒ त्वद॑स्ति ॥ १० ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अर्हन् । बिभर्षि । सायकानि । धन्व । अर्हन् । निष्कं । यजतं । विश्वरूपं ।
> अर्हन् । इदं । दयसे । विश्वं । अभ्वं । न । वै । ओजीयः । रुद्र । त्वत् । अस्ति ॥ १० ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे रुद्र त्वमर्हन् अर्हो योग्य एव सन् सायकानि शरान् धन्व धनुश्च
> बिभर्षि । धारयसि । तथार्हन्नेव यजतं यजनीयं पूजनीयं विश्वरूपं
> बहुविधरूपयुक्तं निष्कं हारं बभर्षि । तथार्हन्नेवेदं विश्वं सर्वमभ्वं ।
> महन्नामृतत् । अतिविस्तृतं जगद्दयसे । रक्षिसि । देज् रक्षणे । हे रुद्र त्वत्
> त्वत्तोऽन्यत् किंचिदोजीय ओजस्वितरं बलवत्तरं न वा अस्ति । न खलु विद्यते ।
> अतस्त्वमेवोक्तव्यापारेषु योज्य इत्यर्थः ॥ ओजःशब्दान्मत्वर्तियो विनिः । ततः
> अतिशायनिक इष्टन् । विन्मत्तोर्लुक् । टेरिति टिलोपः ॥

*Gist:* O Rudra, though worthy of worship you bear arrows, bow and a many-formed necklace, and protect this vast universe; nothing is mightier than you. The tail treats *ojīyaḥ*.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

रुद्र (*rudra*)—O Rudra; अर्हन् (*arhan*)—you who are worthy of worship; सायकानि (*sāyakāni*)—arrows; धन्व (*dhanva*)—and bow; बिभर्षि (*bibharṣi*)—you bear; अर्हन् (*arhan*)—being worthy of worship; यजतं (*yajataṃ*)—worthy of worship; विश्वरूपं (*viśvarūpaṃ*)—of many forms; निष्कं (*niṣkaṃ*)—a necklace (you wear); अर्हन् (*arhan*)—being worthy of praise; इदं विश्वं (*idaṃ viśvaṃ*)—this whole; अभ्वं (*abhvaṃ*)—and great world; दयसे (*dayase*)—you protect; रुद्र (*rudra*)—O Rudra; ओजीयः (*ojīyaḥ*)—one with greater inner strength than you; त्वत् (*tvat*)—other than you, anyone; न वै अस्ति (*na vai asti*)—there is none at all.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Rudra, you who are worthy of worship bear arrows and bow. Being worthy of worship, you wear a necklace that is worthy of worship and of many forms. Being worthy of praise, you protect this whole and great world. O Rudra, there is none at all other than you who has greater strength than you.

### Printed p. 214

*Running head: [214 Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [Maṃ. 2. A. 4. Sū. 33.] (as supplied).*

**Printed English translation**

Worthy ( of reverence ), you bear arrows and a bow : worthy
(of praise), you wear an adorable and omniform necklace; worthy (of
adoration), you preserve all this vast universe: there is no one more
powerful than you.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Addressing Rudra as "O Rudra", the text says that this Rudra, being himself worthy of worship, bears bow and arrows; that he wears यजनीयं पूजनीयं विश्वरूपं निष्कं हारं बिभर्षि (*yajanīyaṃ pūjanīyaṃ viśvarūpaṃ niṣkaṃ hāraṃ bibharṣi*), necklaces that are worthy of worship and of manifold forms; and that अर्हन्नेव इदं विश्वं अभ्वं दयसे (*arhanneva idaṃ viśvaṃ abhvaṃ dayase*), he protects all this vast world. Thus the power, the adornment and the wondrous work of this Rudra are described. And ओजेयः न वै अस्ति (*ojeyaḥ na vai asti*) [as supplied; the Ṛk has ओजीयः] — त्वत्तः अन्यत् किंचित् बलवत्तरं न खलु विद्यते (*tvattaḥ anyat kiṃcit balavattaraṃ na khalu vidyate*): since nothing other than this Rudra, nothing greater in strength, exists, त्वमेव उक्तव्यापारेषु योज्यः (*tvameva uktavyāpāreṣu yojyaḥ*) — it is said that Rudra alone is capable of performing the work of protecting this world.

अभ्वं (*abhvaṃ*)—अतिविस्तृतं (*ativistṛtaṃ*). Yāska has read the word अभ्व (*abhva*) among the names of "great" (Ni. 3-13). Sāyaṇa takes this word as an adjective of विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*) and explains the meaning as "very vast".

#### Ṛk 11

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स्तु॒हि श्रु॒तं ग॑र्त॒सदं॒ युवा॑नं मृ॒गं न भी॒ममु॑पह॒त्तु मु॒ग्रं ।
> मृ॒ळा ज॑रि॒त्रे रु॑द्र॒ स्तवा॑नो॒ऽन्यं ते॑ अ॒स्मन्नि व॑पंतु॒ सेनाः॑ ॥ ११ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> स्तुहि । श्रुतं । गर्तसदं । युवानं । मृगं । न । भीमं । उपहत्नुं । उग्रं ।
> मृळ । जरित्रे । रुद्र । स्तवानः । अन्यं । ते । अस्मत् । नि । वपंतु । सेनाः ॥ ११ ॥

> *stuhi | śrutaṃ | gartasadaṃ | yuvānaṃ | mṛgaṃ | na | bhīmaṃ | upahatnuṃ | ugraṃ |*
> *mṛḷa | jaritre | rudra | stavānaḥ | anyaṃ | te | asmat | ni | vapaṃtu | senāḥ ‖ 11 ‖*

### Printed p. 215

*Running head: [A. 2. A. 7. V. 18.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 215 (as supplied).*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> प्रयाणे मृगस्यामनोज्ञवचः श्रुत्वा स्तुहि श्रुतमित्येतां जपेत् । सूत्रितं

> रथः । तत्र सीदंतं युवानं नित्यतरुणं मृगं न भीमं मृगं सिंहमिव भयंकरं ।
> उपहत्नुमुपहंतारं शत्रूणां मुग्रमुद्गूर्णं । हे रुद्र त्वं स्तवानोSस्माभिः
> स्तूयमानः सन् जरित्रॆ स्तोत्रे मह्यं मृळ । सुखय । ते त्वदीयाः सेना
> अस्मदन्यमस्मद्व्यतिरिक्तं पुरुषं निवपंतु । निघ्नंतु ॥

> *prayāṇe mṛgasyāmanojñavacaḥ śrutvā stuhi śrutamityetāṃ japet | sūtritaṃ*

> *he stotaḥ śrutaṃ viśrutaṃ prakhyātaṃ rudraṃ stuhi | kīdṛśaṃ | gartasadaṃ | garto*
> *rathaḥ | tatra sīdaṃtaṃ yuvānaṃ nityataruṇaṃ mṛgaṃ na bhīmaṃ mṛgaṃ siṃhamiva bhayaṃkaraṃ |*
> *upahatnumupahaṃtāraṃ śatrūṇāṃ mugramudgūrṇaṃ | he rudra tvaṃ stavānoSsmābhiḥ*
> *stūyamānaḥ san jaritrè stotre mahyaṃ mṛḷa | sukhaya | te tvadīyāḥ senā*
