Gist: The Maruts, in the form of the Aṅgirases who attained success in ten months, performed the sacrifice before the Ādityas; may they urge us at dawn, as Uṣas drives away the dark nights with her ruddy lights.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

ते (*te*)—those same Maruts; दशग्वाः (*daśagvāḥ*)—having taken the form of the Aṅgirases who attained success in ten months; प्रथमाः (*prathamāḥ*)—ready before the Ādityas; यज्ञमूहिरे (*yajñamūhire*)—carried out the sacrifice; ते (*te*)—those same Maruts; उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—of Uṣas; व्युष्टिषु (*vyuṣṭiṣu*)—at the time of her manifestation; नः (*naḥ*)—us; हिन्वंतु (*hinvaṃtu*)—may they urge on; रामिाः (*rāmiāḥ*) [as printed]—the dark-coloured nights; उषाः (*uṣāḥ*)—Uṣas; अरुणैः (*aruṇaiḥ*)—with attractive lights; अपोर्णुते न (*aporṇute na*)—as she drives away and destroys (so also the Maruts); महः (*mahaḥ*)—great; शुचता (*śucatā*)—shining; गोअर्णसा (*goarṇasā*)—drawing up the water in the form of mist; ज्योतिषा (*jyotiṣā*)—with the light called the Sun (they destroy the darkness).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Those same Maruts, having taken the form of the Aṅgirases who attained success in ten months, were ready before the Ādityas and carried out the sacrifice. May those same Maruts urge us at the time of the manifestation of Uṣas. Uṣas drives away the dark-coloured nights with her attractive

### Printed p. 251

lights, pushing them far away and destroying them, so the Maruts too destroy the darkness with their own radiance called the Sun, which is great, shining and drinks up the water in the form of mist.

**English Translation (as printed)**

May they, who, the first celebrators of the tenmonths' [sic] rite, accomplished this sacrifice, reanimate us at the rising dawn ; for as the dawn with purple rays drives away the night, so (do they scatter the darkness) with great, and pure. and [sic] mist-dispelling radiance.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

> ते दशग्वाः प्रथमाः यज्ञमूहिरे - मरुतः ये दशभिः मासैः सिद्धिंगताः
> अंगिरसः तद्रूपा भूत्वा आदित्येभ्यः प्रथमभाविनः संतः यज्ञमवहन् । आदित्यानां
> अंगिरसां च स्वर्गगमनं प्रति स्पर्धमानानां मध्यॆ पूर्वमेवांगिरसो यागा-
> ननुष्ठाय स्वर्गं प्राप्ताः ।

> *te daśagvāḥ prathamāḥ yajñamūhire - marutaḥ ye daśabhiḥ māsaiḥ siddhiṃgatāḥ*
> *aṃgirasaḥ tadrūpā bhūtvā ādityebhyaḥ prathamabhāvinaḥ saṃtaḥ yajñamavahan | ādityānāṃ*
> *aṃgirasāṃ ca svargagamanaṃ prati spardhamānānāṃ madhyè pūrvamevāṃgiraso yāgā-*
> *nanuṣṭhāya svargaṃ prāptāḥ |*

It is explained: the Maruts, having taken the form of the Aṅgirases who attained success in ten months only, were present before the Ādityas and carried out the sacrifice. A contest arose between the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases, at one time, as to who should reach heaven first; the Aṅgirases performed the sacrifice first and attained heaven before the Ādityas. This story is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 1-16): “आदित्याश्चैवेहासन्नंगिरसश्च तेऽग्रॆग्निनाग्निमयजंत” (*“ādityāścaivehāsannaṃgirasaśca te 'grègnināgnimayajaṃta”*). Sāyaṇa describes the Maruts as having the identity of the Aṅgirases who attained success in ten months, as born and established before the Ādityas, and as performing sacrifices. The inquiry into this identity of the Aṅgirases and the Maruts has been explained in the earlier volumes.

> ते उषसः व्युष्टिषु नः हिन्वंतु तादृशाः ते मरुतः प्रभातेषु सत्सु अस्मान्
> प्रेरयॆंतु ।

> *te uṣasaḥ vyuṣṭiṣu naḥ hinvaṃtu tādṛśāḥ te marutaḥ prabhāteṣu satsu asmān*
> *prerayèṃtu |*

It is said: those same Maruts, when the dawns have broken, may urge us on; that is, may the Maruts, of abundant power, urge us, the sacrificers, to our necessary duties after the time of dawn has passed, that is, in the morning.

> रामाः उषाः न अरुणैः अपोर्णुते महः शुचता गोअर्णसा ज्योतिषा—
> कृष्णवर्णाः राश्रीः उषाः यथा आरोचमानैः स्वतेजोभिः अपसारयति कथा
> महता दीप्यमानेन गच्छदुदकेन सूर्याख्येन तमः निवारयंति । सूर्यमंडल-
> मावृण्वतो वृत्रादीन् हत्वा सर्वं जगत् प्रकाशयंति ।

> *rāmāḥ uṣāḥ na aruṇaiḥ aporṇute mahaḥ śucatā goarṇasā jyotiṣā—*
> *kṛṣṇavarṇāḥ rāśrīḥ uṣāḥ yathā ārocamānaiḥ svatejobhiḥ apasārayati kathā*
> *mahatā dīpyamānena gacchadudakena sūryākhyena tamaḥ nivārayaṃti | sūryamaṃḍala-*
> *māvṛṇvato vṛtrādīn hatvā sarvaṃ jagat prakāśayaṃti |*

(The first word of this gloss is printed रामाः (*rāmāḥ*) in the supplied text, where रामीः (*rāmīḥ*) would be expected from the Saṃhitā; given as supplied.) It is described: as Uṣas drives away the night, black with darkness, with her well-shining lights, so the Maruts, filled with water, cover the sun, kill Vṛtra and the others who make darkness, break up the cloud that prevents the sun's light

### Printed p. 252

from reaching the world, and make light for the world. So it is described.

#### Ṛk 13

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ते क्षो॒णीभि॑ररु॒णेभि॒र्नांजिभी॑ रु॒द्रा ऋ॒तस्य॒ सद॑नेषु वावृधुः ।
> नि॒मेघ॑माना॒ अत्ये॑न॒ पाज॑सा सुश्चं॒द्रं वर्ण०॑ दधिरे सु॒पेश॑सं ॥१३॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ते । क्षोणीभिः । अरुणेभिः । न । अंजिभिः । रुद्राः । ऋतस्य । सदनेषु । ववृधुः ।
> निमेघमानाः । अत्येन । पाजसा । सुचंद्रं । वर्णं । दधिरे । सुपेशसं ॥ १३ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> रुद्रा रुद्रपुत्रास्ते मरुतः क्षोणीभिः शब्दकारिभिर्विर्णाख्यैर्विणाविशेषैर-
> रुणेभिर्नांजभिः ॥ नशब्दः समुच्चये ॥ आरोचमानैररुणवर्णैर्वा रूपाभिव्यंज-
> कैरलंकारैश्च समन्विताः संत ऋतस्योदकस्य सदनेषु निवासभूतेषु मेघेषु
> वावृधुः । वर्धंते । अपि च अत्येन सततगामिना शीघ्रं व्याप्नुवता पाजसात्मीयेन
> बलेन निमेघमाना नितरां मेघादुदकं चिंतयंतस्ते सुचंद्रं शोभनाह्लादनं
> सुपेशसं ॥ पेश इति रूपनाम ॥ शोभनरूपं वर्णं दधिरे । कांतिं धारयंति ॥

> *rudrā rudraputrāste marutaḥ kṣoṇībhiḥ śabdakāribhirvirṇākhyairviṇāviśeṣaira-*
> *ruṇebhirnāṃjabhiḥ ‖ naśabdaḥ samuccaye ‖ ārocamānairaruṇavarṇairvā rūpābhivyaṃja-*
> *kairalaṃkāraiśca samanvitāḥ saṃta ṛtasyodakasya sadaneṣu nivāsabhūteṣu megheṣu*
> *vāvṛdhuḥ | vardhaṃte | api ca atyena satatagāminā śīghraṃ vyāpnuvatā pājasātmīyena*
> *balena nimeghamānā nitarāṃ meghādudakaṃ ciṃtayaṃtaste sucaṃdraṃ śobhanāhlādanaṃ*
> *supeśasaṃ ‖ peśa iti rūpanāma ‖ śobhanarūpaṃ varṇaṃ dadhire | kāṃtiṃ dhārayaṃti ‖*

Gist: The Maruts, sons of Rudra, equipped with sounding lutes and red ornaments, grow in the clouds, the abodes of water, and take on a fair, lovely colour.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

रुद्राः (*rudrāḥ*)—the Maruts, sons of Rudra; ते (*te*)—they; क्षोणीभिः (*kṣoṇībhiḥ*)—provided with lutes having charming sounds; अरुणेभिर्न (*aruṇebhirna*)—like the red colour; अंजिभिः (*aṃjibhiḥ*)—adorned with ornaments; ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of water; सदनेषु (*sadaneṣu*)—in the clouds that are its abodes; वावृधुः (*vāvṛdhuḥ*)—they grow; अत्येन (*atyena*)—swift-going; पाजसा (*pājasā*)—with their own strength; निमेघमानाः (*nimeghamānāḥ*)—squeezing the water out of the cloud; सुश्चंद्रं (*suścaṃdraṃ*)—delightful; सुपेशसं (*supeśasaṃ*)—showing an attractive form; वर्णं (*varṇaṃ*)—the lustre; दधिरे (*dadhire*)—they obtain.

### Printed p. 253

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The Maruts, sons of Rudra, provided with lutes of charming sounds and adorned with ornaments like the red colour, grow in the clouds, the abodes of water. Squeezing the water of the cloud by their swift strength, they possess a lustre that is delightful and shows an attractive form.

**English Translation (as printed)**

They, the Rudras (equipped) with melodious (lutes), and decorated with purple ornaments, exalt in the dwellings of the waters ; and scattering the clouds with rapid vigour, they are endowed with delightful and beautiful forms.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

> रुद्राः—रुद्रपुत्राः

> *rudrāḥ—rudraputrāḥ*

The word रुद्र (*rudra*) is explained as "children of Rudra"; the Maruts, sons of Rudra,

> क्षोणीभिः—शब्दकारीभिः विणाख्यैः वीणावीशेषैः ।

> *kṣoṇībhiḥ—śabdakārībhiḥ viṇākhyaiḥ vīṇāvīśeṣaiḥ |*

are provided with sounding lutes called वाणि (*vāṇi*) (Sāyaṇa's gloss has विणाख्यैः (*viṇākhyaiḥ*), as supplied).  And

> अरुणेभिः नांजिभिः—अरुण
> वर्णैः ना रूपाभिव्यंजकैरलंकारैश्च समन्विताः ।

> *aruṇebhiḥ nāṃjibhiḥ—aruṇa*
> *varṇaiḥ nā rūpābhivyaṃjakairalaṃkāraiśca samanvitāḥ |*

they are endowed with a red colour of great brightness, or with ornaments that bring out (make beautiful) the form (shape), and so they grow in the middle of the clouds. Again,

> अत्येन पाजसा
> निमेघमानाः सुश्चंद्रं सुपेशसं वर्ण० दधिरे—शीघ्रं व्याप्नुवता आत्मीयेन
> बलेन मेघादुदकं नितरां चितयंतः शोभनाह्लादनं शोभनरूपं कांतिं धार
> यंति ।

> *atyena pājasā*
> *nimeghamānāḥ suścaṃdraṃ supeśasaṃ varṇa0 dadhire—śīghraṃ vyāpnuvatā ātmīyena*
> *balena meghādudakaṃ nitarāṃ citayaṃtaḥ śobhanāhlādanaṃ śobhanarūpaṃ kāṃtiṃ dhāra*
> *yaṃti |*

the Maruts, with their (powerful) strength that quickly spreads, make the rain-water pour from the clouds without remaining at all (completely); they are very delightful and bear a form of beautiful shape. So it is explained.

> सुपेशसं— पेश इति रूपनाम ।

> *supeśasaṃ— peśa iti rūpanāma |*

The word पेशसं (*peśasaṃ*) is given among the names of form (Ni. 3-13) and among the names of gold, and is explained: पेश इति रूपनाम पिंशतेर्विपिशितं भवति (*peśa iti rūpanāma piṃśatervipiśitaṃ bhavati*) (Ni. 8-12).

#### Ṛk 14

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ता इ॑या॒नो महि॒ वरू॑थमू॒तय॒ उप॒ फेदे॒ना नम॑सा
> गृणीमसि ।
> त्रि॒तो न यान्पंच॒ होत्था॑न॒भिष्ट॑य आव॒नवर्त॒दव॑राञ्च॒क्रियाव॑से ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तान् । इयानः । महि । वरूथं । ऊतये । उप । घ । इत् । एना । नमसा ।
> गृणेमसि ।
> त्रितः । न । यान् । पंच । होत्यन् । अभिष्टये । आववर्तत् । अवरान् । चक्रिया ।
> अवसे ॥ १४ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> तान् मरुतो महि महद्वरूथं वरणीयं प्रशस्तं धनं तन्मरुत ऊतये
> रक्षणार्थमियान इयाना याचमाना वयं ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति जसः सुः ॥ एनानेन
> नमसा नमस्कारेण स्तोत्रेण वोपेत् उपेत्य गृणीमसि । स्तुमः ॥ घेति पादपू-
> रणः । एनेत्यत्र सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयाया आजादेशः । नशब्दः समुच्चये ॥ त्रित
> ऋषिश्च यानेतान् मरुतः पंच होत्थन् अध्यात्मप्राणापानादिपंचवृत्तात्मना
> वर्तमानान् अत एव होमनिष्पादकान् अवरान् मुख्यानभिष्टयेऽभिलषितसिद्ध्यर्थं
> चक्रिया नाभिचक्रेणावसेऽवितुं संगंतुमाववर्तत् । स्वस्मान्निर्जिगमिषून्प्राणान्
> स्वात्माभिमुखमावर्तयत् । यद्वा चक्रिया ऋष्टाख्येनायुधेन युक्तान् अवसे
> स्तुत्यादिभिस्तर्पयितुमावर्तयत् । तान् स्तुम इति संबंधः ॥ ववर्तदिति वृतेर्ण्यं-
> ताल्लुजि चङि रूपं ॥

> *tān maruto mahi mahadvarūthaṃ varaṇīyaṃ praśastaṃ dhanaṃ tanmaruta ūtaye*
> *rakṣaṇārthamiyāna iyānā yācamānā vayaṃ ‖ supāṃ sulugiti jasaḥ suḥ ‖ enānena*
> *namasā namaskāreṇa stotreṇa vopet upetya gṛṇīmasi | stumaḥ ‖ gheti pādapū-*
> *raṇaḥ | enetyatra supāṃ sulugiti tṛtīyāyā ājādeśaḥ | naśabdaḥ samuccaye ‖ trita*
> *ṛṣiśca yānetān marutaḥ paṃca hotthan adhyātmaprāṇāpānādipaṃcavṛttātmanā*
> *vartamānān ata eva homaniṣpādakān avarān mukhyānabhiṣṭaye 'bhilaṣitasiddhyarthaṃ*
> *cakriyā nābhicakreṇāvase 'vituṃ saṃgaṃtumāvavartat | svasmānnirjigamiṣūnprāṇān*
> *svātmābhimukhamāvartayat | yadvā cakriyā ṛṣṭākhyenāyudhena yuktān avase*
> *stutyādibhistarpayitumāvartayat | tān stuma iti saṃbaṃdhaḥ ‖ vavartaditi vṛterṇyaṃ-*
> *tālluji caṅi rūpaṃ ‖*

Gist: We, imploring the Maruts for ample, choice wealth for protection, approach and praise them with this homage; Trita turned the five Maruts towards himself.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

न (*na*)—and; पंच (*paṃca*)—five in number, as prāṇa, apāna and the rest; यान् (*yān*)—which Maruts; अवरान् (*avarān*)—very chief; होत्यन् (*hotyan*)—as priests (for the sacrifice); अभिष्टये (*abhiṣṭaye*)—for the accomplishment of his desired end; चक्रिया (*cakriyā*)—with their weapons; अवसे (*avase*)—for protecting himself;

### Printed p. 255

त्रितः (*tritaḥ*)—Trita; अववर्तत् (*avavartat*)—whom he prayed not to go out and held back in himself; तान् (*tān*)—those Maruts; मही (*mahi*)—great; वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*)—and praiseworthy wealth; ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection; इयानः (*iyānaḥ*)—we who pray; एना नमसा (*enā namasā*)—with this praise accompanied by homage; उप इत् (*upa it*)—approaching; गृणीमसि (*gṛṇīmasi*)—we praise.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

We who pray for great and praiseworthy wealth for protection approach with this praise accompanied by homage, and praise those Maruts — the five, prāṇa, apāna and the rest, whom Trita, for the accomplishment of his desired end, as very chief priests of the sacrifice, and for protecting himself with their weapons, prayed not to go out and held back within himself.

**English Translation (as printed)**

Imploring them for ample wealth, and (having recourse to him) for protection, we glorify them with this praise ; like the five chief priests whom Trita detained for the (performance of) the sacrifice, and to protect it with their weapons.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

> त्रितः यान् पंच होत्यन् अपर्रा अभिष्टये चक्रिया अवसे आववर्तत्-त्रित
> ऋषिः एतान् मरुतः अध्यात्मप्राणापानादिपंचवृत्तात्मना वर्तमानान् आत एव
> होमनिष्पादकान् मुख्यान् अभिलषितसिद्ध्यर्थं, नाभिचक्रेण अनितुं संगंतुं स्वस्मा
> न्निर्जिगमिषून् प्राणान् स्वात्माभिमुखमावर्तयत् । यद्वा चक्रिया ऋष्टाख्येना
> युधेन युक्तान् स्तुत्यादिभिः तर्पयितुं आवर्तयत् !

> *tritaḥ yān paṃca hotyan aparrā abhiṣṭaye cakriyā avase āvavartat-trita*
> *ṛṣiḥ etān marutaḥ adhyātmaprāṇāpānādipaṃcavṛttātmanā vartamānān āta eva*
> *homaniṣpādakān mukhyān abhilaṣitasiddhyarthaṃ, nābhicakreṇa anituṃ saṃgaṃtuṃ svasmā*
> *nnirjigamiṣūn prāṇān svātmābhimukhamāvartayat | yadvā cakriyā ṛṣṭākhyenā*
> *yudhena yuktān stutyādibhiḥ tarpayituṃ āvartayat !*

Here the word पंचहोत्यन् (*paṃcahotyan*) is used in the sense that in this body the Maruts (the winds), bearing the names prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna and samāna, dwell doing their respective functions in keeping with the body, as the maintainers of the state of the self. By this it is indicated that they are the chief means by which the worship of the bodily Vaiśvānara fire is accomplished. Since their seat is in the heart as prāṇa, in the anal region as apāna, and in the navel as samāna, the sage Trita held these Maruts, who were eager to go out of the body, in the Svādhiṣṭhāna wheel in the navel, and made them face himself; and it is said that by this Trita's protection came about, and that these Maruts are chief in bringing about all desired ends and the meditation that takes the form of worship of the self; and also that in the sacrifices performed in the world by the sacrificers, the Marut deities, receiving the oblations, are chief in accomplishing the sacrificers' desires.

### Printed p. 256

The Marut deities' accomplishing of the oblation is described in two ways, and their chief place in fulfilment of desires in three ways. In the second sense, the Maruts bear a spear-weapon named ṛṣṭi; and for protecting the sacrificers, or those who praise them, the sage Trita turned them back so that they should be in his navel-wheel, in order to please the Maruts with praise and the like. So it is explained.

> तान् महि वरूथं ऊतये इयानः उप इत् गृणीमसि—मरुतः महत्
> प्रशस्तं धनं तत्! मरुतः रक्षणार्थं यजमानाः वयं अनेन नमस्कारेण
> स्तोत्रेण वा उपेत्य स्तुमः

> *tān mahi varūthaṃ ūtaye iyānaḥ upa it gṛṇīmasi—marutaḥ mahat*
> *praśastaṃ dhanaṃ tat! marutaḥ rakṣaṇārthaṃ yajamānāḥ vayaṃ anena namaskāreṇa*
> *stotreṇa vā upetya stumaḥ*

Thus it is described: we sacrificers, praying to the Marut deities for obtaining the wealth that can necessarily be had for our protection, and for protecting us, will worship them with homage or with praises.

The word वरूथ (*varūtha*) is mentioned by Yāska among the names of houses (Ni. 3 13). Here Sāyaṇa gives the sense "choice" and explains it as praiseworthy wealth. In त्रितः न (*tritaḥ na*) he states that the word न is used in the sense of conjunction (नशब्दः समुच्चये (*naśabdaḥ samuccaye*)).

#### Ṛk 15

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यया॑ र॒ध्रं पा॒रय॒थात्यंहो॒ यया॑ नि॒दो मुं॒चथ॒॑॑
> वंदितारं ।
> अ॒र्वाची॒ सा म॑रुतो॒ या व॑ ऊ॒तिरो षु वा॒श्रेव॑ सुम॒तिर्जि॑-
> गातु ॥ १५ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यया । रध्रं । पारयथ । अति । अंहः । यया । निदः । मुंचथ । वंदितारं ।
> अर्वाची । सा । मरुतः । या । वः । ऊतिः । ओ इति । सु । वाश्राइव । सुमतिः ।
> जिगातु ॥ १५ ॥

> *yayā | radhraṃ | pārayatha | ati | aṃhaḥ | yayā | nidaḥ | muṃcatha | vaṃditāraṃ |*
> *arvācī | sā | marutaḥ | yā | vaḥ | ūtiḥ | o iti | su | vāśrāiva | sumatiḥ |*
> *jigātu ‖ 15 ‖*

### Printed p. 257

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 21, p. 257.*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतो ययोत्या रध्रमाराधकं यजमानमंहः पापमति पारयथ।
> अतिक्रमयथ । ययोत्या वंदितारं स्तोतारं निदो निंदितुः शत्रोः सकाशान्मुं-
> चथ । मोचयथ । हे मरुतो वो युष्मदीया योतिः सर्वाच्यस्मदभिमुखा
> भवतु । तथा सुमतिर्युष्मदीया शोभना मतिरनुग्रहात्मिका बुद्धिश्च वाश्रेव
> हंभारवं कुर्वती धेनुरिव वत्सं सुष्टु ओ जिगातु । एवं गच्छतु । आस्मान् प्रति
> सर्वथागच्छत्व्यर्थः ॥

> *he maruto yayotyā radhramārādhakaṃ yajamānamaṃhaḥ pāpamati pārayatha|*
> *atikramayatha | yayotyā vaṃditāraṃ stotāraṃ nido niṃdituḥ śatroḥ sakāśānmuṃ-*
> *catha | mocayatha | he maruto vo yuṣmadīyā yotiḥ sarvācyasmadabhimukhā*
> *bhavatu | tathā sumatiryuṣmadīyā śobhanā matiranugrahātmikā buddhiśca vāśreva*
> *haṃbhāravaṃ kurvatī dhenuriva vatsaṃ suṣṭu o jigātu | evaṃ gacchatu | āsmān prati*
> *sarvathāgacchatvyarthaḥ ‖*

Gist: O Maruts, may the protection by which you carry the worshipper over sin and free the praiser from the reviler, and your gracious thought, like a cow lowing to her calf, come towards us.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

Marutaḥ—O Maruts; yayā—by which protection; radhram—the worshipping sacrificer; aṃhaḥ—from sin; ati pārayatha—you carried over; yayā—by which protection; vaṃditāram—the devotee who praises you; nidaḥ—from the reviling enemy; muṃcatha—you released; vaḥ—your; yā ūtiḥ—that well-known protection which is yours; sā—that; arvācī—may it be turned towards us; vāśreva—as a cow, making her sound of affection, goes to and joins her calf; sumatiḥ—your gracious thought also; su—exceedingly; o jigātu—may it come towards us.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Maruts, by whatever protection you carried the worshipping sacrificer across sin, and by whatever protection you freed the devotee who praises you from the reviling enemy, may that same protection be turned towards us also. As a cow, making her sound of affection, goes to her calf, may your gracious thought also spread exceedingly towards us.

**English Translation (as printed)**

Maruts, may that protection wherewith you convey the worshipper beyond sin, wherewith you rescue thc [sic] reciter of your praise from the scoffer, be present with us: may your benign disposition tend towards us, like a loving (cow towards her calf).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

> यया ऊत्या रध्रं अंहतः अति पारयथ, वंदितारं निदः मुंचथ वः सा
> आर्वाची—अराधकं यजमानं पापमतिक्रमयथ स्तोतारं निंदितुः शत्पोः
> सकाशात् मोचयथ युष्मदीया सा ऊतिः अस्मदभिमुखा भवतु ।

> *yayā ūtyā radhraṃ aṃhataḥ ati pārayatha, vaṃditāraṃ nidaḥ muṃcatha vaḥ sā*
> *ārvācī—arādhakaṃ yajamānaṃ pāpamatikramayatha stotāraṃ niṃdituḥ śatpoḥ*
> *sakāśāt mocayatha yuṣmadīyā sā ūtiḥ asmadabhimukhā bhavatu |*

Explained thus: the Maruts carry the worshipping sacrificer across sins; they free the praiser from the reviling enemy; may that protection of yours be turned towards us. The Marut deities are said to possess a manner of protection that carries across sins the sacrificer who serves them, and

### Printed p. 258

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 35, p. 258.*

that destroys the enemies who revile and injure those who praise them, and protects the latter. So the power of protection belonging to the Maruts is to be turned towards the sacrificers; thus the sacrificers' prayer is described.

> सुमतिः वाश्रेव सुष्टु ओजिगातु - युष्मदीया शोभना मतिः अनुग्रहात्मिका
> बुद्धिश्च हंभारवं कुर्वती धेनुरिव वत्समिव गच्छतु

> *sumatiḥ vāśreva suṣṭu ojigātu - yuṣmadīyā śobhanā matiḥ anugrahātmikā*
> *buddhiśca haṃbhāravaṃ kurvatī dhenuriva vatsamiva gacchatu*

The thought of the Marut deities, which protects others or bestows favour, is to be well disposed towards us sacrificers, as a milch cow approaches her calf with a lowing sound. So it is prayed.

## Sūkta 35 (Maṇḍala 2)

*The thirty-fifth sūkta.*

**Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta** (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

> उपेमिति पंचदशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं गार्त्समदं त्रैष्टुभमपांनपाद्दे-
> वताकं । > तथा चानुक्रांतं । उपेमपोनप्रीयमिति ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

*Gist:* the third sūkta of the fourth anuvāka, of fifteen ṛks, of the Gārtsamada seer, in *triṣṭubh*, for Apāṃ Napāt; the Anukramaṇī is quoted; the use of the sūkta is by the Liṅga (indication).

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta beginning उपेमसृक्षि (*upemasṛkṣi*) [as supplied] is the third sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has fifteen ṛks. Gṛtsamada is the seer; Apāṃ Napāt is the deity; the metre is *triṣṭubh*. The Anukramaṇikā says: उपेमपोनप्रीयमिति (*upemaponaprīyamiti*) [as supplied]. The use (viniyoga) is *laiṅgika* (by indication).

**Sūkta 35** — Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 35; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Vargas 22, 23, 24. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 15. Seer: Gṛtsamada (the label is printed as "यमः" for ऋषिः). Deity: Apāṃ Napāt (printed "अपांसपात्" [sic]). Metre: *triṣṭubh*.

> *vājayurvājamannamātmana icchanna hamīmenāṃ vacasyāṃ vacasaḥ stotrasye-*

> *eṣoSgnirjāyata iti tatpautratvaṃ | etatsaṃjñako devo giraḥ | gṛṇātīti gīḥ stotā|*
> *tasya me mama kuvit | bahunāmaitat | bahulaṃ canoSnnaṃ dadhīta | dadhātu |*
> *vidadhātu | prayacchṛtvityarthaḥ | api cāsmān supeśasaḥ śobhanarūpān śobhanālaṃkā-*
> *rānvā karati | karotu ‖ karotervyatyayena śap | kaḥkaratkaratikṛdhikṛteṣvanaditeḥ |*

Gist: wishing for food, I produce this praise for Apāṃ Napāt (Agni, the grandson of the waters), who hears praises; may he give me abundant food and make us well-formed.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

Vājayuḥ—I, who desire food; īṃ vacasyām—this praise; upa asṛkṣi—I produce [as supplied: "ನಿರ್ಮಿಸುತ್ತೇನೆ"]; hi—because; saḥ—Agni (Agni in the form of Apāṃ Napāt); joṣiṣat—enjoys the praises; nādyaḥ—belonging to the sounding waters of the clouds; āśuhemā—swift-moving; apāṃ napāt—the one who is the grandson of the waters, that Agni; giraḥ—of the praiser; me—to me; kuvit—abundantly [as supplied: "ಪ್ರಭೂತವಾಗ", the final letter apparently lost]; canaḥ—food; dadhīta—may he provide; supeśaḥ—having a beautiful form; karati—may he make (us).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Agni, famous as Apāṃ Napāt, enjoys praise with affection. Therefore I, desiring food, produce this praise. He who belongs to the sounding waters,

### Printed p. 260

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 35, p. 260.*

swift-moving, the grandson of the waters, may that Agni provide abundant food to me, his praiser.

**Printed English translation**

Desiring food, I put forth this laudatory hymn: may the sounding and swift-moving grandson of the waters bestow abundant food upon me his worshipper : may he make us of goodly appearance, for verily he is propitiated by praise.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

> वाजयुः ईं वचस्यां उप आसृक्षि—अन्नमात्मन इच्छन्नहं एनां स्तोत्र-
> स्येच्छां उत्पादयामि । अपां नपातं स्तोतुं प्रवृत्तः अस्मि ।

> *vājayuḥ īṃ vacasyāṃ upa āsṛkṣi—annamātmana icchannahaṃ enāṃ stotra-*
> *syecchāṃ utpādayāmi | apāṃ napātaṃ stotuṃ pravṛttaḥ asmi |*

The seer of the mantra says that, desiring to obtain food, he will praise the deity named Apāṃ Napāt, who bestows food upon him.

> स च नाद्यः आशुहेमा अपां नपात्—सः शब्दकारिणीनां मेघस्थानामपां
> संबंधी, शीघ्रंगंता, अपां पौत्रस्थानीयः अद्भ्य ओषधिवनस्पतयो जायंते
> ओषधिवनस्पतिभ्यो एष अग्निः जायते इति तत्पौत्रत्वं ।

> *sa ca nādyaḥ āśuhemā apāṃ napāt—saḥ śabdakāriṇīnāṃ meghasthānāmapāṃ*
> *saṃbaṃdhī, śīghraṃgaṃtā, apāṃ pautrasthānīyaḥ adbhya oṣadhivanaspatayo jāyaṃte*
> *oṣadhivanaspatibhyo eṣa agniḥ jāyate iti tatpautratvaṃ |*

This deity Apāṃ Napāt is connected with the waters in the sounding clouds that are filled with water; that is, he is the son's son of the waters. For this reason the deity has received the name Apāṃ Napāt. Plants and trees arise from the waters, and Agni arises from these plants and trees; so Agni is regarded as the grandson of the waters; thus it is explained.

In explaining the word अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) the Nirukta authors say अपांनपात् (*apāṃnapāt*) is explained like तनूनप्रा (*tanūnaprā*) व्याख्यातः (*vyākhyātaḥ*) (Ni. 10-18) [as supplied]. The word तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) is explained in two senses: अज्यमिति कात्थक्यः अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः (*ajyamiti kātthakyaḥ agniriti śākapūṇiḥ*) (Ni. 8-5) [as supplied]. Following the view of the teacher Śākapūṇi, the meaning of तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*), namely Agni, is taken over by the word अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*); thus it is explained.

> गिरः मे कुवित् चनः दधीत—एतत्संज्ञको देवः। गृणातीति गीर् स्तोता। तस्य
> बहुलं अन्नं विदधातु ।

> *giraḥ me kuvit canaḥ dadhīta—etatsaṃjñako devaḥ| gṛṇātīti gīr stotā| tasya*
> *bahulaṃ annaṃ vidadhātu |*

The word गिरः (*giraḥ*), formed from the root गृ (*gṛ*) meaning "to utter words", is used in the sense of one who recites stanzas (the praiser). And it is prayed that this deity Apāṃ Napāt bestow abundant food on the one who praises him.

### Printed p. 261

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 22, p. 261.*

> जोषिषत् सुपेशसः करति—अस्मान् शोभनरूपान् शोभनालंकारान् वा
> करोतु । अयं देवः स्तोत्राणि सेवते तस्मादस्मानेवमनुगृह्णातु ।

> *joṣiṣat supeśasaḥ karati—asmān śobhanarūpān śobhanālaṃkārān vā*
> *karotu | ayaṃ devaḥ stotrāṇi sevate tasmādasmānevamanugṛhṇātu |*

The word जोषिषत् (*joṣiṣat*) is used in the sense of one who hears the praises and is pleased; therefore it is prayed that this deity make us, who recite the praises, possessed of an excellent form or of auspicious ornaments.

The word जनक (*janaka*) [as supplied] is cited by Yāska in the verse:

> अद्धीदिंद्र प्रस्थितेमा हवींषि चनो दधिष्ट पचतोत सोमं ।
> प्रयस्वंतः प्रति हर्यामसि त्वा सत्याः संतु यजमानस्य कामाः ॥

> *addhīdiṃdra prasthitemā havīṃṣi cano dadhiṣṭa pacatota somaṃ |*
> *prayasvaṃtaḥ prati haryāmasi tvā satyāḥ saṃtu yajamānasya kāmāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-116-8)

On this verse it is explained: चन इत्यन्न नाम (*cana ityanna nāma*) (Ni. 6-16) [as supplied], "caná is a name of food". The word कुवित् (*kuvit*) is included among the many-names (Ni. 3-13). Here the meaning बहुलं (*bahulaṃ*) is given.

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> इ॒मं स्व॑स्मै हृ॒द आ सुत॑ष्टं॒ मंत्रं॑ वोचेम कु॒विद॑स्य॒ वेद॑त् ।
> अ॒पां नपा॑दसु॒र्य॑स्य म॒ह्ना विश्वा॑न्य॒र्यो भुव॑ना जजान ॥ २ ॥

> *imaṃ svasmai hṛda ā sutaṣṭaṃ maṃtraṃ vocema kuvidasya vedat |*
> *apāṃ napādasuryasya mahnā viśvānyaryo bhuvanā jajāna ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अपां । नपात् । असुर्यस्य । मह्ना । विश्वानि । अर्यः । भुवना । जजान ॥ २ ॥

> *imaṃ | su | asmai | hṛdaḥ | ā | sutaṣṭaṃ | maṃtraṃ | vocema | kuvit | asya | vedat |*
> *apāṃ | napāt | asuryasya | mahnā | viśvāni | aryaḥ | bhuvanā | jajāna ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अस्मा अपांनपात्संज्ञकाय देवाय हृदो, हृदयात् सुतष्टं सुष्टु
> निर्मितमिमं मंत्रं सुष्टु आभिमुख्येन वोचेम । ब्रवाम । आस्यास्माभिरुक्त-
> मिमं मंत्रं कुविद्वेदत् । बहुलं जानातु ॥ वेत्तेर्लॆट्यडागमः । निपातैर्य-
> द्यदिहंतेति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥ किं स्तोत्रमिति चेदुच्यते । आर्यः स्वाम्यपांनपा

*Gist:* We address to Apāṃ Napāt this well-made hymn from the heart; may he fully know it. [The bhāṣya continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 262

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 35, p. 262.*

> त्संज्ञको वैद्युतोऽग्निरसुर्यस्य । असुरः शत्रून् क्षेप्ता । तस्य स्वभूतस्य बलस्य
> मह्ना महिम्ना महत्वेन विश्वानि सर्वाणि भुवना भुवनानि वृष्ट्युदकानि वृष्टु-
> त्पादनेन भूतजातानि वा जजान । जनयामास ॥

*Gist:* the lord, the lightning Agni called Apāṃ Napāt, whose strength hurls down enemies, by that might has produced all beings (or the rain-waters, by causing rain).

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अस्यै (*asyai*)—for offering to Agni, named Apāṃ Napāt; हृदः (*hṛdaḥ*)—from the heart (sincerely); सुतष्टं (*sutaṣṭaṃ*)—excellently fashioned; इमं मंत्रं (*imaṃ maṃtraṃ*)—this mantra, which is of the nature of praise; सु (*su*)—exceedingly; आ वोचेम (*ā vocema*)—we recite, standing facing him; अस्य (*asya*)—this mantra; कुवित् (*kuvit*)—fully; वेदत् (*vedat*)—may (Agni) know; आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)—the lord; अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*)—Agni named Apāṃ Napāt; असुरस्य (*asurasya*)—of his strength, which defeats enemies; मह्ना (*mahnā*)—by the greatness; विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all; भुवना (*bhuvanā*)—beings; जजान (*jajāna*)—created.

*॥ ಭಾನುವಾರ ॥* (printed between the Pratipadārtha and the Bhāvārtha, apparently "Sunday"; no explanation is given in the supplied text.)

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

I recite this mantra, sincerely and excellently composed and of the nature of praise, standing before Agni, in order to offer it to him. May Agni know this mantra fully. Agni, the lord, named Apāṃ Napāt, by the greatness of his strength that defeats enemies, created all beings.

**Printed English translation**

Let us address to him the prayer that is conceived in our hearts, and may he fully understand (its purport); for he the lord, the grandson of the waters, has generated all beings by the greatness of his might.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

> आर्यः असुर्यस्य मह्ना विश्वानि भुवना जजान—स्वामी अपां नपात्संज्ञ-
> को वैद्युतोग्निः असुरः शत्रुन् क्षेप्ता । तस्य स्वभूतस्य बलस्य महत्वेन सर्वाणि
> वृष्टु दकानि वृष्टुत्पादनेन भूतजातानि वा जनयामास ।

> *āryaḥ asuryasya mahnā viśvāni bhuvanā jajāna—svāmī apāṃ napātsaṃjña-*
> *ko vaidyutogniḥ asuraḥ śatrun kṣeptā | tasya svabhūtasya balasya mahatvena sarvāṇi*
> *vṛṣṭu dakāni vṛṣṭutpādanena bhūtajātāni vā janayāmāsa |*

The word आर्य (*ārya*) is stated among the names of the lord (Ni. 3-11). The word अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) is explained as the lightning Agni. This Agni is the master of all and destroys enemies. Therefore this deity, by the greatness of his natural might, creates the rain-waters, and by those rain-waters creates all living beings; thus it is explained.

### Printed p. 263

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 22] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 263.*

> अस्मै हृदं सुतष्टं इमं मंत्रं आ वोचेम—अपां नपात्संज्ञकाय
> देवाय हृदयात् सुष्टु निर्मितं इमं मंत्रं सुष्टु अभिमुख्येन ब्रवाम ।

> *asmai hṛdaṃ sutaṣṭaṃ imaṃ maṃtraṃ ā vocema—apāṃ napātsaṃjñakāya*
> *devāya hṛdayāt suṣṭu nirmitaṃ imaṃ maṃtraṃ suṣṭu abhimukhyena bravāma |*

Here the bhāṣya on Ṛk 2 is restated: for the deity named Apāṃ Napāt we recite, standing facing him, this mantra, well made from the heart, of the nature of praise, we the sacrificers, sincerely composed. अस्माभिरुक्तमिमं मंत्रं कुवित् वेदत्—बहुलं जानातु । (*asmābhiruktamimaṃ maṃtraṃ kuvit vedat—bahulaṃ jānātu |*) We the sacrificers have recited this hymn in order to please this deity; may the deity listen to it well: thus a prayer is stated. The discussion of the lightning Agni was given earlier.

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> सम॒न्या यंत्युप॑ यंत्य॒न्याः स॑मा॒नमू॒र्वं न॒द्यः॑ पृणंति ।
> तमू॒ शुचिं॒ शुच॑यो दीदि॒वांस॑म॒पां नपा॑तं॒ परि॑ तस्थु॒रापः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सं । अन्याः । यंति । उप । यंति । अन्याः । समानं । ऊर्वं । नद्यः । पृणंति ।
> तं । ऊं इति । शुचिं । शुचयः । दीदिऽवांसं । अपां । नपातं । परि । तस्थुः । आपः॥३॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अपोनप्रीये वसतीवरीसमीप एकधनासु प्राप्तासु समन्या यंतीत्येषा-
> नुवक्तव्या । सूत्रितं च । समन्या यंत्युपयंत्यन्या इति तीर्थदेशे । आ. ५-१. ।
> इति ॥ सारस्वते च शस्त्रे यद्यप्सु शम्या निपतेत् तदानीमपोनप्रीयश्चरुः कार्यः।
> तत्रेष्टैव याज्या । सूत्रितं च। समन्या यंत्युपयंत्यन्या इत्यातःसमानं सर्वॆषां।
> आ. १२-६. । इति ॥
> अन्या वर्ष्या आपो सं यंति । भूम्या संगच्छंते । अन्याश्च पूर्वं तत्राव-
> स्थिता उपयंति । उपगच्छंति । ताः सर्वा अपः समानं सह नद्यो नदीभूता
> ऊर्वं समुद्रमध्यॆ वर्तमानं वडवानलं पृणंति ॥ पृण प्रीणने तौदादिकः ॥
> तमु तमेवापां नपातं शुचिं निर्मलं दीदिवांसं दीप्यमानं ॥ दीदेतिश्कांदसो
> दीप्टिकर्मा । लिटः क्वसुः । वस्वेकाचाद्भसाविति नियमादिडभावः । छंदसि वेति वक्त-

*Gist:* the Apōnaptrīya rite and the Sārasvata śastra use this Ṛk (with Āśvalāyana sūtra references); the other waters join the rain-waters. [The bhāṣya continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 264

> व्यमिति वचनाद्द्विर्वचनाभावः ॥ एवंभूतं शुचयः शुद्धा आपः परितस्थुः । परिवृत्य

> वडवानलरूपेण वर्तमानं तं पर्युपासत इत्यर्थः । यद्वा अन्या एकधनाख्या
> आपः संयंति । चात्वालोत्करयोर्मध्यॆ वसतीवरीभिः संगच्छंते । अन्या वसती
> वर्याख्या अपश्चोपयंति । उपगच्छंति । ऐकमत्यं प्राप्ता भवंति । एताश्च मिलित्वा
> यज्ञं साधयंत्यस्तत्साध्यवृष्टिद्वारा नद्यो भूत्वोर्वं पृणंतीत्यादि समानं !
> एवं हि आपो ना अस्पर्धंत ः यं पूर्वं यज्ञं वक्ष्यामः । ऐ. ब्रा. २-२०. ।
> इत्यादिकं ब्राह्मणविनियोगश्चानुगृह्यते ॥

*Gist:* the waters, pure, surround the shining Apāṃ Napāt, the lightning fire in the cloud and the ocean fire; or, alternatively, the Ekadhanā and Vasatīvarī waters of the sacrifice unite and flow as rivers (Ai. Brā. 2-20).

*Stray line in the supplied text after the bhāṣya, kept as supplied:* । क्रि.श. १२९८ ॥ (*| kri.śa. 1298 ‖*) (no explanation is given).

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अन्याः (*anyāḥ*)—waters produced by rain; सं यंति (*saṃ yaṃti*)—together reach the earth; अन्याः (*anyāḥ*)—waters that were already on the earth; उप यंति (*upa yaṃti*)—join with these rain-waters; समानं (*samānaṃ*)—all these waters, gathering together; नद्यः (*nadyaḥ*)—in the form of rivers; ऊर्वं (*ūrvaṃ*)—the submarine fire in the midst of the ocean; पृणंति (*pṛṇaṃti*)—satisfy; शुचिं (*śuciṃ*)—the pure one; दीदिनांसं (*dīdināṃsaṃ*) (as supplied; the Pada has दीदिऽवांसं (*dīdi 'vāṃsaṃ*))—the shining one; तमु अपां नपातं (*tamu apāṃ napātaṃ*)—that same Agni named Apāṃ Napāt; शुचयः (*śucayaḥ*) pure; आपः (*āpaḥ*)—waters; परि तस्थुः (*pari tasthuḥ*)—stand around and attend upon.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Waters produced by rain gather together on the earth. The waters that were already on the earth join with these rain-waters. All these waters, gathering together, flow as rivers and satisfy the submarine fire in the ocean. The pure waters stand around and attend upon that same pure and shining Agni named Apāṃ Napāt.

**Printed English translation**

Some waters collect together (from the rain): others, (already collected on earth), unite with them; as rivers they flow together to propitiate the ocean-fire : the pure waters are gathered round the pure and brilliant grandsons of the waters.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In the sacrifice called Apōnaptrīya, the Ṛk beginning समन्या यंति (*samanyā yaṃti*) is to be recited as the anuvākya mantra near the Vasatīvarī waters, as explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta sūtra समन्यायंत्युपयंत्यन्या इति तीर्थदेशे (*samanyāyaṃtyupayaṃtyanyā iti tīrthadeśe*) (Ā. 5-1); also at the time of the Sārasvata śastra recitation,

### Printed p. 265

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 22] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 265.*

if the weapon called śamyā falls into the water, the Apōnaptrīya caru oblation is to be made, and then this Ṛk beginning समन्या यंति (*samanyā yaṃti*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra, as explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta sūtra समन्या यंत्युपयंत्यन्या इत्यातः समानं सर्वेषां (*samanyā yaṃtyupayaṃtyanyā ityātaḥ samānaṃ sarveṣāṃ*) (Ā. 12-6).

> अन्याः सं यंति, अन्याः उप यंति, समानं नद्यः ऊर्वं पृणंति—वर्ष्याः
> आपः भूम्या संगच्छंते अन्याश्च पूर्वं तत्रावस्थिताः उपगच्छंति ताः सर्वाः आपः
> नदीभूताः समुद्रमध्यॆ वर्तमानं वडवानलं प्रीणयंति ।

> *anyāḥ saṃ yaṃti, anyāḥ upa yaṃti, samānaṃ nadyaḥ ūrvaṃ pṛṇaṃti—varṣyāḥ*
> *āpaḥ bhūmyā saṃgacchaṃte anyāśca pūrvaṃ tatrāvasthitāḥ upagacchaṃti tāḥ sarvāḥ āpaḥ*
> *nadībhūtāḥ samudramadhyè vartamānaṃ vaḍavānalaṃ prīṇayaṃti |*

Waters coming as rain on the earth and the waters that were on the earth before unite and gather together. All these waters, combined, in the form of a river join the ocean; these waters, having joined the ocean in river form, are said to please the submarine fire that is in the midst of the ocean.

> तं अपां नपातं शुचिं निर्मलं दीदिवांसं शुचयः आपः परि तस्थुः—
> निर्मलं दीप्यमानं शुद्धाः आपः परिवृत्य शिष्ठंति । एष हि वैद्युताग्निरूपेण मेघे
> वर्तमानः अस्मानजीजनदिति बुद्ध्या बडबानलरूपेण वर्तमानं तं पर्युपासत
> इत्यर्थः ।

> *taṃ apāṃ napātaṃ śuciṃ nirmalaṃ dīdivāṃsaṃ śucayaḥ āpaḥ pari tasthuḥ—*
> *nirmalaṃ dīpyamānaṃ śuddhāḥ āpaḥ parivṛtya śiṣṭhaṃti | eṣa hi vaidyutāgnirūpeṇa meghe*
> *vartamānaḥ asmānajījanaditi buddhyā baḍabānalarūpeṇa vartamānaṃ taṃ paryupāsata*
> *ityarthaḥ |*

This deity Apāṃ Napāt is wholly pure and shines with splendour. Being in the cloud, the form of the lightning Agni, he has created us who exist in the form of water; so thinking, the waters surround him, who is also in the midst of the ocean in the form of the submarine fire, and serve him. This is one kind of meaning described; second:

> यद्वा अन्या एकधनाख्या आपः संयंति चात्वालोत्करयोर्मध्यॆ वसती
> वरीभिः संगच्छंते । अन्या वसतीवर्याख्या अपश्चोपयंति उपगच्छंति । ऐकमत्यं
> प्राप्ता भवंति । एताश्च मिलित्वा यज्ञं साधयंत्यः तत्साध्यवृष्टिद्वारा नद्यो
> भूत्वा ऊर्वं प्रीणंति । एवं हि आपो वा अस्पर्धंत वयं पूर्वं यज्ञं वक्ष्या
> मः (ऐ. ब्रा. २-२०) इत्यादि ब्राह्मणविनियोग अनुगृह्यते ।

> *yadvā anyā ekadhanākhyā āpaḥ saṃyaṃti cātvālotkarayormadhyè vasatī*
> *varībhiḥ saṃgacchaṃte | anyā vasatīvaryākhyā apaścopayaṃti upagacchaṃti | aikamatyaṃ*
> *prāptā bhavaṃti | etāśca militvā yajñaṃ sādhayaṃtyaḥ tatsādhyavṛṣṭidvārā nadyo*
> *bhūtvā ūrvaṃ prīṇaṃti | evaṃ hi āpo vā aspardhaṃta vayaṃ pūrvaṃ yajñaṃ vakṣyā*
> *maḥ (ai. brā. 2-20) ityādi brāhmaṇaviniyoga anugṛhyate |*

In the second meaning: among the waters used in the sacrificial acts, those known by the name Ekadhanā flow. In the sacrificial hall, in the region between the Cātvāla and the Utkara, they join with the waters called Vasatīvarī (some other waters). Thus all these waters come together. All of them together bring the sacrificial act to completion. After the rain to be obtained by the sacrifice has fallen, the waters flow in the form of rivers and serve the submarine fire in the midst of the ocean. The meaning is established in accordance with the passage stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa.

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तमस्मे॑रा युव॒तयो॒ युवा॑नं मर्मृ॒ज्यमा॑नाः॒ परि॑ यं॒त्यापः॑!
> स शु॒क्रेभिः॒ शिक्व॑भी रे॒वद॒स्मे दी॒दाया॑नि॒ध्मो घृ॒तनि॑र्णिग॒प्पु ॥ ४ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तं । अस्मेराः । युवतयः । युवानं । मर्मृज्यमानाः । परि । यंति । आपः ।
> सः । शुक्रेभिः । शिक्वभिः । रेवत् । अस्मे इति । दीदाय । अनिध्मः । घृतनिर्निक् । अप्सु॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> तमपां नपातमग्निमस्मेरा अस्मयमाना दर्परहिता युवतयो
> युवानं युवराजमिव मर्मृज्यमाना अत्यर्थमलंकुर्वाणा आपः ॥ मृजू
> शौचालंकारयोः ॥ परि यंति । परितो गच्छंति प्राप्नुवंति । धृतनिर्निक् क्षरणशी-
> लोदकनिर्नॆजनः । यद्वा निर्निगिति रूपनाम । दीप्तरूपः सोpां[?] नपादग्निरप्पु
> मेघांतर्गतासु समुद्रगतासु वा मध्येऽनिद्म इंधनरहित एव सन् अस्मै अस्माकं
> रेवद्धनयुक्तमन्नं यथा भवति तथा शुक्रेभिः शुभैर्निर्मलैः शिक्वभिस्तेजोभि-
> र्दिदाय । दीप्यते ॥

*Gist:* the waters, like modest young women adorning a young man, surround Agni; he shines among the waters without fuel, giving us wealth-bearing food.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अस्मेराः (*asmerāḥ*)—bashful; युवतयः (*yuvatayaḥ*)—young women; युवानं (*yuvānaṃ*)—a young man; मर्मृज्यमानाः (*marmṛjyamānāḥ*)—as if surrounding and adorning; आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters; तं (*taṃ*)—him, the Agni named Apāṃ Napāt; परि यंति (*pari yaṃti*)—surround and attend upon; धृतनिर्निक् (*dhṛtanirnik*) (as supplied; the Pada has घृतनिर्निक् (*ghṛtanirnik*))—having a form purified by ghee; सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni; अप्सु (*apsu*)—in the midst of the waters; अनिध्मः (*anidhmaḥ*)—remaining without fuel; आस्मे (*āsme*) (as supplied; Pada अस्मे (*asme*))—for us; रेवत् (*revat*)—so that food endowed with wealth is obtained; शुक्रेभिः (*śukrebhiḥ*)—with bright; शिक्ष्वभिः (*śikṣvabhiḥ*) (as supplied; Pada शिक्वभिः (*śikvabhiḥ*))—splendours; दीदायु (*dīdāyu*) (as supplied; Pada दीदाय (*dīdāya*))—he shines.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

As bashful young women surround and adorn a young man, so the waters surround and attend upon Agni named Apāṃ Napāt. That Agni, of a form purified by ghee, remaining without fuel in the midst of the waters, shines with bright splendours so that food endowed with wealth is obtained by us.

### Printed p. 267

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 22] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 267.*

**Printed English translation**

The young and modest (waters) wait upon the youth, assiduous in bathing him, and he, although unfed with fuel, yet cleansed with clarified butter, shines with bright rays amidst the waters, that abundanceee [sic] (may be) to us.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

तं आपः अस्मेराः युवतयः युवानं मर्मृज्यमानाः परि यंति (*taṃ āpaḥ asmerāḥ yuvatayaḥ yuvānaṃ marmṛjyamānāḥ pari yaṃti*)—Sāyaṇa explains: अपांनपातमग्निं अस्मयमानाः दर्परहिताः युवतयः युवानां युवराजमिव आत्यर्थमलंकुर्वाणाः आपः परितः प्राप्नु वंति (*apāṃnapātamagniṃ asmayamānāḥ darparahitāḥ yuvatayaḥ yuvānāṃ yuvarājamiva ātyarthamalaṃkurvāṇāḥ āpaḥ paritaḥ prāpnu vaṃti*). The meaning is described thus: as young women in their youth, free of pride, attend upon a young prince in his youth, so the waters of the rivers that join the ocean greatly tend and serve the Agni named Apāṃ Napāt.

सः अप्पु अनिध्मः (*saḥ appu anidhmaḥ*)—अपां नपादग्निः मेघांतर्गतासु समुद्रगतासु मध्यॆ वा इंधनरहितः (*apāṃ napādagniḥ meghāṃtargatāsu samudragatāsu madhyè vā iṃdhanarahitaḥ*)—the Agni named Apāṃ Napāt, in the midst of the waters that are within the clouds or have gone to the ocean, has no means of blazing; that is, he has the water itself as his fuel. And अस्मे रेवत् शुक्लेभिः शिक्वभिः दीदाय (*asme revat śuklebhiḥ śikvabhiḥ dīdāya*)—अस्माकं धनयुक्तं अन्नं यथा भवति तथा शुभ्रैः निर्मलैः तेजोभिः दीप्यते (*asmākaṃ dhanayuktaṃ annaṃ yathā bhavati tathā śubhraiḥ nirmalaiḥ tejobhiḥ dīpyate*): this Agni, granting to us the sacrificers food endowed with wealth, shines with pure and bright splendours; so it is described.

> कृता॑ इ॒वोप॒ हि प्र॑स॒र्स्रॆ अ॒प्सु स पी॒यूषं॑ धयति पूर्व॒सूनां॑॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> नारीर्नेत्र्यस्तिस्रो देवीर्देव्य इळासरस्वतीभारश्याख्या अव्यथ्यायाव्यथना-
> यास्मै देवायापां नपातेऽन्नं सोमाख्यं दिधिषंति । धारयंति ॥ धिष शब्दे
> जौहोत्यादिकः । व्यत्ययेनांत्यादेशः । धातूनामनेकार्थत्वादत्र धारणार्थः ॥
> अप्सूदकेषु कृता इवोपप्रसर्स्रॆ । प्रसरंति ॥ सृ गतौ । लिटीरयो रे इति रेआदेशः।
> छांदसो हलादिशेषाभावः ॥ यस्मादेवं तस्मात्पूर्वसूनां पूर्वं ब्रह्मणः
> सकाशादुत्पन्नानामपां पीयूषं सारभूतं सोमाख्यममृतं सोpां[?]नपाद-
> ग्निर्धयति । पिबति ॥

*Gist:* the three goddesses Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī bear the Soma-food to the unharmed god Apāṃ Napāt; he drinks the essence of the waters, the Soma-ambrosia.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

देवीः (*devīḥ*)—divine; शिस्रः[?] नारीः (*śisraḥ[?] nārīḥ*) (as supplied; the Saṃhitā has तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*))—three women, Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī; अव्यथाय (*avyathāya*)—to the unharmed; अस्मै देवाय (*asmai devāya*)—to this Agni named Apāṃ Napāt; अन्नं (*annaṃ*)—the food in the form of Soma; दिधिषंति (*didhiṣaṃti*)—carry and offer; अप्पु (*appu*) (as supplied; Pada अप्सु (*apsu*))—in the waters themselves; कृता इव (*kṛtā iva*)—as if made; उप प्रसस्रे (*upa prasasre*)—they spread out and extend; पूर्वसूनां (*pūrvasūnāṃ*)—of the waters produced of old from Brahmā; पीयूषं (*pīyūṣaṃ*)—the ambrosia that is the essence and has the form of Soma; सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni named Apāṃ Napāt; धयति (*dhayati*)—drinks.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The three divine women, Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, carry and offer the food in the form of Soma to this unharmed Agni named Apāṃ Napāt. As if made in the waters themselves, they spread out and extend. This Agni drinks the ambrosia, the essence of the waters produced of old from Brahmā, in the form of Soma.

**Printed English translation**

Three divine females present food to that uninjurable divinity ; as if formed in the waters they spread abroad, and he drinks the ambrosia of the first-created (element).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

नारीः तिस्रः देवीः अव्यथाय अस्मै देवाय अन्नं दिधिषंति (*nārīḥ tisraḥ devīḥ avyathāya asmai devāya annaṃ didhiṣaṃti*)—नेत्रः इळा सरस्वतीभारत्याख्याः तिस्रः देव्यः अपांनपाते सोमाख्यं अन्नं धारयंति (*netraḥ iḷā sarasvatībhāratyākhyāḥ tisraḥ devyaḥ apāṃnapāte somākhyaṃ annaṃ dhārayaṃti*). Here the word *anna* is explained as Soma. The three goddesses Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, who control the world, that is, are the regulators of the world, for the god Apāṃ Nahāt [?], the food called Soma,

### Printed p. 269

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 23] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 269.*

bearing it, are serving him; and अप्पु कृता इव (*appu kṛtā iva*): this Soma, as if it had been produced in the waters themselves, abundantly spreads, and these goddesses offer Soma to this god. Therefore this god, पूर्वसूनां पीयूषं (*pūrvasūnāṃ pīyūṣaṃ*)—drinks the ambrosia named Soma, the essence of the waters that came into being first of what was created by Brahmā; so it is described, and in this way the greatness of this god, whom Iḷā, Bhāratī and Sarasvatī also serve, and the excellence of Soma are described.

Yāska explains तिस्रोः देवीः (*tisroḥ devīḥ*) as तिस्त्रः देव्यः (*tistraḥ devyaḥ*) and, citing this reasoning (the following verse),

> आ नो यज्ञं भारती तूयमेत्विळा मनुष्वदिह चेतयंती ।
> तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं स्योनं सरस्वती स्वससः सदंतु ॥

> *ā no yajñaṃ bhāratī tūyametviḷā manuṣvadiha cetayaṃtī |*
> *tisro devīrbarhiredaṃ syonaṃ sarasvatī svasasaḥ sadaṃtu ‖*

(Ma. Saṃ. 10-110-8)

and then explaining it:

> ऐतु नो भारती यज्ञं क्षिप्रं । भरत आदित्यस्तस्य भा इळा च मनुष्यवदिह
> चेतयमाना तिस्रो देव्यो बर्हिरिदं सुखं सरस्वती च सुकर्माण आसीदंतु ।

> *aitu no bhāratī yajñaṃ kṣipraṃ | bharata ādityastasya bhā iḷā ca manuṣyavadiha*
> *cetayamānā tisro devyo barhiridaṃ sukhaṃ sarasvatī ca sukarmāṇa āsīdaṃtu |*

Ni. 8-14) (as printed, closing parenthesis only) he has explained the meaning thus: Bhāratī, the radiance of Āditya who nourishes all beings with waters; Iḷā, the well-known deity of the earth region; and Sarasvatī, the deity of the middle region, are called like human beings to the sacrificers' rites, and let them sit in the barhis-place of the sacrificial hall to receive the oblations offered by the sacrificers.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अत्रास्मिन्नपांनपात्संज्ञके देवेऽश्वस्य जनिम जन्म भवति । अपांनप्रधिष्ठिता-
> त्समुद्रादुच्चैःश्रवसो जातत्वात् । किं बहुना! अस्य च स्वः सुष्करणीयस्य सर्वस्य
> जगतो जन्मास्मिन्नेव भवति । अयं हि मेघमध्यॆ वर्तमानो वृष्टिद्वारेण सर्वं
> जगज्जनयति । तादृशोपांनपात्त्वं द्रुहो द्रोग्गुरपहर्तू रिषो हिंसकस्य च
> संपृचः संपर्कात्तरीन् स्तोत्यनस्मान्पाहि । रक्ष! आमास्वपरिपक्षासु पूर्णु
> पूरयितव्यास्वप्नु परः परस्ताद्वर्तमानमप्रमृष्यमप्रधृष्यमाणं देवमरात-
> योदातारः पुरुषा न विनशन् । न प्राप्पुवंति ॥ नशतिव्याप्तिकर्मा । लेट्यडागमः ॥
> अनृतानि मायाविनो रक्षांसि च न प्राप्पुवंति ॥

> *atrāsminnapāṃnapātsaṃjñake deve 'śvasya janima janma bhavati | apāṃnapradhiṣṭhitā-*
> *tsamudrāduccaiḥśravaso jātatvāt | kiṃ bahunā! asya ca svaḥ suṣkaraṇīyasya sarvasya*
> *jagato janmāsminneva bhavati | ayaṃ hi meghamadhyè vartamāno vṛṣṭidvāreṇa sarvaṃ*
> *jagajjanayati | tādṛśopāṃnapāttvaṃ druho droggurapahartū riṣo hiṃsakasya ca*
> *saṃpṛcaḥ saṃparkāttarīn stotyanasmānpāhi | rakṣa! āmāsvaparipakṣāsu pūrṇu*
> *pūrayitavyāsvapnu paraḥ parastādvartamānamapramṛṣyamapradhṛṣyamāṇaṃ devamarāta-*
> *yodātāraḥ puruṣā na vinaśan | na prāppuvaṃti ‖ naśativyāptikarmā | leṭyaḍāgamaḥ ‖*
> *anṛtāni māyāvino rakṣāṃsi ca na prāppuvaṃti ‖*

*Gist of the bhāṣya: in this Apāṃnapāt the horse (Uccaiḥśravas) was born from the ocean; the whole world is born in him, since he, abiding in the clouds, generates it through rain; he is asked to protect the singers from the harm of the treacherous and violent, and the givers-not and the untruthful cannot reach him. Grammatical tail: the verb नशति (*naśati*) in the sense of pervading; the Let augment.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अश्वस्य (*aśvasya*) — of the horse called Uccaiḥśravas; जनिम (*janima*) — the birth, अत्र (*atra*) — is in this Agni himself. अस्य च स्वः (*asya ca svaḥ*) — the birth of the whole moving world is also in this Agni named Apāṃ napāt. द्रुहः (*druhaḥ*) — of the enemy who practises treachery, रिषः (*riṣaḥ*) — and is violent; संपृचः (*saṃpṛcaḥ*) — from contact; सूरीन् (*sūrīn*) — us, the praisers; पाहि (*pāhi*) — protect. आमासु (*āmāsu*) — in the waters that are unripe, पूर्णु (*pūrṇu*) — and not full; परः (*paraḥ*) — who is in the highest place, अप्रमृष्यं (*apramṛṣyaṃ*) — unassailable, this Agni; आरातयः (*ārātayaḥ*) — men fallen from ritual; न वि नशन् (*na vi naśan*) — cannot approach. अन्मत्तानि (*anmattāni*) — even the untruthful asuras, न (*na*) — cannot approach.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The birth of the horse Uccaiḥśravas is in this Agni named Apāṃ napāt. The birth of the whole moving world is also in this Agni. O Agni, protect us, the praisers, from contact with the enemy who practises treachery and is violent. This Agni, who is in the highest place among the unripe and not-full waters and is unassailable, cannot be approached either by men fallen from ritual or by untruthful asuras.

**Printed English**

In hin [sic] is the birth of the horse ; of him is (the origin of) the world : grandson of the (waters), protect the pious worshippers from the malevolence of the oppressor : those who give no offerings. those who practise untruths, attain not the inconceivable deity, wether [sic] abiding in the immature or the perfect waters.

### Printed p. 271

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

अत्र अश्वस्य जनिम—अपांनपात्संज्ञके देवे अश्वस्य जन्म भवति (*atra aśvasya janima—apāṃnapātsaṃjñake deve aśvasya janma bhavati*) — From this deity famed by the name Apāṃ napāt arises the birth of the excellent horse Uccaiḥśravas. अस्य च स्वः—सुष्टु अरणीयस्य सर्वस्य जगतः जन्म आस्मिन्नेव भवति आयं हि मेघमध्यॆ वर्तमानः वृष्टिद्वारेण सर्वं जगत्‌जनयति (*asya ca svaḥ—suṣṭu araṇīyasya sarvasya jagataḥ janma āsminneva bhavati āyaṃ hi meghamadhyè vartamānaḥ vṛṣṭidvāreṇa sarvaṃ jagatjanayati*) (as printed) — The glory of this deity is told: while in the midst of the clouds, by pouring rain he makes all this moving world come into being.

And द्रुहः रिषः संपृचः सूरीन् पाहि (*druhaḥ riṣaḥ saṃpṛcaḥ sūrīn pāhi*) — describing this deity's power, protection is prayed for: may this deity protect us, the sacrificers or priests who praise him, so that no kind of contact (association) arises with those who cause us harm.

पूर्ण परः अरातयः न वि नशन्—पूरयितव्यासु अप्पु परस्तात् वर्तमानं अप्रधृष्यमाणं देवं अदातारः न प्राप्नुवंति (*pūrṇa paraḥ arātayaḥ na vi naśan—pūrayitavyāsu appu parastāt vartamānaṃ apradhṛṣyamāṇaṃ devaṃ adātāraḥ na prāpnuvaṃti*) — Even while the waters swell and fill the ocean, this deity remains apart from those waters, and since he cannot be rejected by anyone (when sought for sight), no non-givers can reach his presence. And अनृतानि न (*anṛtāni na*): those who follow the crooked path of deceit cannot attain his presence; thus it is described.

The word सूरि (*sūri*) is read among the names of praisers (Ni. 3-19). The word नशत् (*naśat*) is read among the verbs of pervading (Ni. 3-10). Although the word स्वः (*svaḥ*) has many kinds of meaning (Ni. 2-14), here its sense is explained as सुष्टु अरणीयस्य (*suṣṭu araṇīyasya*).

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> योऽपांनपात् स्वे दमे स्वकीये गृहेंतरिलक्षण आसीदति । यस्य च
> धेनुर्माध्यमिका वाक् सुदुघा सुखेन दोग्धव्या भवति । स देवः स्वधां
> वृष्टु दकं पीपाय । वर्धयति ॥ प्याया वृद्धौ । लिड्यजोश्चेति पीभावः ॥
> सुभु सुष्टु भूतं वृष्टेः सकाशादुत्पन्नं हविर्लक्षणमन्नं चात्ति । भक्षयति ।
> सोऽपांनपात्संज्ञको देव ऊर्जयन् बलं कुर्वन् अप्प्यंतर्मेघस्थास्वप्सु
> मध्यॆ विधते परिचरते यजमानाय वसुदेयाय धनदानार्थं विभाति ।
> विशेषेण दीप्यते ॥

> *yo 'pāṃnapāt sve dame svakīye gṛheṃtarilakṣaṇa āsīdati | yasya ca*
> *dhenurmādhyamikā vāk sudughā sukhena dogdhavyā bhavati | sa devaḥ svadhāṃ*
> *vṛṣṭu dakaṃ pīpāya | vardhayati ‖ pyāyā vṛddhau | liḍyajośceti pībhāvaḥ ‖*
> *subhu suṣṭu bhūtaṃ vṛṣṭeḥ sakāśādutpannaṃ havirlakṣaṇamannaṃ cātti | bhakṣayati |*
> *so 'pāṃnapātsaṃjñako deva ūrjayan balaṃ kurvan appyaṃtarmeghasthāsvapsu*
> *madhyè vidhate paricarate yajamānāya vasudeyāya dhanadānārthaṃ vibhāti |*
> *viśeṣeṇa dīpyate ‖*

*Gist: Apāṃ napāt abides in his own home, the atmosphere; his cow is the middle-region speech; he increases the rain-water, eats the food produced by rain, and shines among the cloud-waters to give wealth to the worshipper. Grammatical tail: प्याया वृद्धौ (*pyāyā vṛddhau*), the reduplication by the sūtra लिड्यजोश्च (*liḍyajośca*) (no number printed).*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) — Agni named Apāṃ napāt; स्वे दमे (*sve dame*) — in his own home of the atmospheric form; आ (सीदति) (*ā (sīdati)*) — is seated. यस्य (*yasya*) — whose; धेनुः (*dhenuḥ*) — the cow, the middle-region speech; सुदुघा (*sudughā*) — is excellently milkable. सः (*saḥ*) — that deity; स्वधां (*svadhāṃ*) — the water in the form of rain; पीपाय (*pīpāya*) — makes grow. सुभु (*subhu*) — produced excellently by the rain; अन्नं (*annaṃ*) — the food in the form of oblation; अत्ति (*atti*) — eats. (And) ऊर्जयन् (*ūrjayan*) — gathering strength; अप्वंतः (*apvaṃtaḥ*) — in the midst of the waters in the clouds; विधते (*vidhate*) — for the worshipper, the sacrificer; वसुदेयाय (*vasudeyāya*) — for giving wealth; वि भाति (*vi bhāti*) — shines exceedingly.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Agni named Apāṃ napāt sits in his own home, the atmosphere. He whose cow, the middle-region speech, is excellently milkable, increases the water in the form of rain and eats the oblation-food produced excellently by the rain. In order to give wealth to the worshipping sacrificer he gathers excellent strength and shines exceedingly in the midst of the waters in the clouds.

**Printed English**

He, the grandson of the waters, who abides in his own dwelling ; of whom is the readily-milked cow; who augments the nectar (of the skies and thence) eats the sacrificial food ; he, gatheing [sic] strength in the midst of the waters, shines for the sake of conferring wealth upon his worshipper.

### Printed p. 273

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

The deity named Apāṃ napāt is described thus: in "sve dame" (his own home, the home in the form of the atmosphere) he dwells; "dhenuḥ sudughā" — the cow connected with this deity, namely the middle-region speech (his power), is called upon to produce comfort for all, and so is beneficial to all; "svadhāṃ pīpāya" — this deity increases (the food), the rain-water (because he is in the home of atmospheric form). Thus described, this deity "subhu annaṃ ca atti" — he eats the food in the form of oblation, excellently produced from the rain-water. "Saḥ devaḥ apsyantaḥ" — Apāṃ napāt, being in the midst of the waters in the clouds, "vidhate ūrjayan vasudeyāya vibhāti" — shines with his exceeding splendours in order to bestow strength and abundant wealth upon the clouds and upon the sacrificers who serve him; so it is described.

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यो अ॒प्स्वा शुचि॑ना॒ दैव्ये॑न ऋ॒तावाज॑स्र उर्वि॒या वि॒भाति॑ ।
> व॒या इद॒न्या भुव॑नान्यस्य॒ प्र जा॑यंते वी॒रुध॑श्च प्र॒जाभिः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यः । अप्सु । आ । शुचिना । दैव्येन । ऋतवा । अजस्रः । उर्विया । विभाति ।
> वयाः । इत् । अन्या । भुवनानि । अस्य । प्र । जायंते । वीरुधः । च । प्रजाभिः ॥८॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> योऽपांनपादृतावा । ऋतमित्युदकनाम । तद्वान् सत्यवान्वा अजस्रो नित्य
> एकरूपेण सदा वर्तमान उर्विया उरुविस्तीर्णोऽप्सु मेघस्थासु मध्यॆ शुचिना
> शोचकेन दैव्येन देवसंबंधिना तेजसा आ समंताद्वभाति । विशेषेण प्रकाशते ।
> अस्यापांनपातोऽन्या अन्यानि भुवनानि सर्वाणि भूतजातानि वया इत् शाखा एव ।
> वीरुध ओषधयः प्रजाभिः स्वकीयाभिः पुष्पफलादिभिः सहास्मादेव प्रजायंते ॥

*Gist: Ṛta means water; Apāṃ napāt, truthful (or possessed of water), eternal, ever of one form and vast, shines in the midst of the cloud-waters with divine radiance; all other beings are his branches, and the plants are born with their offspring (flowers and fruits) from him.*

### Printed p. 274

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

यः (*yaḥ*) — which deity Apāṃ napāt; ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*) — being truthful; अजस्रः (*ajasraḥ*) — being eternal and of one form; उर्विया (*urviyā*) — being exceedingly vast; अप्पु (*appu*) — in the midst of the waters in the clouds; शुचिना (*śucinā*) — with the radiant; दैव्येन (*daivyena*) — and divine; with (that) splendour; आ (*ā*) — all around; विभाति (*vibhāti*) — shines exceedingly. अस्य (*asya*) — of that same deity; वया इत् (*vayā it*) — as branches; अन्या भुवनानि (*anyā bhuvanāni*) — all other beings exist. वीरुधश्च (*vīrudhaśca*) — the plants also; प्रजाभिः (*prajābhiḥ*) — together with their offspring in the form of fruits and flowers; प्रजायंते (*prajāyaṃte*) — are born of this Agni itself.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The deity Apāṃ napāt, who is truthful, eternal, of one form and exceedingly vast, shines exceedingly all around with a radiant and divine splendour in the midst of the waters in the clouds; all other beings are, as it were, branches of that deity. The plants also, together with their fruits and flowers, are born of this Agni itself.

**Printed English**

All other beings are, as it were, branches of him, who, truthful, eternal, and vast, shines amidst the waters with pure and divine (radiance); and the shrubs, with their products, are born (of him).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

यः ऋतावा—तद्वान् सत्यवान् वा (*yaḥ ṛtāvā—tadvān satyavān vā*). Although the word ṛta has the meanings truth, water and wisdom (prajñā), Sāyaṇa takes it here in the sense of water or truth, and so explains Apāṃ napāt as one who possesses water or is truthful. अजस्रः—नित्यः सदा एकरूपेण वर्तमानः (*ajasraḥ—nityaḥ sadā ekarūpeṇa vartamānaḥ*): this deity is imperishable and at all times of one kind. उर्विया उरु विस्तीर्णः (*urviyā uru vistīrṇaḥ*): this deity, who pervades exceedingly, अप्पु शुचिना दैव्येन आ विभाति (*appu śucinā daivyena ā vibhāti*) — shines everywhere with his divine splendour in the midst of the waters in the cloud. अस्य अन्या भुवनानि वया इत् (*asya anyā bhuvanāni vayā it*): since the many kinds of beings in the worlds are all born of this deity, they are said to belong to him (like branches to a tree)

### Printed p. 275

वीरुधः प्रजाभिः प्रजायंते (*vīrudhaḥ prajābhiḥ prajāyaṃte*) — (the word prajā is explained as the flowers and fruits produced on creepers) the creepers, and their flowers and fruits too, are born of this deity alone; thus the abundant power of this deity is described.

> तस्य । ज्येष्ठं । महिमानं । वहंतीः । हिरण्यवर्णाः । परि । यंति । यह्वीः ॥ ९ ॥

> सूत्रितं च । अपां नप्रे चरुमपां नपादा ह्यस्थादुपस्थं । आ. १२-६. । इति ॥

> वान् आरूढवान् खलु । किं कुर्वन् । जिह्मानां कुटिलगतीनामपां मध्य ऊर्ध्वः

> तदीयं माहात्म्यं सर्वत्र प्रकटयंत्य इव नद्यः प्रवहंतीत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist: This is the anuvākyā of the Apōnaptrīya (oblation of cooked grain) of the Sārasvata sattra (sūtra reference printed as "Ā. 12-6"). Apāṃ napāt rose into the atmosphere, clothing the lightning cloud, and rained; the golden, mighty rivers flow everywhere as if proclaiming his greatness out of gratitude.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) — Agni named Apāṃ napāt; जिह्मानां (*jihmānāṃ*) — in the midst of the waters of crooked course; ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*) — shining in an elevated region; विद्युत् (*vidyut*) — brilliance

, i.e. the shining cloud; वसानः (*vasānaḥ*) — clothed in it; उपस्थं (*upasthaṃ*) — the atmosphere, the lap (resting-place) of the waters; आ ह्यस्थात् (*ā hyasthāt*) — has taken his stand, resorting to it. तस्य (*tasya*) — of this Apāṃ napāt, the maker of rain; ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*) — praiseworthy; महिमानं (*mahimānaṃ*) — greatness; वहंतीः (*vahaṃtīḥ*) — bearing along; यह्वीः (*yahvīḥ*) — and mighty; हिरण्यवर्णाः (*hiraṇyavarṇāḥ*) — the rivers; परि यंति (*pari yaṃti*) — flow all around.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Agni named Apāṃ napāt shines in an elevated region in the midst of the waters of crooked course, clothed in the shining cloud as in a covering, and stands resting on the atmosphere, the lap of the waters. The mighty rivers, bearing along the praiseworthy greatness of this rain-maker Apāṃ napāt, flow all around.

**Printed English**

The grandson of the waters has ascended the firmament above (the region) of the tortuously-moving (clouds), arrayed in lightnlng [sic] : the broad and golden-coloured (rivers) spread around, bearing (to all quarters) his exceeding glory.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In the cooked-grain oblation connected with the Apōnaptrīya of the Sārasvata sacrifice mentioned earlier, this Ṛk beginning अपांनपादा हि (*apāṃnapādā hi*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra, as set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra अपां नष्टे चरुमपां नपादा ह्यस्थादुपस्थं (*apāṃ naṣṭe carumapāṃ napādā hyasthādupasthaṃ*) (Ā. 12-6).

जिह्वानां ऊर्ध्वः विद्युतं वसानः (*jihvānāṃ ūrdhvaḥ vidyutaṃ vasānaḥ*) — see the Sāyaṇa passage (given above) that begins कुटिलगतीनामपां मध्ये (*kuṭilagatīnāmapāṃ madhye*). In the midst of the waters flowing in a crooked manner this deity shines with his upward-directed splendours; covering the cloud that shines with his own radiance, and pervading the atmosphere, he causes the rain-waters to pour down.

यह्वीं हिरण्यवर्णाः परियंति (*yahvīṃ hiraṇyavarṇāḥ pariyaṃti*) — see the passage above beginning महत्यः हिरण्यवन्निर्मलरूपा नद्यः (*mahatyaḥ hiraṇyavannirmalarūpā nadyaḥ*). The word हिरण्यवर्णाः (*hiraṇyavarṇāḥ*) is stated among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-4). The very large rivers, pure and radiant like gold, abundant rain-waters according to their flow,

*Gist: Apāṃ napāt has a golden body and golden senses (or a body and senses beneficial and pleasing), is golden in hue, sits above his golden seat; the sacrificers who give gold as fee offer him oblation-food.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सः अपां नपात् (*saḥ apāṃ napāt*) — the deity Apāṃ napāt; हिरण्यरूपः (*hiraṇyarūpaḥ*) — having a form made of gold; हिरण्यसंदृक् (*hiraṇyasaṃdṛk*) — having attractive senses; सेदु (*sedu*) — he himself; हिरण्यवर्णः (*hiraṇyavarṇaḥ*) — being of golden colour; हिरण्ययात् (*hiraṇyayāt*) — golden; योनेः (*yoneḥ*) — of the seat; परि (*pari*) — upon; निषद्य (*niṣadya*) — seated (he shines); अस्मै (*asmai*) — to this Apāṃ napāt

### Printed p. 278

deity, addressing him; हिरण्यदाः (*hiraṇyadāḥ*) — the sacrificers who offer gold (as fee); अन्नं (*annaṃ*) — food in the form of oblation; ददति (*dadati*) — offer.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The deity Apāṃ napāt, of golden form, with attractive senses and of golden hue, shines seated upon a golden seat. The sacrificers who offer gold as fee to this Agni also offer food in the form of oblation.

**Printed English**

The grandson of the waters is of golden form, of golden aspect, of golden hue, and (shines) seated upon a seat of gold : the givers of gold (at solemn rites) present to him (sacrificial) food.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

सः अपां नपात् हिरण्यरूपः (*saḥ apāṃ napāt hiraṇyarūpaḥ*) — रूप्यत इति रूपं शरीरं । सुवर्णमयशरीरः हितरमणीयशरीरो वा (*rūpyata iti rūpaṃ śarīraṃ | suvarṇamayaśarīraḥ hitaramaṇīyaśarīro vā*). Here the word rūpa is used in the sense of body. The deity Apāṃ napāt wears a body of golden lustre, or a body pleasant and charming to all, so it is explained.

हिरण्यसंदृक् (*hiraṇyasaṃdṛk*) — सम्यक् पश्यंतीति संदृश इंद्रियाणि । सुवर्णमयेंद्रियो हितरमणीयेंद्रियो वा (*samyak paśyaṃtīti saṃdṛśa iṃdriyāṇi | suvarṇamayeṃdriyo hitaramaṇīyeṃdriyo vā*). The word sandṛś is used in the sense of the senses, the means of full knowledge. The senses of this deity are radiant like gold, or productive of pleasure and charming; the deity is explained as possessing such senses.

हिरण्ययात् योनेः परि निष द्य (*hiraṇyayāt yoneḥ pari niṣa dya*) — सुवर्णमयात् स्थानादुपरि उपविश्य राजते (*suvarṇamayāt sthānādupari upaviśya rājate*). This deity shines, seated comfortably above a region of golden lustre.

अस्मै हिरण्यदाः अन्नं ददति (*asmai hiraṇyadāḥ annaṃ dadati*) — ईदृग्विधाय अपां नपाते दक्षिणारूपस्य दातारः यजमानाः हविर्लक्षणमन्नं प्रयच्छंति (*īdṛgvidhāya apāṃ napāte dakṣiṇārūpasya dātāraḥ yajamānāḥ havirlakṣaṇamannaṃ prayacchaṃti*). Addressing this deity of such abundant power, the sacrificers are described as giving gold as the sacrificial fee and offering food in the form of oblation.

#### Ṛk 11

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तद॒स्यानी॑कमु॒त चारु॒ नामा॑पी॒च्यं॑ वर्धते॒ नपु॑र॒पां ।
> यमिं॒धते॑ युव॒तयः॒ समि॒त्था हिर॑ण्यवर्णं घृ॒तमन्न॑मस्य ॥ ११ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तत् । अस्य । अनेकं । उत । चारु । नाम । अपीच्यं । वर्धते । नपुः । अपां ।
> यं । इंथते । युवतयः । सं । इत्था । हिरण्यवर्णं । घृतं । अन्नं । अस्य ॥११॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अस्यापांनपुर्देवस्यानीकं रश्मिसमूहरूपं शरीरं चारु शोभनं । उत
> अपि च अस्य नाम संज्ञा च चारु शोभनं न पातयति न विनाशयतीति नपादिति
> तद्व्युत्पत्तेः । तदुभयमपीच्यं । अंतर्हितनामैतत् । मेघांतर्हितं सद्वर्धते ।
> युवतयः संगमनस्वभावा आपो हिरण्यवर्णं हिरण्यसमानतेजसं यमपांनपात-
> मित्थामुत्रांतरिक्षे समिंधते । सम्यक् दीपयंति । अस्य च देवस्य धृतं क्षरणशील-
> मुदकमन्नं भक्ष्यं । अबंधनो ह्यसौ वैद्युतोऽग्निः ॥

*Gist: his body of massed rays and his name are both beautiful; hidden in the cloud they grow; the youthful waters kindle him in the firmament; water is his food.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

हिरण्यवर्णं (*hiraṇyavarṇaṃ*) — of form attractive like gold; यं (*yaṃ*) — whom, the Agni called Apāṃ napāt; युवतयः (*yuvatayaḥ*) — the waters, having the nature of joining together; इत्था (*itthā*) — in the firmament; सं इंधते (*saṃ iṃdhate*) — cause to blaze; अस्य (*asya*) — of such; अपां नप्तुः (*apāṃ naptuḥ*) — of the grandson of the waters, Agni; तत् अनेकं (*tat anekaṃ*) — that body, of the form of a mass of rays; चारु (*cāru*) — is charming; उत (*uta*) — and; नाम (*nāma*) — the name of this Agni too is attractive to the mind (this form and name, both attractive); अपीच्यं (*apīcyaṃ*) — hidden within the cloud; वर्धते (*vardhate*) — they grow; अस्य (*asya*) — to this deity; धृतं (*dhṛtaṃ*) — water; अन्नं (*annaṃ*) — is nourishing food.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The waters, which have the nature of joining together, cause to blaze in the firmament the Agni called Apāṃ napāt, whose form is attractive like gold; the body of this grandson of the waters, in the form of a mass of rays, is charming. The name of this Agni too is charming. This attractive form and name, both of them, grow while hidden within the cloud. For this deity water is nourishing food.

### Printed p. 280

**Printed English**

Beautiful is his form (of aggregated lustre, beautiful) is the name of the grandson of the waters; (both) flourish, though hidden (by the clouds); the youthful waters collectively kindle the golden-coloured divinity in the firmament, for water is his food.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

अस्यं अनेकं चारु—रश्मिसमूहरूपं शरीरं शोभनं (*asyaṃ anekaṃ cāru—raśmisamūharūpaṃ śarīraṃ śobhanaṃ*) — Taking the word *anīka* to mean a body in the form of a mass of rays, the body of this deity is handsome, being endowed with a multitude of rays (radiances).

अस्य नाम चारु—अस्य संज्ञाच चारु शोभनं। न पातयति न विनाशयशीति नपादिति व्युत्पत्तेः। (*asya nāma cāru—asya saṃjñāca cāru śobhanaṃ| na pātayati na vināśayaśīti napāditi vyutpatteḥ|*) — The word *napāt* means "one who does not make fall" (*na pātayati*, does not abandon) or "one who does not destroy" (*na vināśayati*, does not bring to ruin). Hence this deity does not abandon or cast down or destroy those who have taken refuge in him, and for this reason the name of this deity too is auspicious.

यं युवतयः अपीच्यं हिरण्यवर्णं इत्था समिंधते — संगमनस्वभावाः आपः मेघांतर्हितं हिरण्यसमानतेजसं अमुत्रांतरिक्षे समिंधते । (*yaṃ yuvatayaḥ apīcyaṃ hiraṇyavarṇaṃ itthā samiṃdhate — saṃgamanasvabhāvāḥ āpaḥ meghāṃtarhitaṃ hiraṇyasamānatejasaṃ amutrāṃtarikṣe samiṃdhate |*) The deity Apāṃ napāt is hidden in the midst of the clouds and has a lustre equal to gold. The waters, which have the nature of flowing or pervading, make this deity grow in the firmament. And in अस्य धृतं अन्नं—अस्य च देवस्य क्षरणशीलमुदकं भक्ष्यं । (*asya dhṛtaṃ annaṃ—asya ca devasya kṣaraṇaśīlamudakaṃ bhakṣyaṃ |*) the food of this deity is just the water, of flowing nature; and it is described that this deity is the lightning-fire, which is delightful (अभिनंदनवागिरुव (*abhinaṃdanavāgiruva*) in the Kannada explanation).

अपीच्यं (*apīcyaṃ*) — this word is stated by Yāska (Nir. 3-19) among the names of hidden things.

*Gist: to this first of many deities, our friend, we offer worship with sacrifices, oblations and homage; I adorn his high place, feed him with kindling wood and food, and praise him with Ṛks.*

The grammatical tail of the bhāṣya (on the root *mṛj*, accent-suppression, *dhiṣ*, the reduplicated present and its accent) is transcribed above and not explained.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

बहूनां (*bahūnāṃ*) — among many deities; अवमाय (*avamāya*) — the first one; सख्ये (*sakhye*) — who is our friend; अस्मै (*asmai*) — to this Agni called Apāṃ napāt [sic, supplied text reads अपानं पात् (*apānaṃ pāt*)]; यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*) — which are means of sacrifice; हविर्भिः (*havirbhiḥ*) — with oblations such as *caru* and *purodāśa*; नमसा (*namasā*) — with salutations; विधेम (*vidhema*) — I offer service; सानु (*sānu*) — the high place of Agni; सं मार्ज्मि (*saṃ mārjmi*) — I cleanse and adorn; बिल्मैः (*bilmaiḥ*) — with fuel that makes him blaze; दिधिषामि (*didhiṣāmi*) — I nourish; अन्नैः (*annaiḥ*) — with food in the form of oblations; दधामि (*dadhāmi*) — I support; ऋग्भिः (*ṛgbhiḥ*) — with hymns of praise; परि वंदे (*pari vaṃde*) — I salute, circumambulating.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

To this Agni called Apāṃ napāt, the first among many deities and our friend, I render service with the sacrificial *caru* and *purodāśa* and with salutations. I cleanse and adorn the high place of this Agni. I nourish him with fuel that makes him blaze. I support him with food in the form of oblations. With hymns of praise I salute him, circumambulating.

**Printed English**

To him our friend, the first of many (deities), we offer worship with sacrifices, oblations, and prostration: I decorate the high place

### Printed p. 282

(of his presence) : I nourish him with fuel ; I nourish him with (sacrificial) viands :  I glorify him with hymns.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

अस्मै बहूनां अवमाय (*asmai bahūnāṃ avamāya*)—पुरोवर्तिने देवानां आद्याय (*purovartine devānāṃ ādyāya*) (to him who is present before us, the first of the gods). The word बहु (*bahu*) is established in the sense of *prabhūta* (much, many). For this word, which is always used as an adjective, the word देवानां (*devānāṃ*) has been supplied as the noun qualified. The word अवम (*avama*) always conveys the sense "inferior"; here the sense "first" is given, and it is described that because this Apāṃ napāt deity is the first among the gods worthy of the sacrifice, and regards the sacrificers as friends, being सख्यॆ (*sakhyè*)—समानख्यानाय (*samānakhyānāya*) (of equal renown), the sacrificers worship this deity नमसा हविर्भिः (*namasā havirbhiḥ*) with salutations and with offerings of oblations.

सानु संमार्ज्जि (*sānu saṃmārjji*)—समुच्च्रितप्रदेशं सम्यक् शोधयामि अलंकरोमि वा (*samuccritapradeśaṃ samyak śodhayāmi alaṃkaromi vā*) (I cleanse well, or adorn, the raised place). Since the place where this fire Apāṃ napāt is set is the altar (*vedi*) in the sacrificial hall, it is explained that the sacrificer or the priests make this raised place pure or adorn it.

बिल्मैः (*bilmaiḥ*)—भासनैः काष्ठैः (*bhāsanaiḥ kāṣṭhaiḥ*) (with shining pieces of wood). Yāska explains the word बिल्म (*bilma*) as बिल्मं भिल्मं भासनमिति वा (*bilmaṃ bhilmaṃ bhāsanamiti vā*) (Nir. 1-20). Durgācārya, explaining the formation of the word बिल्म (*bilma*) as भिदेर्भासतीर्वा बिल्म शब्दः (*bhiderbhāsatīrvā bilma śabdaḥ*), describes the meaning of the word *bilma* as भेदो व्यासः अथवा भासनमेव बिल्मशब्देनोच्यते (*bhedo vyāsaḥ athavā bhāsanameva bilmaśabdenocyate*), that is, explaining or making bright. Here Sāyaṇa has given the meaning "fuel (wood), the means of making the fire blaze".

*Gist: the fire Apāṃ napāt, becoming the impregnator, produced himself as an embryo in the cloud-waters, drinks them as their child, and as the earthly fire pervades this world with a body of wood.*

The grammatical tail of the bhāṣya (on the root *lih*, with optional *l* for *r*, and the root *viṣ*/*vyāp*) is transcribed above and not explained; the last words are garbled in the supplied text.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

स ईं (*sa īṃ*)—that same fire called Apāṃ napāt; वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—being possessed of the power of sprinkling; तासु (*tāsu*)—in the waters abiding in the cloud; गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—an embryo; अजनयत् (*ajanayat*)—produced (for himself). स ईं (*sa īṃ*)—that same fire who has himself created his embryo; शिशुः (*śiśuḥ*)—born as an infant in the form of lightning; धयति (*dhayati*)—drinks (the waters abiding in the cloud); तं (*taṃ*)—this fire; रिहंति (*rihaṃti*)—(the waters) touch; सः अपां नपात् (*saḥ apāṃ napāt*)—that same fire called Apāṃ napāt; अनभिम्लातवर्णः (*anabhimlātavarṇaḥ*)—possessing a radiance that does not decay in the least; इह (*iha*)—on this earth; अन्यस्येव तन्वा (*anyasyeva tanvā*)—with the bodies of wood and the like of the earthly fire, which is other than the lightning form; विवेष (*viveṣa*)—has pervaded.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

That same fire called Apāṃ napāt, possessed of the power of sprinkling, created for himself his own embryo in the waters abiding in the cloud. Afterwards, born himself as an infant in the form of lightning, he drinks the waters abiding in the cloud. The waters touch this fire. That same fire, with a radiance that does not decay in the least, has pervaded this earth with the bodies, wood and the like, of the earthly fire, which is other than the lightning form.

**Printed English**

Vigorous, he has generated himself as an embryo in those (waters): he is their infant; he sucks them; they bedew him (with moisture); the grandson of the waters of untarnished splendour has descended to this (earth) in the form of a different (fire).

### Printed p. 284

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

स ईं वृषा तासु गर्भं अजनयत् (*sa īṃ vṛṣā tāsu garbhaṃ ajanayat*)—सोऽयमपां नपात्संज्ञको देवः सेक्ता भूत्वा मेघस्थास्वप्पु स्वात्मानमेव गर्भरूपेण वर्षणार्थं कृतवान् (*so 'yamapāṃ napātsaṃjñako devaḥ sektā bhūtvā meghasthāsvappu svātmānameva garbharūpeṇa varṣaṇārthaṃ kṛtavān*). It has been explained earlier that the deity Apāṃ napāt exists in the form of the lightning-fire in the midst of the clouds, and in the form of the submarine fire in the midst of the sea. It is explained here, by showing as an illustration the course by which a living creature comes into the womb, is born, grows and spreads in the world, that this deity, being in the midst of the cloud, came into being in the manner of the world, and that this deity, being in the form of an infant, grows and pervades the world. Since the waters in the clouds are in a dense (solid) form, this deity is in the midst of the clouds so that the rain-waters may fall to the earth. To this eternal deity (who has neither birth nor death) the state of being in the womb is attributed. After coming out of the womb (after birth) the infant needs food in order to grow; likewise स ईं शिशुः धयति (*sa īṃ śiśuḥ dhayati*)—सोयं माध्यमिकः वैद्युतः अग्निः तासां शिशुपुत्रस्सन् मेघस्थाः ताः पिबति । अबंधनोसौ (*soyaṃ mādhyamikaḥ vaidyutaḥ agniḥ tāsāṃ śiśuputrassan meghasthāḥ tāḥ pibati | abaṃdhanosau*). This deity, existing in the form of the lightning-fire, a deity of the middle region, becoming the infant of the waters, drinks the waters that are in the clouds, just as an infant takes food for the growth of its body: so it is described.

अपांनपात् अनभिम्लातवर्णः इह अन्यस्येव तन्ना विवेश (*apāṃnapāt anabhimlātavarṇaḥ iha anyasyeva tannā viveśa*) [sic, as supplied: तन्ना विवेश (*tannā viveśa*)] आयं वृष्टा सह भूमौ निपतितः म्लातः म्लानः क्षीणः वर्णो यस्य तद्विपरीतः अत्यर्थं दीप्यमानः अस्मिन् लोके पार्थिवस्यॆवाग्ने काष्ठेंधनत्वलक्षणेन शरीरेण व्याप्तो बभूव (*āyaṃ vṛṣṭā saha bhūmau nipatitaḥ mlātaḥ mlānaḥ kṣīṇaḥ varṇo yasya tadviparītaḥ atyarthaṃ dīpyamānaḥ asmin loke pārthivasyèvāgne kāṣṭheṃdhanatvalakṣaṇena śarīreṇa vyāpto babhūva*). It is described that the clouds, together with the rain-waters, pervade the earth; that he, taking the form of the earthly fire, which is other than the food in the form of his lightning-fire [the supplied text reads आहार (*āhāra*), "food"], pervades the whole world; and that this earthly fire takes, in his own form, the wood-fuels necessary for his growth.

अनभिम्लातवर्णः (*anabhimlātavarṇaḥ*)—अभितः क्षीणः वर्णः यस्य तद्विपरीतः अत्यर्थं दीप्यमानः (*abhitaḥ kṣīṇaḥ varṇaḥ yasya tadviparītaḥ atyarthaṃ dīpyamānaḥ*). The meaning is described thus: that which is devoid of lustre in every way is *abhimlāta-varṇa*, and, opposed to it, that which is endowed with abundant lustre is *anabhimlāta-varṇa*.

> वहंतीर्वहंत्यः ॥

*Gist: the waters, bearing watery food to their grandson Apāṃ napāt, who abides in the supreme intermediate region and shines daily with undecaying lustre, flow around him of their own accord.*

The grammatical tail of the bhāṣya (दीयति (*dīyati*) as a verb of motion, from the root दीज् (*dīj*) "to waste away", with an irregular parasmaipada) is transcribed above and not explained.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

ಪರಮೇ (parame)—in that supremely excellent; ಅಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಪದೇ (asmin pade)—place in the form of the atmosphere; ತಸ್ಥಿವಾಂಸಂ (tasthivāṃsaṃ)—who abides; ಅಧ್ವಸ್ಮಭಿಃ (adhvasmabhiḥ)—with undecaying radiances; ವಿಶ್ವಹಾ (viśvahā)—on all days; ದೀದಿವಾಂಸಂ (dīdivāṃsaṃ)—and who shines, the fire called Apāṃ napāt; ಯಹ್ವೀಃ (yahvīḥ)—of great form; ಅಪಃ (apaḥ)—the waters; ನಪ್ನೇ (napne)—to their grandson; ಧೃತಂ (dhṛtaṃ) [sic, as supplied; the Saṃhitā has ಘೃತಂ]—watery; ಅನ್ನಂ (annaṃ)—food; ವಹಂತೀಃ (vahaṃtīḥ)—carrying; ಸ್ವಯಂ (svayaṃ)—by their own impulse; ಅತ್ಕೈಃ (atkaiḥ)—with their own forms that move constantly; ಪರಿ ದೀಯಂತಿ (pari dīyaṃti)—flow around him.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Having in view the fire called Apāṃ napāt, who abides in that supremely excellent place in the form of the atmosphere and shines on all days with undecaying radiances, the great waters, carrying watery food to their grandson, flow around him by their own impulse with their own forms that move constantly.

**Printed English**

The abundant waters, bearing sustenance to their grandson, flow round him wiih [sic] spontaneous movements; when abiding in his supreme sphere, and shining daily with imperishable (rays).

### Printed p. 286

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

The deity Apāṃ napāt is परमे पदे तस्थिंवांसं (*parame pade tasthiṃvāṃsaṃ*) (the supplied text has ತಸ್ಥಿಂವಾಂಸಂ)—उत्कृष्टे अंतरिक्षलक्षणे स्थाने स्थितवंतं (*utkṛṣṭe aṃtarikṣalakṣaṇe sthāne sthitavaṃtaṃ*). The word *paramapada* is explained as the atmosphere, which is the highest of all or the most excellent, and the deity is also described as one who dwells in the atmosphere.

अध्वस्मभिः विश्वहा दीदिवांसं (*adhvasmabhiḥ viśvahā dīdivāṃsaṃ*)—ध्वंसनरहितैः तेजोभिः सर्वाण्यहानि दीप्यमानं (*dhvaṃsanarahitaiḥ tejobhiḥ sarvāṇyahāni dīpyamānaṃ*): it is explained that this deity shines at all times with his own lustres, which are not put down by other lights or which suffer no fall.

यह्वीः आपः स्वयमत्कैः परि दीयंति (*yahvīḥ āpaḥ svayamatkaiḥ pari dīyaṃti*)—महत्यः आपः आत्मना सततगंतृभिः स्वकीयैः रूपैः परिगच्छंति (*mahatyaḥ āpaḥ ātmanā satatagaṃtṛbhiḥ svakīyaiḥ rūpaiḥ parigacchaṃti*). The abundant waters, of themselves, being all around with their respective forms which are endowed with the nature of flowing at all times, serve this deity.

And नप्रे अपांनपाते धृतमन्नं वहंतीः (*napre apāṃnapāte dhṛtamannaṃ vahaṃtīḥ*): the meaning is given that the rivers too, flowing by nature, carry food in the form of water for this deity. From this it is indicated, and may be understood, that the common practice of the world is stated: just as dependants or kinsmen, who are close to a lord of lofty and honoured station and radiant, and who are favoured by him, serve him, so the waters and rivers serve this deity.

The meaning of the word *paramapada* has been explained fully elsewhere.

> जनाय । अस्मदीयपुत्रादिजननार्थं । तथा मघवद्यो हविर्लक्षणधनयुक्तेभ्यो

> तद्भद्रमस्माकं भवतु । सुवीराः सुपुत्रा वयं विदथे यज्ञे गृहे वा बृहत्
