*Gist: Agni, I have come to you for offspring and with a hymn for the offerers; may all the good that the gods protect be ours, and may we, rich in sons, recite a mighty hymn at the sacrifice.*

The grammatical tail of the bhāṣya (the root यम उपरमे (*yama uparame*), "to cease") is transcribed above and not explained.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

ಅಗ್ನೇ (agne)—O Agni; ಸುಕ್ಷಿತಿಂ (sukṣitiṃ)—you, who have an excellent dwelling; ಜನಾಯ (janāya)—for the sake of offspring; ಆಯಾಂಸಂ (āyāṃsaṃ)—I have approached (to ask); ಮಘವದ್ಭ್ಯಃ (maghavadbhyaḥ)—for the sacrificers who are endowed with wealth in the form of oblations; ಸುವೃಕ್ತಿಂ (suvṛktiṃ)—a beautiful hymn; ಅಯಾಂಸಂ (ayāṃsaṃ)—I have approached, offering; ಯತ್ ಭದ್ರಂ (yat bhadraṃ)—which good; ದೇವಾಃ (devāḥ)—all the gods; ಅವಂತಿ (avaṃti)—protect; ವಿಶ್ವಂ ತತ್ (viśvaṃ tat)—all that good (may it also fall to us); ಸುವೀರಾಃ (suvīrāḥ)—we, endowed with excellent sons; ವಿದಥೇ (vidathe)—in the house of sacrifice; ಬೃಹತ್ (bṛhat)—a mature hymn; ವದೇಮ (vadema)—will recite.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, I have approached you, who have an excellent dwelling, to ask for offspring. I have approached, offering a beautiful hymn for the sacrificers endowed with wealth in the form of oblations. May all that good which all the gods protect fall to us also. We, endowed with excellent sons, will recite a mature hymn in the house of sacrifice.

**Printed English**

I:have [sic] come, Agni, to you, (the giver) of good dwellings. for the sake of offspring : I have come with a propitiatory hymn for the sake of the opulent (offerers of oblations) : may all the good which the gods defend (be ours) ; that, blessed with excellent descendants, we may worthily glorify you at this sacrifice.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

The meaning of the first half of this Ṛk may be said to be a prayer of the seer who saw the mantra, and that of the second half a prayer of the sacrificers (who perform the sacrifice).

### Printed p. 288

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 35, p. 288.*

[Continuing the Special Topics of Ṛk 15:] Addressing Agni with अग्ने (*agne*), the commentary says सुकृतिं जनाय आयासं (*sukṛtiṃ janāya āyāsaṃ*): "I have approached (you of) an excellent dwelling, for the birth of our sons and others"; that is, it is prayed that Agni, who has an excellent abode, may cause sons and others to be born to us who serve him. Here, for the word जनाय (*janāya*) the meaning पुत्रादिजननं (*putrādijananaṃ*), "the birth of sons and others", is given. Although the word मघ (*magha*) is listed among the names of wealth (Nighaṇṭu 3-9), for the word मघवद्भ्यः (*maghavadbhyaḥ*) the commentary gives हविर्लक्षणधनयुक्तेभ्यः (*havirlakṣaṇadhanayuktebhyaḥ*), "for those who possess wealth in the form of oblations", i.e. for the sacrificers; and it explains that an excellent hymn concerning Agni is recited for them.

The prayer that we sacrificers make to Agni is this: यत् भद्रं सर्वे देवाः अवंति (*yat bhadraṃ sarve devāḥ avaṃti*), "the good which all the gods desire and protect" — may that good also come to us sacrificers. So it is expressed.

## Sūkta 36 (Maṇḍala 2)

*The thirty-sixth sūkta.*

**Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta** (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

> तुभ्यमिति षडृचं चतुर्थं सूक्तं गार्त्समदं जागतं । प्रथमाया इंद्रो
> मधुश्च देवता । द्वितीयाया मरुतो माधवश्च । तृतीयायास्त्वष्टा शुक्रश्च ।
> चतुर्थ्या अग्निः शुचिश्च । पंचम्या इंद्रो नभश्च । षष्ठ्या मित्रावरुणौ नभस्यश्च ॥ तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । तुभ्यं षडृतव्यं तु जागतं त्विति ॥ दशरात्रे षष्ठेऽहनि ऋतुयाजेषु
> ऋक्शिरस्कैः प्रैषैः प्रेषितव्यं यष्टव्यं च । तताद्यानां षण्णां प्रैषाणामुपरि-
> ष्वादेव ताः षडृचोऽहोरात्रादिभिः क्रमेणावपनीयाः । तथा च सूत्रितं ।
> उपरिष्टात्त्वृच ऋतुयाजानामित्युपक्रम्य तुभ्यं हिन्वानो वसिष्ट गा अप इति
> द्वादशेत्यंतेन । आ. ८-१. ॥

*Gist:* the fourth sūkta of the fourth anuvāka, of six ṛks, of the Gārtsamada seer, in *jagatī*; the deities of the six ṛks are listed (Indra and Madhu; the Maruts and Mādhava; Tvaṣṭṛ and Śukra; Agni and Śuci; Indra and Nabha; Mitra-Varuṇa and Nabhasya); the Anukramaṇī is quoted; the use is in the Ṛtuyājas of the sixth day of the Daśarātra, with the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra cited (8-1).

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, तुभ्यं हिन्वानः (*tubhyaṃ hinvānaḥ*), is the fourth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has six ṛks. Gṛtsamada is the seer of this sūkta; the metre is *jagatī*. For the first ṛk of this sūkta the deities are Indra and the month Madhu (the month of Caitra); for the second ṛk, the Marut deities and Mādhava, that is, the month of Vaiśākha; for the third ṛk, Tvaṣṭṛ and Śukra, or the month of Jyeṣṭha; for the fifth ṛk, Indra and Nabha, or the month of Śrāvaṇa; for the sixth ṛk, Mitra and Varuṇa and Nabhasya, or the month of Bhādrapada. [The fourth ṛk, Agni and Śuci, is not mentioned in the Kannada here as supplied.]

### Printed p. 289

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 25, p. 289 (the Kannada text prints the first abbreviation as "ಅ." as supplied).*

What the Anukramaṇikā says is: तुभ्यं षडृतव्यं तु जागतं त्विति (*tubhyaṃ ṣaḍṛtavyaṃ tu jāgataṃ tviti*). On the sixth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, when the oblations called Ṛtuprayājas are made, the ṛks of this sūkta are to be used both as Praiṣa mantras and as Yājyā mantras. Of the Praiṣa mantras, the use of the six ṛks of this sūkta is stated for the first six. Thereafter, the same six ṛks are to be used, in order, in the days and nights for the Āvapanīya mantras; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra beginning उपरिष्टात्त्वृच ऋतुयाजानामित्युपक्रम्य (*upariṣṭāttvṛca ṛtuyājānāmityupakramya*) and ending तुभ्यं हिन्वानो वसिष्ठ गा अप इति द्वादशेत्यंतेन (*tubhyaṃ hinvāno vasiṣṭha gā apa iti dvādaśetyaṃtena*) (Ā. 8-1).

**Sūkta 36** — Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 36; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 25. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Seer: Gṛtsamada. Deities: 1. Indra and Madhu; 2. the Maruts and Mādhava; 3. Tvaṣṭṛ and Śukra; 4. Agni and Śuci; 5. Indra and Nabha; 6. Mitra-Varuṇa and Nabhasya. Metre: *jagatī*. (The supplied text has stray figures "५" before and after the metre line; not read.)

> हे इंद्र तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं हिन्वानः प्रेर्यमाणः सोमो गा गोविकाराणि
> दधिपयःप्रभृतीनि श्रपणद्रव्याणि वसतीवर्याख्या अपश्च वसिष्ट!! वस्ते । आच्छादयति ।
> तैः संयुज्यत इत्यर्थः । नरो यज्ञस्य नेतारोऽध्वर्यवश्च सीमेनं सोममवि-
> भिरवेर्वालमय्यर्दशापवित्रैरद्रिभिग्र्रावभिश्चाधुक्सन् । अक्षारयन् । ग्रावभिरभिषुत्य
> दशापवित्रेण पुनंतीत्यर्थः । हे इंद्र यस्त्वमीशिषे । सर्वस्य जगत ईश्वरो भवसि
> त्वं प्रथमोऽन्येभ्यो देवेभ्यः पूर्वभावी सन् स्वाहा स्वाहाकारेण प्रहुतं
> प्रकर्षणाग्नौ क्षिप्तं वषट्कृतं वषट्कारेण च त्यक्तं तं सोमं होत्राद्दोतु-
> र्यागादा समंतात्पिब ॥

*Gist: Indra, the Soma pressed for you is mixed with milk products and waters; the priests have pressed it with stones and strained it; you, lord of the world, drink it first, from the Hotṛ's sacrifice.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra. तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you. हिन्वानः (*hinvānaḥ*)—the Soma that has been pressed. गाः (*gāḥ*)—the products of the cow, milk and the like. अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters, the Vasatīvarī and others. वसिष्ठ (*vasiṣṭha*)—has joined with (them). नरः (*naraḥ*)—the leaders, the Adhvaryus. सीं (*sīṃ*)—this Soma. आविभिः (*āvibhiḥ*)—with the ten-fold filters [as supplied]. अद्रिभिः (*adribhiḥ*)—with stones. अधुक्सन् (*adhuksan*)—have pressed and strained. इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra. यः (*yaḥ*)—you who. ईशिषे (*īśiṣe*)—are lord of the whole world (such as you are). प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—before the other gods. स्वाहा (*svāhā*)—with the cry Svāhā. प्रहुतं (*prahutaṃ*)—cast into the fire. वषट् कृतं (*vaṣaṭ kṛtaṃ*)—offered with the cry Vaṣaṭ. सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma. होत्रात् (*hotrāt*)—receiving it from the Hotṛ's sacrifice. आ पिब (*ā piba*)—drink.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, the Soma pressed for you is joined with the products of the cow, such as milk, and with waters such as the Vasatīvarī. The leaders, the Adhvaryus, have pressed this Soma with the pressing stones and strained it with the ten-fold filters. O Indra, you who are lord of the whole world, coming before the other gods, receive from the Hotṛ's sacrifice the Soma that has been cast in with the cry Svāhā and purified with the cry Vaṣaṭ, and drink it.

**Printed English**

(The libation) that is being presented, Indra, to you, comprises the (products of the) cow, and the (consecrated) water ; and the leaders (of the rite) have expressed it with stones, and strained it through woollen (filters) : Indra, you are the first (of the gods), and rule (over the world), drink the Soma offered [printed "off ered"] by the Hotri, and sanctificed [sic] bythe [sic] exclamations Swaha and Vashat.

### Printed p. 291

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 25, p. 291 (the Kannada text prints the first abbreviation as "ಅ." as supplied).*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

गाः—गोविकाराणि दधिपयःप्रभृतीनि श्रयणद्रव्याणि (*gāḥ—govikārāṇi dadhipayaḥprabhṛtīni śrayaṇadravyāṇi*). Here the word *go* is explained as the substances connected with the cow, such as milk and curds, which are mixed with the Soma juice; and अपः—वसतीवर्याख्या अपश्च (*apaḥ—vasatīvaryākhyā apaśca*): the word *ap* is used in the sense of the waters called Vasatīvarī. Having thus explained the meaning, the commentary describes the Soma juice pressed for Indra as joined with curds, ghee, milk and the like, products of the cow, and with the waters called Vasatīvarī.

नरः—यज्ञस्य नेतारो अध्वर्यवश्च (*naraḥ—yajñasya netāro adhvaryavaśca*). The word *nara* is stated by Yāska among the names of men (Ni. 3-7, as printed "ಸಿ.೩-೭"). Sāyaṇa explains this word as the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice and the priests such as the Adhvaryu; and for सीं अविभिः अद्रिभिः अधुक्षन्—ग्रावभिः अभिष्टुत्य दशापवित्रेण पुनंति (*sīṃ avibhiḥ adribhiḥ adhukṣan—grāvabhiḥ abhiṣṭutya daśāpavitreṇa punaṃti*) he says that the sacrificers and the priests have prepared this Soma by crushing it with stones, pressing out the juice and purifying it with the ten-fold filters.

Addressing Indra, the commentary describes this Indra as lord of all; प्रथमः—अन्येभ्यो देवेभ्यः पूर्वभावी र्स (*prathamaḥ—anyebhyo devebhyaḥ pūrvabhāvī rsa*) [sic as supplied: र्स (*rsa*) for *san*]: coming to the sacrifice before the other gods, may he drink in full the Soma offered in the fire for Indra with the words Vaṣaṭkāra and Svāhā.

> प्रिया उत ।
> आ॒सद्या॑ ब॒र्हिर्भ॑रतस्य सूनवः पो॒त्रादा सोमं॑ पिबता दिवो
> नरः ॥ २ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यज्ञैः । संमिश्लाः । पृषतीभिः । ऋष्टिभिः । यामन् । शुभ्रासः । अंजिषु । प्रियाः ।
> उत ।
> आसद्य । बर्हिः । भरतस्य । सूनवः । पोत्रात् । आ । सोमं । पिबत । दिवः । नरः ॥२॥

> *yajñaiḥ | saṃmiślāḥ | pṛṣatībhiḥ | ṛṣṭibhiḥ | yāman | śubhrāsaḥ | aṃjiṣu | priyāḥ |*
> *uta |*
> *āsadya | barhiḥ | bharatasya | sūnavaḥ | potrāt | ā | somaṃ | pibata | divaḥ | naraḥ ‖2‖*

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 36, p. 292.*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतो यज्ञैर्याग्यैः संमिश्लाः संयुक्ताः पृषतीभिः स्ववाहनभूताभिः
> पृषद्वतीभिर्वडवाभियुक्ते यामन् यामनि गमनसाधने रथेऽवस्थिता ऋष्टिभिः
> स्वकीयैरायुध्यैः शुभ्रासः शुभ्राः शोभमानाः । उतशब्दश्चार्थे । अंजिष्वाभरणेषु
> प्रियाश्च हे भरतस्य सूनवः सर्वस्य जगतो भर्तू रुद्रस्य पुत्रा दिवो नरो
> दिवोंतरिक्षस्य नेतारः एवंभूता हे मरुतः ते यूयं बर्हिरास्तीर्णे बर्हिष्या-
> सद्योपविश्य पोत्रात् पोतुर्यागात् सोममापिबत ॥

*Gist: O Maruts, joined together in sacrifices, riding the car of spotted mares, bright with spears, dear in ornaments, sons of Rudra and leaders of the sky, sit on the grass and drink the Soma from the Potṛ.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*)—by the sacrifices. संमिश्लाः (*saṃmiślāḥ*)—those who are worshipped together. पृषतीभिः (*pṛṣatībhiḥ*)—with the mares called Pṛṣadvatī (yoked). यामन् (*yāman*)—those seated in the car. ऋष्टिभिः (*ṛṣṭibhiḥ*)—with weapons. शुभ्रासः (*śubhrāsaḥ*)—those who shine. अंजिषु (*aṃjiṣu*)—in ornaments. प्रियाः (*priyāḥ*)—those who are fond. भरतस्य (*bharatasya*)—of Rudra, the supporter of the world. सूनवः (*sūnavaḥ*)—sons. दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the firmament. नरः (*naraḥ*)—leaders; O Maruts such as these. बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—upon the spread seat of darbha grass. आ सद्य (*ā sadya*)—having sat down. पोत्रात् (*potrāt*)—offered by the Potṛ. सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma. आ पिबत (*ā pibata*)—drink.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Maruts, who are worshipped together in the sacrifices, who sit in the car yoked with mares called Pṛṣadvatī, who shine with weapons, who are fond of ornaments, who are sons of Rudra the supporter of the world and leaders of the firmament: sit on the spread seat of darbha grass and drink the Soma juice offered by the Potṛ.

**Printed English**

Maruts, together worshipped with sacrifices, standing in the car drawn by spotted mares, radiant with lances, and delighted by ornaments, sons of Bharata, leaders in the firmament, seated on the sacred grass, drink the Soma presented by the Potri.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this ṛk the Marut deities are described. These Maruts are पृषतीभिः यामन्—स्ववाहनभूताभिः पृषद्वतीभिर्वडवाभिः युक्ते गमनसाधने रथे अवस्थिताः (*pṛṣatībhiḥ yāman—svavāhanabhūtābhiḥ pṛṣadvatībhirvaḍavābhiḥ yukte gamanasādhane rathe avasthitāḥ*): that is, seated in cars to which are yoked their own mounts, horses with white spots, as the means of travelling about,

### Printed p. 293

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 25, p. 293 (the Kannada text prints the first abbreviation as "ಅ." as supplied).*

and ऋष्टिभिः शुभ्रासः (*ṛṣṭibhiḥ śubhrāsaḥ*), shining with their weapon famed as the *ṛṣṭi*, a spear; भरतस्य सूनवः—सर्वस्य जगतो भर्तुः रुद्रस्य पुत्राः (*bharatasya sūnavaḥ—sarvasya jagato bhartuḥ rudrasya putrāḥ*): sons of Rudra, the lord of all the worlds. Having so described them, it explains their power: दिवो नरः—अंतरिक्षस्य नेतारः (*divo naraḥ—aṃtarikṣasya netāraḥ*), leaders of the firmament, that is, rulers of the sky; and it says of them, पोत्रात् सोममापिबत (*potrāt somamāpibata*) (as supplied), may they drink the Soma offered by the priest called Potṛ (printed प्रोतृ (*protṛ*)).

### Printed p. 294

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 36, p. 294 (as supplied).*

*Gist of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Ṛk 3 (the Sanskrit is given on p. 293):* Sāyaṇa says the Ṛk is the Neṣṭṛ's prasthita-yājyā at the third pressing; Tvaṣṭṛ and the other deities are asked to come together, sit on the grass, rest, and enjoy the Soma food with their company.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सुहवाः (*suhavāḥ*)—O Tvaṣṭṛ and the rest of you, who are invoked in an excellent manner; नः (*naḥ*)—to us; अमेव (*ameva*)—all together; आ गंतन (*ā gaṃtana*)—come; बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—on the darbha grass; नि सदतन (*ni sadatana*)—sit down; रणिष्टन (*raṇiṣṭana*)—take rest and play; अथ (*atha*)—afterwards; त्वष्टः (*tvaṣṭaḥ*)—O Tvaṣṭṛ; देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)—with the other gods; जनिभिः (*janibhiḥ*)—with the wives of the gods; सुमद्गणः (*sumadgaṇaḥ*)—you who are joined by an excellent company; अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—the food in the form of Soma; जुजुषाणः (*jujuṣāṇaḥ*)—partaking of; मंदस्व (*maṃdasva*)—be satisfied.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Tvaṣṭṛ and the rest of you, who are invoked in an excellent manner, come to us all together. Sitting on the grass, take rest and play. Afterwards, O Tvaṣṭṛ, you who have made an excellent company with the other gods and the wives of the gods, partake of the food in the form of Soma and be satisfied.

**Printed English**

You, who are devoutly invoked, come to us together, and seated on the sacrificial grass. enjoy your rest ; and then, Twashtri, you head a brilliant cohort, (come) with the gods and their wives, and rejoice, being pleased with the (sacrificial) food.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

At the third pressing this Ṛk अमेव नः (*ameva naḥ*) is to be used as the prasthita-yājyā mantra to be recited by the Neṣṭṛ; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra अमेव नः सुहवा आ हि गंतनेंद्राविष्णू पिबतं मध्वो अस्य (*ameva naḥ suhavā ā hi gaṃtaneṃdrāviṣṇū pibataṃ madhvo asya*) (Ā. 5-5). In अमेव (*ameva*) the word इव (*iva*) is not used in the sense of a word of comparison; since it is stated in the sense of emphasis, it is used in the sense "together indeed".

सुहवाः (*suhavāḥ*)—शोभनाह्वानाः (*śobhanāhvānāḥ*)—describing the invocation of Tvaṣṭṛ and the other deities as auspicious, it expresses the wish that these deities come together to the sacrificial hall of us, the sacrificers.

बर्हिषि नि सदतन (*barhiṣi ni sadatana*)—वेद्यामास्तिर्णे निषण्णा भवत (*vedyāmāstirṇe niṣaṇṇā bhavata*). It explains: let them come to the sacrificial hall and be seated on the darbha grass spread on the altar; and रणिष्टन (*raṇiṣṭana*)—रमध्वं (*ramadhvaṃ*). रणशब्दार्थः अत्र क्रीडायां वर्तते धातूनामनेकार्थत्वात् (*raṇaśabdārthaḥ atra krīḍāyāṃ vartate dhātūnāmanekārthatvāt*). The root रण (*raṇa*) here

### Printed p. 295

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2 [sic, as supplied], Adhyāya 7, Varga 25, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, p. 295 (as supplied).*

is used in the sense of play, according to the rule that roots have many meanings; hence it explains that these deities, Tvaṣṭṛ and the rest, coming to the sacrificial hall, sitting on the grass, may take their ease.

जनिभिः देवेभिः सुमद्गणः (*janibhiḥ devebhiḥ sumadgaṇaḥ*)—अन्यैः देवैः देवपत्नीभिश्च शोभनगणः (*anyaiḥ devaiḥ devapatnībhiśca śobhanagaṇaḥ*). Because this god Tvaṣṭṛ is joined with the deities of his own retinue, with the other deities and with the wives of the gods, it expresses the wish that this god, joined with his company, partake of the oblation that is in the form of Soma and be satisfied.

अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—सोमलक्षणस्यान्नस्य (*somalakṣaṇasyānnasya*). The word अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*) is stated among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). Here it explains the meaning as food that is in the form of Soma.

The word विप्र (*vipra*) is stated among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19). Here, by this word, it explains that Agni is wise, and addresses him.

होतः उशन् त्रिषु योनिषु निषद (*hotaḥ uśan triṣu yoniṣu niṣada*)—देवानामाह्वातः त्वं अस्मदीयं कामयमानः गार्हपत्यादि लक्षणेषु त्रिषु स्थानेषु उपविश (*devānāmāhvātaḥ tvaṃ asmadīyaṃ kāmayamānaḥ gārhapatyādi lakṣaṇeṣu triṣu sthāneṣu upaviśa*). … in the sacrifices of the sacrificers he desires the offering of the oblation, and it expresses the wish that this Agni sit in the sacrificial hall in the respective places fixed for him and known as the Gārhapatya, the Āhavanīya and the Dakṣiṇāgni.

प्रस्थितं सोम्यं मधु प्रति वीहि (*prasthitaṃ somyaṃ madhu prati vīhi*) and the explanation that follows (उपविश्यच होमार्थमुत्तरवेदिं प्रत्यानीतं सोममयं मधु प्रतिकामयस्व (*upaviśyaca homārthamuttaravediṃ pratyānītaṃ somamayaṃ madhu pratikāmayasva*)): the sacrificers, having offered the oblation in the places fixed for the fires, each according to its rite, place this Agni, when performing the Paśuka and Soma rites, at another place called the Uttaravedi, and there offer Soma, ghee and the other oblations in the fire. It is described as the wish of the sacrificers that Agni, seated on the Uttaravedi in those rites, accept the sweet drink known as Soma.

### Printed p. 298

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 36, p. 298 (as supplied).*

> हृतश्च । अस्येमं सोमं ब्राह्मणात् ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनो यागात्तृपत् तृप्यं-
> स्त्वमापिब । अभिमुख्येन पिब ॥ क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाद-
> स्येति चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठी ॥

*Gist:* Sāyaṇa: this Soma augments Indra's bodily strength and places might in his arms; it is pressed and brought for him; let him drink it, satisfied, from the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's sacrifice.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

O Indra; स्यः (*syaḥ*)—the well-known; एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—this Soma juice; ते (*te*)—your; तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*)—body's; नृम्मवर्धनः (*nṛmmavardhanaḥ*)—is the increaser of strength (the Soma juice by which); प्रदिवि (*pradivi*)—of you, the ancient one; बाहोः (*bāhoḥ*)—in the arms; सहः (*sahaḥ*)—the strength that defeats enemies; ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—the inner power that is its root; हितः (*hitaḥ*)—has been established; मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra; तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you alone; सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—(this juice) has been pressed; तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for the sake of performing the sacrifice directed to you; आभृतः (*ābhṛtaḥ*)—has been brought to the Uttaravedi; अस्य (*asya*)—this Soma; ब्राह्मणात् (*brāhmaṇāt*)—from the sacrifice of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; तृपत् (*tṛpat*)—becoming satisfied; त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you; आ पिब (*ā piba*)—come face to face and drink.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, this well-known Soma juice is the increaser of the strength of your body. By this same Soma juice the strength that defeats enemies and the inner power that is its root have been established in the arms of you, the ancient one. O wealthy Indra, this juice has been pressed for you alone; it has been brought to the Uttaravedi for the sake of performing the sacrifice directed to you. In the sacrifice of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin come face to face, drink the Soma and be satisfied.

**Printed English**

This (libation), Indra, is the augmenter of your bodily (vigour), favourable of old to the resistless strength of (your) arms : it is effused Maghavan, for you : it is brought to you from the Brahmana ; drink and be satisfied.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

नृष्णवर्धनः—बलस्य वर्धनः (*nṛṣṇavardhanaḥ—balasya vardhanaḥ*). The words नृष्णं (*nṛṣṇaṃ*), सहः (*sahaḥ*) and ओजः (*ojaḥ*) are read by Yāska among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9). For the word नृष्णवर्धनः (*nṛṣṇavardhanaḥ*) Sāyaṇa gives शरीरस्य बलस्य वर्धकः (*śarīrasya balasya vardhakaḥ*): Soma increases the strength connected with the body. By this he states the use of the word नृष्ण (*nṛṣṇa*) in the sense of bodily strength. बाह्वोः सहः—हस्तयोः परेषामभिभवनलक्षणं सामर्थ्यं (*bāhvoḥ sahaḥ—hastayoḥ pareṣāmabhibhavanalakṣaṇaṃ sāmarthyaṃ*); ओजः—तत्कारणभूतं बलं (*ojaḥ—tatkāraṇabhūtaṃ balaṃ*): this is the commentary given. By it the meaning is explained: सहः (*sahaḥ*)

### Printed p. 299

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 25, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 299 (as supplied; the head was not recognised by the splitter and the page marker was inserted by hand).*

is the valour famed for overcoming enemies, and ओजः (*ojaḥ*) is the power of mind that is its cause. It is further explained that Soma is said to produce these three kinds of capacity in Indra. Having thus described the power of the Soma juice, the verse addresses Indra as मघवन्—धनवन् (*maghavan—dhanavan*), the wealthy, and says तुभ्यं सुतः, तुभ्यमाभृतः (*tubhyaṃ sutaḥ, tubhyamābhṛtaḥ*): the Soma, pressed by the priests beginning with the Adhvaryu and ready on the Uttaravedi to be offered with reference to Indra, ब्राह्मणात् तृपन् आ पिब (*brāhmaṇāt tṛpan ā piba*) (the text as supplied reads तृपन् (*tṛpan*) here, and तृपत् (*tṛpat*) in the verse) — ब्राह्मणांच्छंसिनो यागात् तृप्यन् (आ पिब) अभिमुख्येन पिब (*brāhmaṇāṃcchaṃsino yāgāt tṛpyan (ā piba) abhimukhyena piba*). It is described as the wish of the sacrificer that Indra drink, until he is satisfied, what the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin offers in the fire.

> शस्त्राणि शंसतीत्यर्थः । अपि च नमः सोमलक्षणमन्नमावृतमृत्वग्निर्वॆष्टितं

> अभिमुख्येन पिबतं ॥

*Gist:* Sāyaṇa addresses Mitra and Varuṇa: enjoy my sacrifice and note my call; the seated Hotṛ recites the ancient nivids; the Soma food, surrounded by the priests, comes to you; drink the sweet Soma from the Praśāstṛ's sacrifice.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa; यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—this sacrifice; जुषेथाः (*juṣethāḥ*)—enjoy [the supplied text reads जुषेथाः (*juṣethāḥ*) against जुषेथां (*juṣethāṃ*) in the verse]; मे (*me*)—my; हवस्य (*havasya*)—call; बोधतं (*bodhataṃ*)—understand; सत्तः (*sattaḥ*)—the seated; होता (*hotā*)—Hotṛ; पूर्व्या (*pūrvyā*)—ancient; निविदः (*nividaḥ*)—nivid mantras; अनु (*anu*)—recites; आवृतं (*āvṛtaṃ*)—surrounded by the priests; नमः (*namaḥ*)—the food in the form of Soma; राजाना (*rājānā*)—you who shine; अच्छ (*accha*)—coming face to face; एति (*eti*)—approaches; सोम्यं (*somyaṃ*)—made of Soma; मधु (*madhu*)—and intoxicating; the oblation; प्रशास्त्रात् (*praśāstrāt*)—from the sacrifice of the Praśāstṛ; आ पिबतं (*ā pibataṃ*)—drink.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Mitra and Varuṇa, enjoy this sacrifice. Understand my call. The Hotṛ seated here recites the ancient nivid mantras. The food in the form of Soma, surrounded by the priests, comes face to face with you who shine and approaches you. Drink the oblation, made of Soma and intoxicating, from the sacrifice of the Praśāstṛ.

**Printed English**

Mitra and Varuna, both be gratified with the sacrifice: hear my invocation as the seated Hotri repeats in succession the ancient praises : the (sacrificial) food, encompassed (by the priests), attends the royal pair; drink both of you, the sweet Soma libation, offered by the Prasastri.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

यज्ञं जुषेथां—हे मित्रावरुणौ मदीयमिमं यज्ञं सेवेथां (*yajñaṃ juṣethāṃ—he mitrāvaruṇau madīyamimaṃ yajñaṃ sevethāṃ*). Addressing Mitra and Varuṇa, it is expressed as a wish that they enjoy the sacrifices of the sacrificers; and मे हवस्य बोधतं—मम हवमाह्वानं अवगच्छतं (*me havasya bodhataṃ—mama havamāhvānaṃ avagacchataṃ*): the meaning of the word हव (*hava*) is explained as invocation. It is expressed as a wish that Mitra and Varuṇa take note of the sacrificer's invocation, calling them to come for the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 301

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 25, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, p. 301.*

[Continuing the Special Topics of Ṛk 6:] होता पूर्व्याः निविदः अनु- (*hotā pūrvyāḥ nividaḥ anu-*) ("the Hotṛ recites after the ancient nivids"): अस्मदीयः होता चिरंतनीः शस्त्रलक्षणा वाचः (*asmadīyaḥ hotā ciraṃtanīḥ śastralakṣaṇā vācaḥ*) ("our Hotṛ, the ancient utterances of the nature of śastras") recites. उद्गातृभिः कृतस्य स्तोत्रस्यानुगुण्येनाज्यादीनि शंसति (*udgātṛbhiḥ kṛtasya stotrasyānuguṇyenājyādīni śaṃsati*) ("he recites the ājya and the rest in accordance with the stotra performed by the Udgātṛs"). It is described that the priest who invites the gods to the sacrifice with the respective mantras, when he performs the sacrifice, recites, in accordance with the praises recited by the priest called Udgātṛ, the mantras known as śastras, which from ancient times must necessarily be recited at the times of performing the respective rites.

आवृतं नमः राजाना अच्छ एति (*āvṛtaṃ namaḥ rājānā accha eti*) ("the encompassed food approaches the two who shine"): ऋत्विग्निः वेष्टितं सोमलक्षणमन्नं राज (*ṛtvigniḥ veṣṭitaṃ somalakṣaṇamannaṃ rāja*) ("the food in the form of Soma, surrounded by the priests, approaches you two who shine face to face"; the sentence continues on the next line in the supplied text). The word नमः (*namaḥ*) (*namaḥ*) is explained as meaning "food". It is described that the food in the form of Soma, surrounded by the priests and offered in the fire, comes near Mitra and Varuṇa, who shine with their own splendours; and, since the priest called Praśāstṛ has offered this Soma in the fire, the sacrificer's wish is described: may Mitra and Varuṇa drink this intoxicating Soma. (The supplied text at this point reads the phrase अभिमुख्येन पिबतं (*abhimukhyena pibataṃ*), "drink face to face", together with the name प्रशास्त्र (*praśāstra*) as supplied.)

निविदः (*nividaḥ*) (*nividaḥ*)—the word *nivid* is read among the names of speech (Ni. 2-13); the sense is: sentences describing the greatness of the gods.

In the beginning Prajāpati was alone; desiring to create beings and to become many, he practised austerity for a year, resorting to silence. Then, after he had recited twelve times the nivid mantras comprising twelve great sentences, all beings in the world were created. Having thus declared the power of these mantras, the text then praises Kutsa, who knew their secret, and the greatness of the ṛk that he recited.

Quotation (Brāhmaṇa): तदेतदृषिः पश्यन्नभ्यनूवाच स पूर्वया निविदा कव्यतायोरिमाः प्रजा (*tadetadṛṣiḥ paśyannabhyanūvāca sa pūrvayā nividā kavyatāyorimāḥ prajā*) ... अजनयन्मनूनामिति (*ajanayanmanūnāmiti*) ("the seer, seeing this, said: 'He, with the ancient nivid, ... created these people of the Manus'"; the quotation is divided between two lines in the supplied text and is given here as supplied). The Kannada explains: the seer Kutsa grasped the truth that by the power of the nivid mantras all beings of the world were created, and recited the mantra "Sa pūrvayā" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-2).

Quotation (Brāhmaṇa): तद्यदेतां पुरस्तात् सूक्तस्य निविदं दधाति प्रजात्यै (*tadyadetāṃ purastāt sūktasya nividaṃ dadhāti prajātyai*) ("therefore he places this nivid at the beginning of the sūkta, for procreation"); प्रजायते प्रजया पशुभिर्य एवं वेद (*prajāyate prajayā paśubhirya evaṃ veda*) ("he who knows thus is born with offspring and cattle"). For this very reason the Hotṛ, by reciting the nivid mantra at the beginning of the sūkta, obtains offspring. For those who have this understanding, all wealth, beginning with good offspring, will be obtained.

[Continuing:] A mantra which addresses one deity or one group of deities, describes their uncommon qualities and invokes them, is known as a nivid mantra.

कर्मैव तावत्सावित्र्यां निविदि स्तौति कर्मणा । (*karmaiva tāvatsāvitryāṃ nividi stauti karmaṇā |*)
यद्धेनुः सप्त्यनड्वाहौ वोळ्हा दोग्धाशुरेव वा ॥ (*yaddhenuḥ saptyanaḍvāhau voḷhā dogdhāśureva vā ‖*)

For example, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-3, the nivid mantra addressed to the deity Savitṛ declares Savitṛ's distinction and the description of his uncommon action. From the word दोग्धिर् (*dogdhir*) (*dogdhir*) we understand a cow that yields milk; from *āśu* (swift), a horse; from वोळ्हा (*voḷhā*) (*voḷhā*), "one who bears a burden", an ox: so their distinctive characters are known. In the same way the nivid mantra praises each deity by stating that deity's individual qualities through the description of the respective actions.

The thirty-sixth sūkta is ended.

## Sūkta 37 (Maṇḍala 2)

*The thirty-seventh sūkta.*

> *krameṇa prakṣepaṇīyāḥ | sūtraṃ tu pūrvamevodāhṛtaṃ ‖*

*Gist:* the sūkta *Mandasva* has six ṛks, seer Gṛtsamada, in *jagatī*; the first four ṛks have Draviṇodas, the fifth the Aśvins, the sixth Agni as deity; on the sixth day of the Daśarātra the six ṛks are used as Praiṣa and Yājyā mantras in the Ṛtuyājas. (The supplied text reads यतुयाजेषु (*yatuyājeṣu*) in the Sanskrit, while the Kannada below says Ṛtuyāga; noted as supplied.)

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** Now the eighth adhyāya in the second aṣṭaka begins. In the fourth anuvāka of the second maṇḍala, this sūkta beginning *Mandasva hotrāt* is the fifth sūkta. It has six ṛks. Gṛtsamada is the seer of this sūkta. The Anukramaṇikā says "Mandasva". Since the Anukramaṇikā earlier said "ṛtavyaṃ tu jāgataṃ tviti" and used the particle *tu*, this sūkta too is a sūkta of ṛks in the *jagatī* metre, addressed to the Ṛtu deities. In sūkta addressed to the Ṛtus it is usual that other deities are praised together with the Ṛtu deities. Therefore, along with the Ṛtu deities, the ṛks of this sūkta have separate deities as well. Hence the first four ṛks of this sūkta have Draviṇodā as deity; the fifth ṛk has the Aśvins; the sixth ṛk has Agni. In the Ṛtuyāga performed on the sixth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, the ṛks of the Ṛgveda are used as Praiṣa mantras, and with those ṛks the recital of the Praiṣa mantras and the oblation must be done. Of such Praiṣa mantras, after the seventh Praiṣa mantra, the six ṛks of this sūkta beginning with *Mandasva* are used in order as Praiṣa mantras and Yājyā mantras. The sūtra sentence on this matter was already given earlier.

*Two stray lines in the supplied text, "ಪಿ ರ್ ಱ ಕ" and "485", stand here; kept as a note, not read.*

In the Ṛtuprayāja oblations made for the Ṛtus, the six ṛks of the previous sūkta and the six ṛks of this sūkta are both used as Praiṣa mantras and as Yājyā mantras. To ṛks addressed to the Ṛtus, other deities are joined along with the Ṛtus. For example, for the first four ṛks of this sūkta, along with the Ṛtus, the deities called Draviṇodā are stated; for the fifth ṛk, the Aśvins; for the sixth ṛk, Agni. The same order is found in the fifteenth sūkta of the first maṇḍala, of twelve ṛks, beginning *Indra somaṃ piba*: that is, for ṛks 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 respectively, the deities are Indra, Marut, Tvaṣṭā, Agni, Indra, and Mitrāvaruṇa, each together with an Ṛtu. In the last six ṛks, as in the present sūkta, four ṛks have the deity Draviṇodā together with the Ṛtus, the next ṛk the Aśvins, and the last ṛk Agni.

### Printed p. 305

*Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 1, p. 305 (as supplied).*

**Note on the Ṛtus (Kannada commentary).** In the previous sūkta and in this one, the gods are prayed to drink Soma together with the Ṛtus. A detailed explanation of the Ṛtus is therefore necessary here. The Ṛtus are the deities presiding over the months. A year has twelve months, and every two months are known as one Ṛtu; so the twelve months make six Ṛtus. In common usage the year is generally divided into three, summer, rainy season and winter; but in the Vedas, taking two months to a Ṛtu, six Ṛtus are reckoned. On this subject:

> वसंतेनर्तुना देवाः । वसवस्त्रिवृता स्तुतं । रथंतरेण तेजसा । हविरिंद्रे
> पयोः दधुः ॥
> ग्रीष्मेण देवा ऋतुना । रुद्राः पंचदशे स्तुतं । बृहता यशसा बलं ।
> हविरिंद्रे पयो दधुः ॥
> वर्षाभिर्युतुनादित्याः । स्तोमे सप्तदशे स्तुतं । वैरूपेण विशौजसा ।
> हविरिंद्रे पयो दधुः ॥
> शारदेनर्तुना देवाः । एकविग्ंश ऋभवः स्तुतं । वैराजेन श्रिया श्रियं ।
> हविरिंद्रे पयो दधुः ॥
> हेमंतेनर्तुना देवाः । मरुतस्त्रिणवे स्तुतं । बलेन शक्वरीः सहः ।
> हविरिंद्रे पयो दधुः ॥
> शैशिरेणर्तुना देवाः । त्रयस्त्रिग्ंशेऽमृतग्स् स्तुतं । सत्येन रेवतीःक्षत्रं ।
> हविरिंद्रे पयो दधुः ॥

> *vasaṃtenartunā devāḥ | vasavastrivṛtā stutaṃ | rathaṃtareṇa tejasā | haviriṃdre*
> *payoḥ dadhuḥ ‖*
> *grīṣmeṇa devā ṛtunā | rudrāḥ paṃcadaśe stutaṃ | bṛhatā yaśasā balaṃ |*
> *haviriṃdre payo dadhuḥ ‖*
> *varṣābhiryutunādityāḥ | stome saptadaśe stutaṃ | vairūpeṇa viśaujasā |*
> *haviriṃdre payo dadhuḥ ‖*
> *śāradenartunā devāḥ | ekavigṃśa ṛbhavaḥ stutaṃ | vairājena śriyā śriyaṃ |*
> *haviriṃdre payo dadhuḥ ‖*
> *hemaṃtenartunā devāḥ | marutastriṇave stutaṃ | balena śakvarīḥ sahaḥ |*
> *haviriṃdre payo dadhuḥ ‖*
> *śaiśireṇartunā devāḥ | trayastrigṃśe 'mṛtags stutaṃ | satyena revatīḥkṣatraṃ |*
> *haviriṃdre payo dadhuḥ ‖*

(Tai. Br. 2-6-19-1, 2)

In this anuvāka of the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa it is said that the gods praised the spring Ṛtu with the Trivṛt stoma, the summer Ṛtu with the Pañcadaśa stoma, the rainy season with the Saptadaśa stoma, the autumn with the Ekaviṃśa stoma, the Hemanta Ṛtu with the Triṇava stoma, and the Śaiśira Ṛtu with the Trayastriṃśa stoma; and that, having offered the oblation, they obtained desired things such as strength, fame and wealth. Therefore a year has six Ṛtus in all: Vasanta, Grīṣma, Varṣa, Śarad, Hemanta and Śaiśira. On some occasions Hemanta and Śaiśira are joined and reckoned as a single Ṛtu, "Hemanta-śiśira".

> वसंतमृतूनां प्रीणामि स मा प्रीतः प्रीणातु
> ग्रीष्ममृतूनां प्रीणामि स मा प्रीतः प्रीणातु
> वर्षायतूनां प्रीणामि ता मा प्रीताः प्रीणंतु

### Printed p. 306

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 37, p. 306 (as supplied).*

> शरदमृतूनां प्रीणामि सा मा प्रीता प्रीणातु
> हेमंतशिशिरावृतूनां प्रीणामि शौ मा प्रीतौ प्रिणीतां

> *śaradamṛtūnāṃ prīṇāmi sā mā prītā prīṇātu*
> *hemaṃtaśiśirāvṛtūnāṃ prīṇāmi śau mā prītau priṇītāṃ*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-6-2-3)

Here Hemanta and Śiśira are taken as a single Ṛtu, so that five Ṛtus in all are described. Yāska, giving the etymology of the word *ṛtu*, says ऋतुरर्तॆर्गतिकर्मणः (*ṛturartèrgatikarmaṇaḥ*) (Ni. 2-25), "by the Ṛtus, by the times" (Ni. 8-3). That is, the word *ṛtu* is formed from the root *ṛ* in the sense of going (ऋ गतौ (*ṛ gatau*)) and conveys the meaning "time". Which months combine to form which Ṛtus is also stated in the Yajurveda itself.

> मधुश्च माधवश्च वासंतिकावृतू
> शुक्रश्च शुचिश्च ग्रैष्मावृतू
> नभश्च नभस्यश्च वार्षिकावृतू
> इषश्चोर्जश्च शारदावृतू
> सहश्च सहस्यश्च हैमंतिकावृतू
> तपश्च तपस्यश्च शैशिरावृतू

> *madhuśca mādhavaśca vāsaṃtikāvṛtū*
> *śukraśca śuciśca graiṣmāvṛtū*
> *nabhaśca nabhasyaśca vārṣikāvṛtū*
> *iṣaścorjaśca śāradāvṛtū*
> *sahaśca sahasyaśca haimaṃtikāvṛtū*
> *tapaśca tapasyaśca śaiśirāvṛtū*

(Tai. Saṃ. 4-4-11-1)

That is, Caitra and Vaiśākha together are known as the spring Ṛtu; Jyeṣṭha and Āṣāḍha as the summer Ṛtu; Śrāvaṇa and Bhādrapada as the rainy season; Āśvayuja and Kārttika as the autumn; Mārgaśira and Puṣya as the Hemanta Ṛtu; Māgha and Phālguna as the Śiśira Ṛtu. Such is the description of the Ṛtus. Hence here, that is in this sūkta and in the previous one, *ṛtu* means the deity presiding over the Ṛtu. In the ṛks of this sūkta it is prayed that Draviṇodā (Agni) and the other deities come to the sacrificial ground together with these Ṛtu deities and drink Soma.

The Ṛtuyāja oblations

The Ṛtuyāja oblations have twelve mantras. For these twelve oblations the Praiṣa mantras and the Yājyā mantras are one and the same. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā:

> मधुश्च माधवश्च शुक्रश्च शुचिश्च नभश्च नभस्यच्छेषश्चोर्जश्च सहश्च सहस्यश्च
> तपश्च तपस्यश्चोपयामगृहीतोऽसि सग्ंसर्पोऽस्यग्ंहस्पत्याय त्वा ॥

> *madhuśca mādhavaśca śukraśca śuciśca nabhaśca nabhasyaccheṣaścorjaśca sahaśca sahasyaśca*
> *tapaśca tapasyaścopayāmagṛhīto 'si sagṃsarpo 'syagṃhaspatyāya tvā ‖*

(Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-4-14-1) [reference printed "ಕೃ. ಸಂ." as supplied]

In the past the gods performed a sacrifice and went by it to the world of heaven. Afterwards they thought: "Men too will perform sacrifice as we do, follow us, and come after us to the world of heaven. We must prevent their coming." So they barred the way with the year and went to heaven. Even so the sages found it out by means of the Ṛtu-vessels the gods had left behind. A year has twelve months; therefore twelve Ṛtu-vessels are to be taken. If this is done, the nature of the year is known and the world of heaven is gained. The first two Ṛtu-vessels are taken together, and likewise the last two; therefore the Ṛtus go in pairs of two months. The Ṛtu-vessel has a mouth on both sides. Who knows this? He recites the Praiṣa mantra for the Ṛtus six times, because the Ṛtus are six; thereby he pleases the Ṛtus. Then he recites the mantras for the Ṛtus four times; thereby he pleases the four-footed animals. Then by reciting the mantra for the Ṛtus twice, he pleases the two-footed beings (men)

*The supplied text of this window ends here, in the middle of a sentence ("… pleases the two-footed (human) beings"); the passage continues on p. 308 (next window).*

### Printed p. 308

*Note on the source text: the page-head line of each page and the passage below are in the supplied text as quoted blocks; here they are given as prose, and the Sanskrit quotation as a block (Kannada-script text unchanged).*

is as if pleased. Again he says that the Praiṣa mantras for the Ṛtus are to be recited six times; likewise four times and twice. For the four-footed animals live following the Ṛtus; the two-footed beings (men) live depending on the four-footed animals. Then, as said before, he says the mantras for the Ṛtus are to be recited six times, four times and twice. By reciting the mantras in this way the sacrificer makes for himself a bridge by which to go to heaven. One must not go following one another; if one does so, the Ṛtus too become so, and a disorder arises in the order of the Ṛtus. Therefore the Adhvaryu goes by the southern door and the Pratiprasthātṛ by the northern door. Following this order the sun moves for six months in the southern direction and for another six months in the northern direction (this indicates the Dakṣiṇāyana and the Uttarāyaṇa). Some say there is also a thirteenth month; the Adhvaryu pleases that also.

In the explanation given above the Ṛtuyāja oblations are divided into three groups: first six, then four, then two, twelve in all. In the first six mantras the singular ऋतुना (*ṛtunā*) is used. The deities of these six mantras are, in order, Indra, the Maruts, Tvaṣṭā, Agni, Indra-Brahmā (Indra and Brahman), and Mitra-Varuṇa. Then, for the four mantras of the second group, that is the seventh, eighth, ninth and tenth, the deity is Draviṇodāḥ (a form of Agni); in these four mantras the plural ऋतुभिः (*ṛtubhiḥ*) is used. Of the two mantras of the third group, the eleventh has the Aśvins and the twelfth Agni as deities. In both of these the singular ऋतुना (*ṛtunā*) is used. (See Ṛg. Saṃ. Sūkta 1-15.)

The twelve Praiṣa mantras recited for these Ṛtuyāja oblations are directed by the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa. The first Praiṣa mantra the Maitrāvaruṇa addresses to the Hotṛ, saying होतायक्षदिंद्रं होतात्सजूर्दिव आ पृथिव्या ऋतुना सोमं पिबतु होतर्यज (*hotāyakṣadiṃdraṃ hotātsajūrdiva ā pṛthivyā ṛtunā somaṃ pibatu hotaryaja*). The deity of this first mantra is Indra. Its meaning: let the Hotṛ recite the Yājyā mantra for Indra; let that Indra, together with the Ṛtu deity, drink Soma from the Hotṛ's vessel. The Yājyā mantra is like it, but at the beginning of the mantra, instead of होतायक्षत् (*hotāyakṣat*), it begins with ये ३ यजामहे (*ye 3 yajāmahe*). This is the first Ṛtuyāja oblation.

In performing the second oblation the Maitrāvaruṇa addresses the Potṛ and directs the Praiṣa mantra that has the Maruts as deity. Then the Potṛ recites the mantra related to the Maruts (the second Ṛk), the meaning being that the Marut deities should come with the Ṛtu deity and drink Soma.

Likewise for the recitation of the third mantra the Praiṣa mantra is addressed to the Neṣṭṛ. The Neṣṭṛ recites the mantra having Tvaṣṭā as deity. The fourth mantra, with Agni as deity, is recited by the Āgnīdhra; the fifth, with Indra as deity, by the priest called Brahman; the sixth, with Mitra-Varuṇa as deity (the Praśāstārau), by the Maitrāvaruṇa, who performs the oblation. The seventh, eighth, ninth and tenth mantras have Draviṇodāḥ as deity. Of these the seventh Ṛk is recited by the Hotṛ, the eighth by the Potṛ, the ninth by the Neṣṭṛ, and the tenth by the priest called Acchāvāka. In all four of these mantras the plural of the word Ṛtu, ऋतुभिः (*ṛtubhiḥ*), is used. The eleventh and twelfth mantras are recited by the Hotṛ himself. The deities of the eleventh are the Aśvins, and of the twelfth Agni (called Gṛhapati). In these last two Ṛks too the singular ऋतुना (*ṛtunā*) is used. The following table makes this clear.

Here the words Madhu, Mādhava and the like indicate the names of the months Caitra, Vaiśākha and so on. Each month, Madhu and the rest, is indicated together with each deity, Indra and the rest, as the Ṛtu-accompanied deity of the respective mantra. Because the plural ऋतुगळु (*ṛtugaḷu*) is used with the deity Draviṇodāḥ (Ṛtavaḥ), the four months Iṣa, Ūrja, Sahaḥ and Sahasyaḥ may have been indicated as the Ṛtu deities.

### Printed p. 310

For the deity Draviṇodāḥ, after Soma has been offered from the vessels of the priests Hotṛ, Potṛ and Neṣṭṛ as stated in Ṛks 7, 8, 9, it is said that from the tenth mantra the Hotṛ offers Soma from the fourth vessel (turīya). This fourth vessel is called अमर्त्यं (*amartyaṃ*) (immortal, deathless). In the eleventh mantra the Aśvins are prayed to drink Soma from the Adhvaryu's vessel, and in the twelfth Agni from the Gṛhapati (Gārhapatya) vessel, together with the Ṛtu deities (Tapaḥ and Tapasyaḥ).

The twelve mantras that direct the Ṛtuyāja oblation are given in Ṛg. Saṃ. 1-15. That sūkta has 12 Ṛks, and these twelve Ṛks explain the twelve Ṛtuyāja mantras as described above. In the present context, that is in the second Maṇḍala, if the 36th and 37th sūktas, of six Ṛks each, are put together, there are 12 Ṛtuyāja mantras: the mantras 1-6 of the Ṛtuyāja oblation are stated in the 36th sūkta and mantras 7-12 in the 37th. The 36th sūkta belongs to the preceding adhyāya; there no special explanation concerning the Ṛtuyāja was given. In the introduction to the 37th sūkta in this adhyāya all these matters are explained.

Now the matters concerning the Ṛtuyāja oblations explained in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa are explained here:

> प्राणा वा ऋतुयाजास्तद्यदृतुयाजैश्चरंति प्राणानेव तद्यजमाने दधति ।

> *prāṇā vā ṛtuyājāstadyadṛtuyājaiścaraṃti prāṇāneva tadyajamāne dadhati |*

The oblations made to the deities presiding over the Ṛtus, Madhu, Mādhava and the rest, are called Ṛtuyāja. The Ṛtuyājas are of the nature of the vital breaths; here "breath" means prāṇa, apāna and vyāna. By performing these Ṛtuyāja oblations it becomes possible for the vital breaths to stay firmly in the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice. If a man is to live long, the breaths must stay firmly in him; if they leave the body and go out, death occurs. Therefore there is the Vedic sentence of prayer, प्राणापानौ मृत्योर्मा पातं प्राणापानौ मा मा हासिष्टं (*prāṇāpānau mṛtyormā pātaṃ prāṇāpānau mā mā hāsiṣṭaṃ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-1-7-1): "May the prāṇa and apāna that dwell in me protect me from death; may they not leave me." So that the vital breaths may stay firmly in the sacrificer and he may be long-lived, these oblations called Ṛtuyāja are made. These Ṛtuyājas, or Ṛtugrahas, are twelve. Among them the first six have some special features; these will be explained here —

The Brāhmaṇa passage continues (the opening word of the quotation is garbled in the supplied text [?]; the sense is that the six oblations with the singular *ṛtunā* are offered as the breath):

> हळ् [?] ऋतूनेति यजंति प्राणमेव तद्यजमाने दधति ।

> *haḷ [?] ṛtūneti yajaṃti prāṇameva tadyajamāne dadhati |*

In the sacrifice the Adhvaryu tells the Maitrāvaruṇa to recite the Praiṣa mantra. Then the Maitrāvaruṇa addresses the six priests beginning with the Hotṛ (Hotṛ, Potṛ, Neṣṭṛ, Āgnīdhra, Brahman and Maitrāvaruṇa) by the Praiṣa mantra and directs that each of them recite one Yājyā mantra, six mantras in all, and make the oblation. Accordingly these priests recite the six mantras in which the singular of the word Ṛtu is used ("may he drink Soma with the Ṛtu"), invite Indra and the other deities together with the Ṛtu deities to drink the Soma, and make the oblation. These six Ṛtuyāja oblations are of the nature of the breath prāṇa. (Here prāṇa means drawing the outer air into the body, that is, taking the breath in.) By making these six oblations, which are of the nature of prāṇa, the Hotṛ and the other priests cause the prāṇa to stand firm in the sacrificer.

> चत्वार ऋतुभिरिति यजंत्यपानमेव तद्यजमाने दधति ।

> *catvāra ṛtubhiriti yajaṃtyapānameva tadyajamāne dadhati |*

Now the special matter of mantras 7 to 10 is explained. In the same order as before, the Maitrāvaruṇa, commanded by the Adhvaryu, indicates through Praiṣa mantras to the Hotṛ and the other priests that the four mantras from the seventh to the tenth, which have Draviṇodas as deity and in which the plural of the word Ṛtu is used ("with the Ṛtus, Soma"), are to be recited and the oblations made. Accordingly the Hotṛ and the others make four oblations. These four oblations are of the nature of the breath apāna. (Apāna means letting the air in the body out, breathing out.) By making these four oblations, which are of the nature of apāna, the Hotṛ and the others cause the apāna to dwell in the sacrificer.

> द्विर्यतुनेत्युपरिष्पाद्वा नमेव [?] तद्यजमाने दधति ।

> *dviryatunetyupariṣpādvā nameva [?] tadyajamāne dadhati |*

Now mantras 11 and 12 are explained. As before, the Maitrāvaruṇa, commanded by the Adhvaryu, recites the Praiṣa mantra addressed to the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer. Hearing that Praiṣa mantra, the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer recite the two mantras with the Aśvins and Agni (printed "ಅಗ್ನ", as supplied) as deities, which have the singular use "with the Ṛtu, Soma", and make the oblations. These two oblations are of the nature of vyāna (vyāna means the air in the body that pervades the whole body and moves about in it). By making these oblations the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer cause all the priests to make the vyāna breath stand firm in the sacrificer. This procedure, that is, the Adhvaryu's telling the Maitrāvaruṇa to recite the Praiṣa mantra and so on —

Thus, regarding the reciting [?] of the first six mantras with the singular of the word Ṛtu, then of mantras 7 to 10 with the plural, and then of mantras 11 and 12 again with the singular, there is this sentence of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā:

> ऋतुना प्रेष्यति षट्कत्व आह षड्वा ऋतव ऋतूनेव प्रीणाति
> ऋतुभिरिति चतुश्चतुष्पद एव पशून्प्रीणाति द्विः पुनर्यतुनाह द्विपद एव प्रीणाति ॥

> *ṛtunā preṣyati ṣaṭkatva āha ṣaḍvā ṛtava ṛtūneva prīṇāti*
> *ṛtubhiriti catuścatuṣpada eva paśūnprīṇāti dviḥ punaryatunāha dvipada eva prīṇāti ‖*

Gist: with the singular "with the Ṛtu" six times he says it, for there are six Ṛtus, so he pleases the Ṛtus; with "with the Ṛtus" four-footed beasts are pleased; "again twice with the Ṛtu" pleases the two-footed.

> स वा आयं प्राणस्त्रेधा विहितः प्राणोपानो व्यान इति तद्यदृतुन ऋतुभि-
> र्यतुनेति यजंति प्राणानां संतत्यै प्राणानामव्यवच्छेदाय ।

> *sa vā āyaṃ prāṇastredhā vihitaḥ prāṇopāno vyāna iti tadyadṛtuna ṛtubhi-*
> *ryatuneti yajaṃti prāṇānāṃ saṃtatyai prāṇānāmavyavacchedāya |*

This breath, the prāṇa, is of three kinds: prāṇa, apāna and vyāna. Prāṇa means drawing the outer air into the body; apāna means letting out the air that is within the body; vyāna means the air that pervades all parts of the body and moves about in it. These twelve Ṛtuyāja oblations are divided into three groups. In the first group, mantras 1 to 6 (six) are used with the singular "with the Ṛtu" (*ṛtunā*) and offered; thereby the prāṇa stands firm in the body of the sacrificer. In the second group, mantras 7 to 10 (four) are used with the plural "with the Ṛtus" (*ṛtubhiḥ*) and offered; thereby the apāna stands firm. In the third group are mantras 11 and 12 (two mantras); these are again offered with the singular *ṛtunā*; thereby the vyāna stands firm in the body. Thus by dividing the twelve Ṛtuyājas as 6+4+2=12 into three groups and offering them, one helps the three kinds of breath, prāṇa, apāna and vyāna, to stay firm in the body of the sacrificer, and to be without interruption so that they do not depart.

> प्राणा वा ऋतुयाजा नर्तुयाजानामनु वषट्कुर्यादसंस्थिता वा ऋतव
> एकैक एव । यदृतुयाजानामनु वषट्कुर्यादसंस्थितानृतून्संस्थापये-
> त्संस्था वा एषा यदनुवषट्कारो य एनं तत्र ब्रूयादसंस्थितानृतून्स-
> मतिष्ठिपद्दुःषमं भविष्यतीति शश्वत्तथा स्युत्तस्मान्नर्तुयाजानामनुवष-

> *prāṇā vā ṛtuyājā nartuyājānāmanu vaṣaṭkuryādasaṃsthitā vā ṛtava*
> *ekaika eva | yadṛtuyājānāmanu vaṣaṭkuryādasaṃsthitānṛtūnsaṃsthāpaye-*
> *tsaṃsthā vā eṣā yadanuvaṣaṭkāro ya enaṃ tatra brūyādasaṃsthitānṛtūnsa-*
> *matiṣṭhipadduḥṣamaṃ bhaviṣyatīti śaśvattathā syuttasmānnartuyājānāmanuvaṣa-*

(Ai. Brā. 9-29)

### Printed p. 313

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 1, p. 313 (the first abbreviation is printed "ಅ." as supplied).*

The Ṛtuyāja oblations are of the nature of the breath. (This matter is also stated in the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa 13-9 and the Gopatha Brāhmaṇa 8-7.) As we know from everyday experience, the Ṛtus, spring and the rest, have no end: as one ends, another follows, one after the other, in an unbroken succession. After the six Ṛtus, Vasanta, Grīṣma, Varṣā, Śarad, Hemanta and Śiśira, are over, spring and the rest begin again. For them there is no break. Therefore, when the Hotṛ recites the Yājyā mantras in the Ṛtuyāja oblations, he must not pronounce the *vaṣaṭkāra* at the end of the mantra. Since the Ṛtus come by a cyclic change, one after another, there is no end to them; therefore it is said that the *vaṣaṭkāra* must not be recited in the oblation. If it were recited, the cyclic order of the Ṛtus would be broken, and as a result illness, poverty and other sorrows would come to the sacrificer. Therefore, so that sorrow and poverty may not befall the sacrificer, the Yājyā mantras in the Ṛtuyāja oblations must not be offered with the *vaṣaṭkāra*.

*(The supplied text prints, as plain lines between the end of this passage and the Saṃhitā, the usual sūkta heading lines; they are summarised in the next paragraph.)*

**Sūkta 37** — Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 37; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 1. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Seer: Gṛtsamada. Deities: 1–4. Draviṇodas; 5. the Aśvins; 6. Agni. Metre: Triṣṭubh (as printed; Sāyaṇa's introduction above calls the sūkta *jāgata*).

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> मंद॑स्व हो॒त्रादनु॒ जोष॒मंध॒सोऽध्व॑र्यवः॒ स पू॒र्णां॒॑॑
> व॑ष्ट्या॒सिचं॑ ।
> तस्मा॑ ए॒तं भ॑रत तद्व॒शो द॒दिर्हो॒त्रात्सोमं॑ द्रविणोदः॒ पिब॒॑॑
> ऋतुभिः ॥ १ ॥

> *maṃdasva hotrādanu joṣamaṃdhaso 'dhvaryavaḥ sa pūrṇāṃ*
> *vaṣṭyāsicaṃ |*
> *tasmā etaṃ bharata tadvaśo dadirhotrātsomaṃ draviṇodaḥ piba*
> *ṛtubhiḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

### Printed p. 314

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 37, p. 314.*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> मंदस्व । होत्रात् । अनु । जोषं । अंधसः । अध्वर्यवः । सः । पूर्णां । वष्टि ।
> आसिचं ।
> तस्मै । एतं । भरत । तत्त्ववशः । ददिः । होत्रात् । सोमं । द्रविणःदः । पिब ।
> ऋतुभिः ॥ १ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे द्रविणोदो द्रविणसोधनस्य दातरेतन्नामक देव अंधसो देवानाम-
> न्नरूपस्य सोमस्य सोमेन होत्रात् होतृकर्तृकाद्यागादनु जोषं प्रतिमनु
> मंदस्व । हे अध्वर्यवः स द्रविणोदाः पूर्णां संपूर्णमासिचं सिच्यमानामा-
> हुतिं वष्टि । कामयते । अतस्तस्मै द्रविणोदसेऽग्निय एतं सोमं भरत । प्राप-
> यत । तद्वशस्तत्कामो द्रविणोदा ददिर्दाता युष्माकमभीष्टफलस्य दाता भवतीति
> शेषः। किंच हे द्रविणोदो होत्रात् होतुर्यागात् ऋतुभिरिषमासाभिमानिभि-
> र्यतुदेवैः सह सोमं पिब ॥

*(Gist: O Draviṇodas, rejoice in the Soma-food of the Hotṛ's sacrifice; Adhvaryus, offer him the full libation, for he desires it and gives the wished-for fruit; drink Soma with the Ṛtu-deities.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(Draviṇodaḥ — O Draviṇodas.) Hotrāt — from the sacrifice performed by the Hotṛ, obtained thereby; aṃdhasaḥ — with the food that is of the nature of Soma; anu joṣaṃ — being pleased; maṃdasva — be gratified. Adhvaryavaḥ — O Adhvaryus. Saḥ — that same Draviṇodas; pūrṇāṃ — full; āsicaṃ — oblation; vaṣṭi — desires. Tasmai — to that Draviṇodas; etaṃ — this Soma; bharata — bring and offer; tadvaśaḥ — that god who desires it; dadiḥ — is a giver of fruit! Draviṇodaḥ — O Draviṇodas; hotrāt — obtained from the sacrifice performed by the Hotṛ; somaṃ — Soma; ṛtubhiḥ — along with the Ṛtu-deities; piba — drink.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Draviṇodas, being pleased with the food, of the nature of Soma, obtained from the sacrifice performed by the Hotṛ, be gratified. O Adhvaryus, that same Draviṇodas desires a full oblation. Offer this Soma to that Draviṇodas. That god, who desires it, is a giver of fruit. O Draviṇodas, drink the Soma obtained from the sacrifice performed by the Hotṛ together with the Ṛtu-deities.

### Printed p. 315

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 1, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, p. 315 (the first abbreviation is printed "ಅ." as supplied).*

**Printed English translation**

Be gratified, Dravinodas, by the sacrificial food presented as the offering of the Hotri; He desires, priests, a full libation ; present it to him, and influenced (by it, he will be your) benefactor : drink, Dravinodas, along with the Ritus, the Soma, the offering of the Hatri [sic].

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*) — Yāska has written a detailed explanation of this word:

> द्रविणोदाः । द्रविणोदाः कस्माद्धनं द्रविणमुच्यते । यदेनदभिद्रवंति ।
> बलं वा द्रविणं यदेनेनाभिद्रवंति । तस्य दाता द्रविणोदाः ॥

> *draviṇodāḥ | draviṇodāḥ kasmāddhanaṃ draviṇamucyate | yadenadabhidravaṃti |*
> *balaṃ vā draviṇaṃ yadenenābhidravaṃti | tasya dātā draviṇodāḥ ‖*

(Ni. 8-1)

Here the derivation of the word द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*) is "one who gives draviṇa". The word द्रविण (*draviṇa*) has two meanings, wealth and strength. Therefore द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*) means one who gives wealth or strength. This is the meaning of the parts of the word. Besides this, Yāska gives the following explanation (nirvacana) of the Ṛk beginning द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*):

> द्रविणोदा यस्त्वं । द्रविणस इति द्रविणसादिन इति वा द्रविणसानिन इति वा
> द्रविणसस्तस्मात् पिबत्विति वा । यज्ञेषु देवमीळते । याचंति स्तुवंति,
> वर्धयंति पूजयंतीति वा ॥

> *draviṇodā yastvaṃ | draviṇasa iti draviṇasādina iti vā draviṇasānina iti vā*
> *draviṇasastasmāt pibatviti vā | yajñeṣu devamīḷate | yācaṃti stuvaṃti,*
> *vardhayaṃti pūjayaṃtīti vā ‖*

That is: the priests who desire wealth, oblations and the like pray to you, called Draviṇodas, to drink the Soma in the sacrifices; this is the main sense. Although द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*) here is a nominative singular, how does it qualify the accusative singular देवं (*devaṃ*)? The words must be supplied so that the sense becomes: द्रविणोदा यः देवः तं देवं (*draviṇodā yaḥ devaḥ taṃ devaṃ*), "that god who is the giver of wealth". Of द्रविणसः (*draviṇasaḥ*) many meanings can be given: they ask for wealth or oblations for the worship of the deities, they praise, they worship.

> तत्कथा द्रविणोदा इंद्र इति क्रौष्टुकिः ।
> स बलधनयोर्दात्तमस्तस्य च सर्वा बलकृतिः ॥

> *tatkathā draviṇodā iṃdra iti krauṣṭukiḥ |*
> *sa baladhanayordāttamastasya ca sarvā balakṛtiḥ ‖*

The word द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*) has now been explained by the meaning of its parts. But who is this deity Draviṇodas? It is Indra who is called Draviṇodas, because Indra is the one who gives in the highest degree strength and wealth, which the word द्रविण (*draviṇa*) denotes; therefore Indra himself should be called Draviṇodas. This is the opinion of one called Krauṣṭuki.

### Printed p. 316

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 37, p. 316.*

> अथाप्यग्निं द्रविणोदसमाहैष पुनरेतस्माज्जायते ।
> यो अत्मनोरंतरग्निं जजान इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥

> *athāpyagniṃ draviṇodasamāhaiṣa punaretasmājjāyate |*
> *yo atmanoraṃtaragniṃ jajāna ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*

Besides this, he gives another meaning for this word: Indra created heaven and earth, and in the middle of them he also created Agni; therefore the word द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*) may also be said to mean Agni. To support this meaning he has given as an example the Ṛk "अश्मनोरंतरग्निं जजान (*aśmanoraṃtaragniṃ jajāna*)" (the quoted Nirukta text above reads अत्मनोरंतरग्निं जजान (*atmanoraṃtaragniṃ jajāna*); the two readings differ in the supplied text, noted as supplied).

> अथाप्यतुयाजेषु द्रविणोदसाः प्रवादा भवंति । तेषां पुनः पात्रस्येंद्र-
> पानमिति भवति ॥ अथाप्येनं सोमपानेन स्तौति । अथाप्याह द्रविणोदाः
> पिबतु द्रविणोदस इति ॥

> *athāpyatuyājeṣu draviṇodasāḥ pravādā bhavaṃti | teṣāṃ punaḥ pātrasyeṃdra-*
> *pānamiti bhavati ‖ athāpyenaṃ somapānena stauti | athāpyāha draviṇodāḥ*
> *pibatu draviṇodasa iti ‖*

In the sacrifices addressed to the Ṛtus, it is said that Indra drinks Soma from the vessel in the hands of the priests, and Indra is praised with mantras connected with Soma-drinking; hence there is a custom of calling the priests Draviṇodasas. All this is the opinion of Krauṣṭuki.

> अयमेवाग्निर्द्रविणोदा इति शाकपूणिः अग्नेयेष्टेव हि सूक्तेषु द्रवि
> होदसाः प्रवादा भवंति ॥

> *ayamevāgnirdraviṇodā iti śākapūṇiḥ agneyeṣṭeva hi sūkteṣu dravi*
> *hodasāḥ pravādā bhavaṃti ‖*

Agni himself is Draviṇodas, according to Śākapūṇi; for in the hymns related to Agni the priests, when praising Agni, use the word द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*) as an epithet of Agni. (In the block the supplied text breaks the word at the line end as द्रवि (*dravi*) / होदसाः (*hodasāḥ*), as supplied.)

> यथो एतत्स बलधनयोर्दातृतम इति सर्वासु देवतास्वैश्वर्यं विद्यते
> यथो “ एतदोजसोजातमुतमन्य एनं ” इति चाहेत्ययमप्यग्नि-
> रोजसा बलेन मध्यमानो जायते तस्मादेनमाह सहसस्पुत्रं सहसः
> सूनुं सहसो यहुं ॥

> *yatho etatsa baladhanayordātṛtama iti sarvāsu devatāsvaiśvaryaṃ vidyate*
> *yatho “ etadojasojātamutamanya enaṃ ” iti cāhetyayamapyagni-*
> *rojasā balena madhyamāno jāyate tasmādenamāha sahasasputraṃ sahasaḥ*
> *sūnuṃ sahaso yahuṃ ‖*

Lordship exists in all the deities; therefore Agni also gives strength and wealth, and because he gives strength and wealth Agni too may be called Draviṇodas. Moreover the word द्रविण (*draviṇa*) means strength. Because Agni is generated by churning with force (strongly), there is a tradition that Agni was born of strength. Therefore Agni is praised with the words सहसस्पुत्रं (*sahasasputraṃ*) (Sahasaḥ — of strength, putraṃ — the son, Agni), सहसः सूनुं (*sahasaḥ sūnuṃ*), सहसो यहुं (*sahaso yahuṃ*) —

> द्रव्यः सर्पिरासुतिः प्रत्नो होता वरेण्यः ।
> सहसस्पुत्रो अद्भुतः ॥

> *dravyaḥ sarpirāsutiḥ pratno hotā vareṇyaḥ |*
> *sahasasputro adbhutaḥ ‖*

(Ma. Saṃ. 2-7-6)

### Printed p. 317

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 1, p. 317.*

> त्वं ह यद्यविष्ठ्य सहसःसूनवाहुत ।
> यता वा यज्ञियो भुवः ॥

> *tvaṃ ha yadyaviṣṭhya sahasaḥsūnavāhuta |*
> *yatā vā yajñiyo bhuvaḥ ‖*

(Ma. Saṃ. 8-75-3)

> अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो ।
> अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥

> *agne vājasya gomata īśānaḥ sahaso yaho |*
> *asme dhehi jātavedo mahi śravaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-79-4)

In these Ṛks the words सहसस्पुत्र (*sahasasputra*), सहसः सूनु (*sahasaḥ sūnu*) and सहसो यहु (*sahaso yahu*) respectively are used when praising Agni. Therefore, although other deities too are givers of strength, it is Agni in particular who is denoted by the word द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*).

Here let us take up the statements of the Bṛhaddevatā and see to which deity this epithet chiefly belongs, and what qualities of that deity are learned from it. The Bṛhaddevatā first explains the derivation of the word अग्नि (*agni*) and then considers why the epithet द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*) is applied to Agni.

> जातो यदग्रे भूतानां अग्रणीरध्वरे च यत् ।
> नाम्ना संनयते वांगं स्तुतोग्निरिति सूरिभिः ॥

> *jāto yadagre bhūtānāṃ agraṇīradhvare ca yat |*
> *nāmnā saṃnayate vāṃgaṃ stutogniriti sūribhiḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-24)

Because he is born first of all beings, because he is the leader (the one who conducts) in sacrifices and rites, and because whatever thing he enters he makes it merge into himself, he is praised by the sages as Agni. This derivation agrees with the derivations stated in the Nirukta: अग्रणीर्भवति अग्रं यज्ञेषु प्रणीयते, अंगं नयति सन्नममानः (*agraṇīrbhavati agraṃ yajñeṣu praṇīyate, aṃgaṃ nayati sannamamānaḥ*) (Ni. 7-14). After explaining the word Agni, it states the derivation of the word द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*):

> द्रविणं धनं बलं वापि प्रायच्छद्येन कर्मणा ।
> तत्कर्म दृष्ट्वा कुत्सस्तु प्राहैनं द्रविणोदसं ॥

> *draviṇaṃ dhanaṃ balaṃ vāpi prāyacchadyena karmaṇā |*
> *tatkarma dṛṣṭvā kutsastu prāhainaṃ draviṇodasaṃ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-25)

The sage Kutsa, having observed the deeds of Agni, who gives wealth and strength generously, praised Agni as द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*), the giver of wealth or of strength.

> द्रविणोदा द्रविणसस्तुरस्य द्रविणोदाः सनरस्य प्र यंसत् ।
> द्रविणोदा वीरवतीमिषं नो द्रविणोदा रासशे दीर्घमायुः ॥

> *draviṇodā draviṇasasturasya draviṇodāḥ sanarasya pra yaṃsat |*
> *draviṇodā vīravatīmiṣaṃ no draviṇodā rāsaśe dīrghamāyuḥ ‖*

(Ma. Saṃ. 1-96-8)

### Printed p. 318

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 37, p. 318.*

Having thus pointed to Kutsa's praise of Agni in this Ṛk, the Bṛhaddevatā again maintains that this indication belongs to the deity Agni and is not meant for other deities:

> अयं हि द्रविणोदोऽग्निरयं दाता बलस्य हि ।
> जायते च बलेनायं मध्यकृत्यृषिभिरध्वरे ॥
> द्रविणोदोऽग्निरेवायं द्रविणोदास्तदोच्यते ।
> आग्नेयेष्टेव दृश्यंते प्रवादा द्रविणोदसः ॥

> *ayaṃ hi draviṇodo 'gnirayaṃ dātā balasya hi |*
> *jāyate ca balenāyaṃ madhyakṛtyṛṣibhiradhvare ‖*
> *draviṇodo 'gnirevāyaṃ draviṇodāstadocyate |*
> *āgneyeṣṭeva dṛśyaṃte pravādā draviṇodasaḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-61; 3-65)

Because Agni is the giver of wealth, the giver of strength, and born of strength, the praise द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*) is fitting for him. Hence the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā maintain that this epithet belongs to the deity Agni.

अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*): of the Soma, which is the food of the gods. The word अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). Soma is said to be the food of the gods; therefore the word अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*) means the Soma juice in the form of food. Besides, the word अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*) in the Ṛgveda generally denotes the Soma juice.

होत्रात् अनु जोषं मंदस्व (*hotrāt anu joṣaṃ maṃdasva*): here the word होत्रात् (*hotrāt*) means "from the sacrifice performed by the Hotṛ", that is, offered in the sacrifice performed by the priest called Hotṛ. The sense is that the deity (Draviṇodas) drinks the Soma juice which the Hotṛ offers into the fire as an oblation addressed to him, and is satisfied.

अध्वर्यवः (*adhvaryavaḥ*): O Adhvaryus, the priests called Adhvaryu. In a sacrifice the parts of the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu are the chief ones. The Hotṛ recites the mantras suited to each moment in order to invoke the gods; the Adhvaryu performs the oblations and other rites in accordance with those mantras. Hence the Śruti statement अध्वर्युर्वा ऋत्विजां प्रथमो युज्यते (*adhvaryurvā ṛtvijāṃ prathamo yujyate*): among the priests the Adhvaryu is the chief.

The word अध्वर (*adhvara*) means a sacrifice that produces an imperishable fruit. In the Nirukta: अध्वर इति यॆज्ञनाम ध्वरतिर्हिंसा कर्म तत्प्रतिषेधः (*adhvara iti yèjñanāma dhvaratirhiṃsā karma tatpratiṣedhaḥ*) (Ni. 1-8): the word अध्वर (*adhvara*) conveys the meaning "sacrifice"; the roots ध्वरति (*dhvarati*) and धूर्वति (*dhūrvati*) convey the meaning of doing harm; therefore Yāska has given the word अध्वर (*adhvara*), formed from those roots, the meaning "a rite without harm". Further, the word अध्वर (*adhvara*) is stated both among the sixteen names of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10) and among the fifteen names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-19). Therefore, for the word अध्वर्यु (*adhvaryu*) —

### Printed p. 319

*Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 1, p. 319.*

> अध्वर्युरध्वरयुरध्वरं युनक्त्यध्वरस्य नेताध्वरं - कामयत इति वा ।
> अपि वाधीयाने युरुपबंधः अध्वर इति यज्ञनाम । ध्वरतिर्हिंसाकर्म
> तत्प्रतिषेधः ॥

> *adhvaryuradhvarayuradhvaraṃ yunaktyadhvarasya netādhvaraṃ - kāmayata iti vā |*
> *api vādhīyāne yurupabaṃdhaḥ adhvara iti yajñanāma | dhvaratirhiṃsākarma*
> *tatpratiṣedhaḥ ‖*

(Ni. 1-8)

the derivation is thus given. That is, in the word अध्वरयु (*adhvarayu*) the vowel a in the letter ra is dropped and it becomes अध्वर्यु (*adhvaryu*). The one who joins (brings together) the sacrificial work: that is, he has the rites that should take place at each time performed by the respective priests and so carries the sacrifice through. Or he looks after the sacrifice so that it is completed with all its parts. Or the meaning is given as "one who desires the sacrifice".

अध्वर्यवः सः पूर्णां असिचं वष्टि (*adhvaryavaḥ saḥ pūrṇāṃ asicaṃ vaṣṭi*): O Adhvaryus, that god called Draviṇodas desires the oblation of full Soma juice. Therefore offer the Soma oblation into the fire for Draviṇodas: thus the sacrificer addresses the priests called Adhvaryus.

तस्मै एतं भरत तद्वशः ददिः (*tasmai etaṃ bharata tadvaśaḥ dadiḥ*): O Adhvaryus, bear (that is, offer) this oblation of Soma juice to that Draviṇodas. Pleased with that Soma, Draviṇodas will give you your desired ends.

द्रविणोदः होत्रात् ऋतुभिः सोमं पिब (*draviṇodaḥ hotrāt ṛtubhiḥ somaṃ piba*): in this sentence the sacrificer addresses Draviṇodas himself and prays: O Draviṇodas, in this sacrifice (or oblation) performed by the priest called Hotṛ, drink the Soma juice together with the Ṛtu deities who preside over the months of Iṣa (Āśvayuja). In the same way, in the next Ṛk the prayer is made in the sacrifice of the priest called Potṛ, in the Ṛk after that in the sacrifice of the priest called Neṣṭṛ, and in the Ṛk after that it is prayed that the Soma in the fourth vessel be drunk together with the Ṛtu deities.

O Draviṇodas, you whom I formerly invoked with prayer in the Soma sacrifice performed by the Hotṛ, that same you I now call in the sacrifice performed by the Potṛ as well. **विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

यं उ पूर्वं अहुवे इदं तं हुवे (*yaṃ u pūrvaṃ ahuve idaṃ taṃ huve*) — हे द्रविणोदः यं त्वां होतृकर्तृके सोमयागे आहूतवानस्मि संप्रति तमेव पोतृकर्तृके सोमयागे आह्वयामि । (*he draviṇodaḥ yaṃ tvāṃ hotṛkartṛke somayāge āhūtavānasmi saṃprati tameva potṛkartṛke somayāge āhvayāmi |*) The sacrificer addresses the deity Draviṇodas again: O Draviṇodas, earlier (in the previous Ṛk) I invited you to drink Soma together with the Ṛtus in the Hotṛ's sacrifice. Now in the Soma sacrifice performed by the priest called Potṛ also, I invite you to come to the sacrificial ground with the deities presiding over the month called Ūrja (Kārttika) and drink the Soma juice.

सः इत् हव्यः उ (*saḥ it havyaḥ u*) — That Draviṇodas is worthy to be invited for drinking Soma. This fact is well known.

यो नाम ददिः पत्यते सोम्यं मधु अध्वर्युभिः प्रस्थितं (*yo nāma dadiḥ patyate somyaṃ madhu adhvaryubhiḥ prasthitaṃ*) — For that Draviṇodas who is renowned as the giver of desired ends to sacrificers and others, the tasty Soma juice has been brought, prepared and placed by the priests called Adhvaryus.

द्रविणोदः पोत्रात् ऋतुभिः सोमं पिब (*draviṇodaḥ potrāt ṛtubhiḥ somaṃ piba*) — हे द्रविणोदः पोतुर्यागात् ऊर्जसंज्ञकैः ऋतुभिः सह सोमं पिब । (*he draviṇodaḥ poturyāgāt ūrjasaṃjñakaiḥ ṛtubhiḥ saha somaṃ piba |*) O Draviṇodas, drink this Soma juice, which the Adhvaryus have prepared for you and placed on the sacrificial altar, together with the deities presiding over the month Ūrja (Kārttika): such is the sacrificer's prayer stated here.

The particles इत् (*it*) and उ (*u*) are used to fill out the pāda. Yāska has said अथापि पदपूरण इदमु तदु (*athāpi padapūraṇa idamu tadu*) (Ni. 1-5) [reference as printed], and Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, also says उकारः पडपूरणः (*ukāraḥ paḍapūraṇaḥ*) [sic, as supplied].

**Printed English translation**

May these your bearers, by whom you are borne along, be satisfied ; lord of the forest, be firm, doing no injury, steadfast of resolve ; come, and being gracious, drink, Dravinodas, along with the Ritus, the Soma, the offering the Neshtri [sic].

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

द्रविणोदः येभिः ईयसे ते वह्नयः मेद्यंतु (*draviṇodaḥ yebhiḥ īyase te vahnayaḥ medyaṃtu*) — the supplied text then adds a Sanskrit explanation (the words of Sāyaṇa's gloss, not repeated here). Kannada explanation: O Draviṇodas, the officiating priests who bring you, born in the fire-sticks (araṇis), to the sacrificial altar: may they be satisfied; thus the prayer is made.

Yāska has given an etymology for this passage (Ni. 8-3): वेद्यंतु ते वह्नयो वोढारो (*vedyaṃtu te vahnayo voḍhāro*) [as supplied; the quotation continues over several lines through वनस्पत इत्येन (*vanaspata ityena*) ... पिबर्तुभिः (*pibartubhiḥ*) and is not retyped here; its words as supplied are in the Kannada file].

According to this etymology the word *medyantu* is derived from the root इम्मिदा (*immidā*) [as supplied], "to be affectionate"; मेद्यंतु (*medyaṃtu*) is the third person plural imperative: "let them rejoice, let them be satisfied". *Vahnayaḥ* means "bearers" (the supplied text has प्रोढारः (*proḍhāraḥ*)): the word *vahni* is formed from the root *vah*, meaning "to carry, to bear, to reach", so *vahnayaḥ* means those who carry. The word can also mean a horse that bears a burden; here it is used in the sense of the priests who carry Agni (Draviṇodas). *Ariṣaṇyat* means "not harming, not being harmed", an epithet of Agni. *Dhṛṣṇu* is generally "one who destroys enemies".

*Dhiṣṇya*, *dhiṣaṇya*: *dhiṣaṇā* means speech (*vāk*). Because the Hotṛ sits near the deity and praises him in verses of praise, *dhiṣṇya* means "one who is praised". Or, according to धीसादिनीति वा धीसानिनीति वा (*dhīsādinīti vā dhīsāninīti vā*): *dhīḥ* means understanding or ritual work (sacrificial work), and since he is reached by understanding or ritual work he is *dhiṣṇya*; or since understanding or ritual work resides in him, or he gives them to those who worship him, the word *dhiṣṇya* may be so derived. *Dhiṣṇya* may also mean sacrificial work or the sacrificial ground. Here the prayer is that Soma be drunk in the sacrifice performed by the priest called Neṣṭṛ.

### Printed p. 324

*Vanaspate* is a vocative addressed to Agni. How is Agni called by the name *vanaspati*? Yāska says (as supplied): एष हि वनानां पाता ना पालयिता वा (*eṣa hi vanānāṃ pātā nā pālayitā vā*) [sic, as supplied; *nā* for *vā*?] — the passage goes on to say that, although Agni is within the forest trees and able to burn them, he does not burn them, and so is their protector. The word *vana* is derived from a root meaning "to be, to dwell". Here *vanaspati* means the lord or protector of trees: Agni, though dwelling within trees, does not burn them but guards them, and is therefore called *vanaspati*, protector of trees.

ऋतुभिः—कालैः (*ṛtubhiḥ—kālaiḥ*): *ṛtus* are definite periods of time. If a year is divided into six equal parts, each part, containing two months, indicates a fixed period of time; such a period is described by the word *ṛtu*.

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अपात् । होत्रात् । उत । पोत्रात् । अमत्त । उत । नेष्ट्रात् । अजुषत । प्रयः ।
> हितं ।
> तुरीयं । पात्रं । अमृक्तं । अमर्त्यं । द्रविणःदाः । पिबतु । द्राविणःदसः ॥ ४ ॥

> *apāt | hotrāt | uta | potrāt | amatta | uta | neṣṭrāt | ajuṣata | prayaḥ |*
> *hitaṃ |*
> *turīyaṃ | pātraṃ | amṛktaṃ | amartyaṃ | draviṇaḥdāḥ | pibatu | drāviṇaḥdasaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

### Printed p. 325

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अच्छावाकस्येयं । यो द्रविणोदा होत्राद्दोतुर्यागात् सोममपात्
> पीतवान् उत किंच पोत्रात्पोतुर्यागादमत्त सोमं पीत्वामाद्यत् । उत आपि
> च नेष्ट्रात् नेष्टुर्यागाद्धितं दत्तं प्रयो देवानामन्न रूपं सोममजुषत ।
> आसेविष्ट । स द्राविणोदसो हवीरूपद्रविणस्य प्रदातृभ्य ऋत्विग्यो हितः ॥ ऋत्वि-
> जोऽत्र द्रविणोदस उच्यंते हविषो दातारस्ते चैनं जनयंति । नि. ८-२ । इति
> यास्केनोक्तत्वात् ॥ तादृशो द्रविणोदा अमृतं दशापवित्रॆणामृष्टममर्त्यम-
> मरणसाधनं तुरीयं पात्रं चतुर्थपात्रस्थं सोमं पिबतु ॥

*Gist:* This verse belongs to the Acchāvāka. Draviṇodas, who drank Soma at the Hotṛ's, Potṛ's and Neṣṭṛ's sacrifices, is asked to drink the unstrained, immortal Soma in the fourth cup.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

Yaḥ — which Draviṇodas. Hotrāt — in the sacrifice performed by the Hotṛ. Apāt — drank the Soma. Uta — and. Potrāt — in the sacrifice performed by the Potṛ. Amatta — was satisfied with drinking Soma. Uta — and. Neṣṭrāt — in the sacrifice performed by the Neṣṭṛ. Hitaṃ — offered. Prayaḥ — food-like for the gods, the Soma. Ajuṣata — enjoyed. (Saḥ — that Draviṇodas.) Draviṇodasaḥ — is for the priests who offer wealth in the form of oblations. Draviṇodāḥ — the same god. Amṛktaṃ — unhurt. Amartyaṃ — free of death. Turīyaṃ pātraṃ — contained in the fourth cup, the Soma. Pibatu — let him drink. (Spellings ಆಪಾತ್, ಆಮತ್ತ, ತುರಿಯಂ, ನೇಷ್ಟೃಕರ್ತಕವಾದ, ಅನ್ನ ಪ್ರಾಯದುದೂ kept as supplied.)

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The Draviṇodas who drank Soma in the sacrifice performed by the Hotṛ, was satisfied by drinking Soma in the sacrifice performed by the Potṛ, and enjoyed the Soma offered in the sacrifice performed by the Neṣṭṛ, which is like food for the gods, is there for the priests who offer wealth in the form of oblations. Let that same god drink the Soma that is unhurt, free of death and contained in the fourth cup.

**Printed English translation**

Whether he has drink [sic] the Soma from the offering of the Hotri ; whether he has been exhilarated by the offering of the Potri ; whether he has been pleased with the (sacrificial) food presented as the act of the Neshtri ; still let Dravinodas quaff the unstrained amborsial [sic] cup the forrth [sic] offered by the priest.

### Printed p. 326

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this Ṛk the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa speaks, addressing the priest called Acchāvāka. In the three preceding Ṛks Draviṇodas has been asked to drink the Soma offered in the sacrifices performed by the priests Hotṛ, Potṛ and Neṣṭṛ. The first half of this Ṛk states the same matter again. Now he is asked to drink the Soma that is in the fourth cup, offered by the priests.

तुरीयं पात्रं (*turīyaṃ pātraṃ*) — the Soma juice in the fourth cup. What has been said up to now is, in order, the Soma juice in the three cups of the priests Hotṛ, Potṛ and Neṣṭṛ; it is explained that the Soma juice offered by these priests is in the fourth cup.

अमृक्तं (*amṛktaṃ*) —
> अमृष्टं, अशुद्धं, अपूर्णमित्यर्थः ।

> *amṛṣṭaṃ, aśuddhaṃ, apūrṇamityarthaḥ |*
O Draviṇodas, the Soma offered up to now by the priests Hotṛ, Potṛ and Neṣṭṛ is incomplete; that is, you have not been fully satisfied by drinking the Soma they offered. Therefore the intended sense is: drink the Soma juice in the fourth cup now offered by the priests and be satisfied.

अमर्त्यं (*amartyaṃ*) —
> अमरणसाधनं । यत् पीत्वा न म्रियते । अमनुष्ययोग्यं ।

> *amaraṇasādhanaṃ | yat pītvā na mriyate | amanuṣyayogyaṃ |*
"Preventing death", that is, one who drinks this Soma does not die. Therefore this divine Soma is not fit for human beings; it is fit for the gods and is like nectar (*amṛta*).

द्रविणोदसः (*draviṇodasaḥ*) —
> हवीरूपद्रविणस्य प्रदातारः ।

> *havīrūpadraviṇasya pradātāraḥ |*
The commentator explains it as the priests who offer oblations. Yāska also says:
> एतदग्निं द्रविणोदसमाहेत्यृत्विजोSत्र द्रविणोदस उच्यंते हविषो
> दातारस्ते चैनं जनयंति ॥

> *etadagniṃ draviṇodasamāhetyṛtvijoStra draviṇodasa ucyaṃte haviṣo*
> *dātāraste cainaṃ janayaṃti ‖*
(Si. 8-2) [as supplied; the bhāṣya quotes this passage as Ni. 8-2]
Thus he gives the etymology: Agni too is named Draviṇodas; because the priests offer oblations to that Agni, the priests also are called Draviṇodas.

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अ॒र्वांच॑म॒द्य य॒य्यं॑ नृ॒वाह॑णं॒ रथं॑ युंजाथामि॒ह वां॒॑॑
> विमोचनं ।

> वसू ॥ ५ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अर्वांचं । अद्य । यय्यं । नृवाहनं । रथं । युंजाथां । इह । वां ।
> विमोचनं ।
> पृंक्तं । हवींषि । मधुना । आ । हि । कं । गतं । अथ । सोमं । पिबतं । वाजिनी-
